- **Selection: `2505.23556` (*Understanding Refusal in Language Models with Sparse Autoencoders*), run 368's preferred continuation for the refusal line.** Collision-checked before any fetch across `aether/`, `core/` and both INDEX files: `2505.23556`, `2410.13787`, `2503.15299`, `2506.18167`, `2410.13032` and `2406.09289` are **all absent** (six measured, zero collisions), so the pool run 368 verified is intact. Taken because run 368 established that refusal lives in a *cone* of at least five dimensions trained on the ablation objective, and this paper supplies the other decomposition of the same behaviour — SAE latents on the residual stream — plus the one comparison the folder lacks: two decompositions of refusal, one vector versus twenty latents, scored on the same three benchmarks with the same collateral column. It earns a **3** for three reasons. (1) **It resolves the single-direction question by neither defending nor refuting the direction but demoting it**: the difference-of-means direction is used only as a candidate filter (top 10 latents per layer by cosine), and the causal selection happens *inside* the filtered pool by attribution patching — so the paper's answer to "is refusal one direction?" is "the direction is the right coordinate system and the wrong object", which is the usable form of `arxiv-2502.17420`'s cone result obtained from a completely different construction. (2) **The upstream/downstream split is measured with a control that is not the baseline the folder usually uses**: clamping the harm features suppresses downstream refusal activation 0.48 / 0.51 against 0.05 / 0.19 for a random feature set a hundred times larger, and the paper then presses the claim further than its own design strictly licenses — the intersection of seven behaviour-specific sets (7 features in Gemma, 10 in Llama) jailbreaks better than category-specific features *inside their own category*, including on Llama where the specific set alone does almost nothing. (3) **The dense-probe collapse is the sharpest shortcut result the folder holds on the probe side**: on adversarial WildJailBreak prompts the model actually complies with, a probe trained on the refusal latents keeps a vanilla-to-adversarial gap of 0.03 / 0.17 while the dense residual-stream probe gives 0.32 / 0.93, and the dense Llama probe scores *higher* on adversarial prompts (0.97) than on vanilla ones (0.03) — the shortcut stated as a number instead of a caveat. Held back from a 4+ by: **attribution is run on the evaluation set, not a separate training set** (the authors say so plainly and justify it as "which method identifies a causal set", but it means the faithfulness numbers are optimistic and the baselines were not given a matched second split); **no seeds, no intervals, and 100 prompts per benchmark per cell**; **the pool is bounded by the direction**, so a feature that matters but is not direction-aligned is invisible by construction; every number comes from two models with quite different SAE families (JumpReLU vs TopK), and the authors themselves attribute several cross-model differences to that rather than to the models.

- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 369): **The correct role for the differencing direction is a candidate filter, not an explanation, and the two-stage version of that sentence is a procedure anyone can run: take the top-k latents by cosine to the direction at every layer, then rank *inside that pool* by an interventional importance score, and the resulting twenty latents jailbreak about as well as steering the full direction while preserving more coherence — Alpaca CE 0.310 against 0.337 on Gemma, 0.224 against 0.150 on Llama, and 2.1 rather than 2.4 GSM8K points lost.** The failure of the naive alternatives is what makes the ordering a finding rather than a default: cosine alone works on Llama and fails on Gemma because it collapses onto one layer's features, and unrestricted attribution patching fails on both because its single-token metric is aimed at the wrong target for a multi-token behaviour. For us this is the practical middle path between the folder's two current poles — the one-vector ablation (`arxiv-2507.11878`, `arxiv-2502.17420`) and the full dictionary (`arxiv-2502.17420`'s cones being the geometric face of the same tension) — and it says something specific about how to build a white-box account: the direction supplies the coordinate system, intervention supplies the object. Coreference `arxiv-2502.17420` (refusal as a five-dimensional cone) and `arxiv-2507.11878` (harmfulness and refusal as separate directions, which this entry re-encodes as separate latent sets).
- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 369): **A probe trained on a label can become an anti-detector exactly where detection matters, and the number that shows it is the vanilla-versus-adversarial gap: on prompts the model is tricked into complying with, a dense residual-stream probe scores 0.97 on adversarial and 0.03 on vanilla (Llama) while a probe on refusal latents scores 0.83 and 0.66 — the dense probe has learned the surface form of the label and inverts on the shifted set.** Two consequences. (1) **Every probe accuracy we report in this folder is missing its adversarial column** — the folder's probe entries report AUROC on in-distribution and, at best, one OOD set (`arxiv-2610.30363`'s two-set design is the closest), and none reports the inversion diagnostic, which is the case where the probe is worse than useless because it points the wrong way. (2) **The relative improvement is the claim, not the absolute score** — the sparse probe's average accuracy is higher (0.86 vs 0.68, 0.75 vs 0.51) but that is a small-sample difference on one split; the gap ratio is the result, and it is stable in direction across both models and both SAE families. Coreference `arxiv-2610.30363` (pooling-by-label-location as the mechanism behind the same *class* of failure) and `arxiv-2511.04527` (a prompt-only baseline that reaches near-probe AUC, the other way to price a decodability claim).
- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 369): **Behaviour-specific and behaviour-shared are not a partition but a hierarchy, and the shared part is the one that actually gates behaviour: clamping the 7–10 latents common to all seven CATQA harmful categories jailbreaks more effectively than clamping the category-specific latents *inside their own category*, and on Llama the specific set alone is largely ineffective because it encodes the harm concept (violence, drugs, legal consequences) rather than the refusal response.** The paper's own appendix walks this back further, noting that its "specific" remainder is still shared across categories and sketching a deeper chain (harm → legality → consequences → refusal), i.e. the two-level split is a first cut. For us the operational lesson is about how to build a concept hierarchy from interventions rather than from labels: compute the feature set for each behaviour, take intersections to find the shared core, then *intervene on the core and the remainder separately with the other frozen* — that frozen-complement design is what makes the comparison causal rather than a difference of two full sets, and it is one line of change to any multi-behaviour probe study. Coreference `arxiv-2502.17420` (independence tested by ablation) and `arxiv-2606.25092` (a structural partition that dissolves under a size-matched null).

- **Selection: `2502.17420` (*The Geometry of Refusal in Large Language Models: Concept Cones and Representational Independence*), the geometry member run 367 named as one of two preferred continuations.** Collision-checked against the whole carried pool before any fetch — `2502.17420`, `2410.13787`, `2505.23556`, `2406.09289`, `2506.18167`, `2410.13032` and `2503.15299` are all **absent from `aether/` file names, `core/` and both INDEX files**, so the pool run 367 measured is intact and six ids remain unread. Taken because the folder's direction entries are all built on a single vector obtained by differencing means, and no entry we hold asks whether that is a fact about the network or about the extraction — this paper answers both halves, first by *training* a direction on the intervention objective instead of measuring one, then by showing that the region is a cone and that orthogonal pairs inside it are not independent. It earns a **3** for three reasons. (1) **Representational independence is the operational version of a question every direction entry in the folder raises and none answers**: are two directions one mechanism or two? The criterion is not orthogonality — the paper constructs an exactly-orthogonal pair and shows in its own Figure 6 that ablating one still reduces how much of the other the later layers carry — but "does ablating X leave cos(x, Y) unchanged at every layer", which is one ablation pass per direction and costs nothing beyond the forward hooks we already have. (2) **The additivity test is the causal half and it is a dose-response design**: ablating the top-k independent directions lifts ASR monotonically and passes the baseline from k = 4, while ablating several difference-of-means directions from different layers does not improve on one — a contrast between k and k that converts "two probes" into "two mechanisms" without a circuit story. (3) **The side-effect column is the entire result and the folder has been mispricing its absence**: on TruthfulQA the baseline direction costs 3.0–8.0 points and the optimised one 1.1–5.0 across all seven models with both, so "the direction ablates refusal" was never the claim worth making — the claim is that it does so without spending 40% of the collateral damage. Held back from a 4+ by: no seeds or intervals anywhere in the ASR comparisons; cone statements are sampled lower bounds over 256 vectors rather than dimension estimates; every direction is optimised against the same generated targets, which the authors admit may make the mechanisms less distinct than the independence test suggests; and **the well-measured direction of the effect is the adversarial one** — the metric that drives the headline is how completely refusal can be switched off.

- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 368): **Orthogonality is not independence, and the counterexample is built inside the paper's own method: a direction trained to be exactly orthogonal to the refusal direction, with the inner product held at zero by construction, still has its representation on harmful prompts systematically reduced when the other is ablated — and the effect is reciprocal — so the angle between two direction vectors, which is the folder's standard evidence that two probes are separate, is a statement about the linear algebra and not about what the network does with either.** The replacement criterion is a fixed point rather than an angle: ablate X everywhere, recompute cos(x, Y) layer by layer, and require it unchanged; if it moves, the non-linear path has coupled them. For us this reprices two entries that lean on angles — `arxiv-2605.14038`'s cognition/action probes collapsing to cosines of −0.018 and 0.026 at the final token, and `arxiv-2507.11878`'s harmfulness and refusal directions reported as near-orthogonal at two token positions — not as wrong, but as *unfinished*: the cheap linear screen says the directions do not overlap, and this entry shows that the cheap screen is falsified by its own construction. The experiment to run is theirs, and it costs one extra forward pass per direction per prompt: take each probe direction, ablate it, and print the cosine of the other at every layer beside the ablation-free baseline. Where the curves coincide the directions are independent in the sense that matters; where they separate, the folder has a coupling it currently reports as zero.
- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 368): **A direction should be trained against the intervention we care about rather than measured off a contrast and then tested, and the difference shows up in the column nobody usually prints: optimising a refusal direction on an ablation objective plus a KL retain term and an addition objective costs 1.1–5.0 TruthfulQA points of collateral damage where the difference-of-means direction extracted from identical layer and data costs 3.0–8.0, on every one of seven models, i.e. roughly 40% of the side effect removed at matched attack strength.** Two design consequences. (1) **Probe directions fitted for classification accuracy are optimised for the wrong objective** — read-ability is a proxy, and this entry's own ablation is what a write-side claim needs: a loss on the behaviour under intervention, a loss on the behaviour on the far side of the intervention, and a retain term that bounds the collateral. (2) **The retain weight is a Pareto dial and the curve is the reportable object**, because the interesting claim is not that a direction works at some weight but that a whole range of weights dominates the baseline on both axes at once — and the failure beyond the knee (ASR collapsing past a retain weight of 4) is the useful warning that the constraint can be over-tightened. Coreference `arxiv-2605.14038` (a probe never intervened on and therefore correlational by construction) and `arxiv-2606.25092` (an ablation whose modularity claim needs an off-target column to survive).
- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 368): **Additivity is the cheapest causal evidence that two directions act on different mechanisms, and it has a control that makes it falsifiable: ablating the top-k independent directions lifts attack success monotonically in k and overtakes the single baseline direction from four on, whereas ablating several difference-of-means directions extracted at *different layers* does not improve on one at all — the same k-curve, run once with directions selected to be independent and once with directions selected to differ, and only the first rises.** For our own multi-probe accounts this is the missing test: whenever we say two probes capture different causes, ablate (or patch) both and print the effect as a function of how many are included, with a same-family, different-layer set as the control. A flat curve means the second direction is a reparameterisation of the first and the folder's "two mechanisms" language should be withdrawn; a rising curve with a plateau is a count of mechanisms, which is the kind of prediction a white-box model of the network can actually be scored against. Coreference `arxiv-2606.25092`'s dose-response curve for expert masking (monotone and flat = busy, not necessary) and `arxiv-2605.14038`'s orthogonality claim that never ablates the cognition probe.

- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 367): **A probe's decodability can be priced against a ceiling built from the same activations, and the ceiling changes the conclusion: give a logistic regression full access to the residual stream the probe works on, ask it the identical question, and compare — a model that reports its own activations from an in-context dialogue lands far below that bound on every axis, so "the model has this information" and "the model can act on it" separate without any intervention at all.** The cost is one extra regression fit per axis, which makes it the cheapest item on the folder's missing-instrument list, and it should attach to every direction we publish in two forms: the ceiling itself (what a full-access decoder achieves) and the in-context score (what the model achieves when the target is mediated through tokens). Where the two agree, the direction is one the model's output machinery can reach; where they diverge, the folder now has a name for the gap that does not require a steering sweep. Coreference `arxiv-2610.21708` (a decodable belief that is inert under a both-directions patch) and `arxiv-2605.14038` (cognition and action probes nearly orthogonal at the read-out) — three entries, three instruments, one distinction.
- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 367): **A control effect is partly an artefact of the model's own output feeding back as input, and separating the two is a design choice rather than a discussion point: instructing the model to imitate a label and letting it write the sentence produces a large shift, instructing it identically on a sentence it did not write produces a much smaller one — same axis, same layer, same instruction, only the provenance of the tokens differs — and at early layers the implicit effect is near zero.** For our intervention writing this is the mirror of the folder's prompt-versus-state warning: whenever an effect we report could be carried by generated tokens, run the foreign-input version and print both numbers, because the explicit effect is what an output filter can see and the implicit one is what a latent monitor must catch on its own. It is also the reason this paper's own safety reading is sharper than a generic jailbreak claim — the covert version needs no cooperation from the token stream at all. Coreference `arxiv-2607.22925` (a latent computation established early and worthless at a single position) and `arxiv-2602.17424`-adjacent work in the folder on a disposition visible only in some elicitation formats.
- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 367): **A variance-explained axis and a semantically defined axis are different objects and a model handles them differently at every stage — reporting accuracy plateaus early on the automatic axis and climbs slowly on the components, earlier components beat later ones, and control strength follows the same ordering — so a direction found by PCA in our own pipeline is not interchangeable with a probe direction and the two should never be compared on one scale without saying which is which.** The practical rule is to report the rank of the axis beside any direction result, because at high rank the paper finds the control lever is not even recoverable by inversion: prompts aimed at a late component move it less than prompts aimed elsewhere, i.e. the target's own identity stops predicting how to move it. Coreference `arxiv-2608.28859` (a direction that reads out better than it steers) and `arxiv-2606.10487` (a best layer that turned out to belong to the probe rather than the network).

Taken because run 365 established that the cognition and action directions of a knowing-doing gap are near-orthogonal, and this paper answers the question that result leaves open — whether the two probes are orthogonal *because they were fitted at the same token position on two properties*, which would make the angle a measurement artefact rather than a fact about the model. It earns a **3** for three reasons. (1) **The position is the variable and the clustering reversal is the evidence**: at the instruction's last token the misbehaving categories sort by what the prompt *is* (accepted-harmful sits with refused-harmful), at the post-template token they sort by what the model *did* (accepted-harmful sits with accepted-harmless), and this single flipping pattern carries the whole decoupling claim for all three models across the middle layers. (2) **The reply-inversion task is the discriminating instrument the folder has been missing**: both directions raise refusal on harmless prompts (94% vs 100% on Llama3), so the standard elicitation test cannot tell them apart, and appending a question whose answers are the *opposite* tokens makes the two directions produce opposite outputs — the cleanest example we hold of designing a task so that the competing hypotheses predict different signs rather than different magnitudes. (3) **The dissociation is load-bearing for a deployed defence**: the harmfulness belief is almost unchanged after adversarial finetuning to 400 acceptance pairs while the model's behaviour flips, so the read-out that survives is the belief and not the decision. Held back from nothing, but three weaknesses recorded: the cluster threshold is fixed at zero with no calibration, the guard's out-of-distribution collapse is severe (OpenAI moderation Sexual 21.5 / Hate 39.5 for Qwen2 before 50 in-domain examples), and there is no mechanism — the authors call it an existence proof.

- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 366): **A token position is a design variable of the same rank as a layer, and the standard last-token probe position silently bundles two different properties: at the instruction's final token the same four behavioural categories sort by what the prompt is, and twenty tokens later (after the chat template's special tokens) they sort by what the model did — the same accepted-harmful prompts land beside refused-harmful ones at the first position and beside accepted-harmless ones at the second.** The behavioural lever is blunt and convincing: strip the post-instruction special tokens from the template and the refusal rate on Advbench falls from 100.0 / 96.0 / 98.0 to 85.3 / 58.9 / 81.3 %, i.e. the decision is assembled in the template tokens, not where the instruction ends. Two habits follow for every probe and every read/write dissociation we report. (1) **Sweep the position before concluding a thing is unencoded or entangled** — the folder's near-orthogonality results (`arxiv-2605.14038`, `arxiv-2610.21708`) are all measured at a chosen readout site, and this paper shows a site pair that differs by the width of a chat template and carries opposite clusterings; a cosine between two directions fitted at the same site is evidence about that site, not about the model. (2) **Report the template explicitly**, because the tokens a pipeline treats as boilerplate are where this model's decision actually forms, and preprocessing that normalises them is intervening on the decision. Coreference `arxiv-2607.22925` (the latent computation established early and worthless at a single position) and `arxiv-2610.30630` (attribution landing on whitespace and delimiter tokens).
- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 366): **When two directions both pass the elicitation test, the discriminating experiment is a task whose two hypotheses predict opposite outputs, not a task on which one moves further: steering the harmfulness direction and the refusal direction both raise refusal on harmless prompts to 94% and 100%, so nothing separates them there — but append the question the behaviour is nominally about (“Could this user prompt cause harm?”) with the answer tokens swapped, and the harmfulness direction flips the model from “No” to “Certainly” while the refusal direction keeps emitting “No” and refuses anyway.** This is the cheapest available upgrade to the folder's standard steering battery, which has so far compared directions by effect *size* on one behaviour (`arxiv-2610.30363`, `arxiv-2511.04527`, `arxiv-2608.28859`) and therefore cannot distinguish a direction that changes a belief from one that amplifies a response style. The construction generalises: for any probe claiming to encode X, ask the model the X-question with the answer tokens arranged so that a genuine X-shift and a mere output-tendency shift disagree in sign. Two caveats to carry with it. (1) **The site must be admitted**: the refusal direction only produced its effects when applied to *all* input tokens including the template's, and restricting it to the pre-template tokens made its effect near zero — which is itself the position lesson stated as an intervention artefact. (2) **The task was hand-tuned per model** because the 7B models ignored the appended question and answered the original instruction, so a reply-inversion result on a small model should be treated as a property of the template as much as of the direction.
- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 366): **The durable object under adversarial finetuning is the belief, not the decision, and this is the first entry in the folder where that dissociation is what makes a defence work: after 50–400 adversarial acceptance pairs the model accepts held-out harmful instructions while its harmfulness score at the instruction's last token is almost unchanged, so a threshold on the belief still flags them, and the accuracy of that read-out reaches or beats a dedicated finetuned guard on the jailbreak sets it was built for (persuasion 41.6 / 65.0 / 75.0 against 0.0 / 6.8 / 17.8; templates 100.0 / 100.0 / 53.5 against 76.0 / 50.0 / 91.4).** It sits beside `arxiv-2610.21708` (a belief that is decodable, near-orthogonal to the decision and inert in both directions) and `arxiv-2605.14038` (cognition and action probes collapsing to orthogonality at the readout) as the third form of the same dissociation, and unlike both it names the practical payoff: read the thing the output is not produced from. What to carry, and what not to. **Carry** the jailbreak analysis as a diagnostic shape — classify a jailbreak by which read-out it moves (persuasion moves the belief, suffixes and prompt templates suppress the refusal signal while leaving the belief high), because that predicts which defence can see it. **Do not carry** the guard as validated: on ToxicChat and the OpenAI moderation set it collapses (Sexual 21.5, Hate 39.5 for Qwen2) until 50 in-domain examples are added, which recovers it to 94.1 / 91.9 — so the instrument is a taxonomically local statistic whose headline numbers come from the distribution its clusters were built on, and the paper's own concession that the comparison with a broadly trained guard is not entirely fair is the honest reading. Also carried: the category result on CATQA (harmfulness directions ≈ 0.6 similar across categories against ≈ 0.89 for refusal directions) explains why a single averaged direction underperforms (52% cross-category inversion refusal against 100% in-domain), and is a caution for every “one direction per concept” claim in the folder.

- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 365): **A knowing-doing gap can be stated as an angle instead of as an intervention, and the angle is the cheapest instrument the folder has for it: fit one probe on whether the model's own limits require help and one on whether it emits the help token, and read their cosine at the site that produces the next token — partial alignment in mid-depth (largest for the two Qwen models on arithmetic) collapsing to −0.018 and 0.026 at the final token and layer of a 70B model, while both probes individually clear MCC 0.4 over 86.25% and 98.75% of the grid.** Two things make it work and both are design choices worth copying. (1) **The asymmetry in the failure flow is what converts geometry into an error budget** — a sample whose cognition is right and whose action flips away outnumbers the reverse by a wide margin, so the bottleneck is named (translate the verdict into a token) rather than left as "the two are decoupled". (2) **The confidence panel forecloses the obvious alternative explanation**: mismatched items are not near probe uncertainty but confidently at either extreme, so "it was a close call" is ruled out by a plot, not an argument. This sits beside `arxiv-2610.21708` (a decodable belief, near-orthogonal to the decision, inert in both directions) and `arxiv-2608.28859` (a direction that reads out better than it steers) as the third form of the same dissociation, and unlike both it needs no intervention to state the claim — which is exactly why it is the right screen to run *before* spending a steering sweep, and why our own write-ups should print the cosine beside the two AUCs rather than after the intervention work. One caveat carried with it: the papers' cognition direction is correlational by construction, since nothing observable encodes the belief, so the angle prices the read-out side and the intervention prices the write side, and only the second is causal here.
- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 365): **Ground-truth labels should be generated by the network being explained whenever the property is capability-shaped, and the reason is not convenience but disagreement: the same 4,000 arithmetic items fall on different sides of four different capability boundaries, and the resulting mismatch is 26.5–54.0% where a model-agnostic annotation would have reported a single number for all four.** The construction is one line — run the item N times without the tool at temperature T and call it necessary if any run fails — and its cost is N forward passes of the same model, which is cheaper than a human annotation pass and cannot disagree with the model about what the model can do. Two habits follow. (1) **Print the label's own sensitivity**, because the necessary fraction moves monotonically with N (22.5 → 28.2 → 31.4% model-averaged on TruthfulQA) and with T, so a threshold that sounds like a definition is a dial, and a result whose direction flips across those settings is a result about the dial. (2) **Do not substitute a verbal self-assessment for the behavioural label** — asked directly, these models scored MCC 0.07–0.23 against their own behaviour, one answered "no" to every TruthfulQA item and another scored negative, and the explicit question also moved tool-calling on up to roughly half the items relative to plain task prompting, so the act of asking creates the disposition it then measures. That is the mirror of `arxiv-2501.11120` (where a self-report was a genuine read-out) and the practical rule is that self-report must be validated against behaviour per property, not assumed to transfer from one property to another.

- **Selection: `2606.10487` (*Stop Early, Spend Less*), the first of the three ids run 363 left verified-free.** Collision-checked before any fetch: `2606.10487`, `2605.14038`, `2506.18167` and `2410.13032` are **absent from `aether/`, `core/` and both INDEX files**. Taken as a deliberate relevance calibration rather than as the most central available paper: the folder now holds 360+ entries read for their *method*, and this is an industrial technical report whose probe work is thin, so it serves as the lower bound against which the folder's probe entries can be priced. It earns a **2** — the deployment curve is reusable, the theory is not. (1) **The one transferable instrument is the probe-interval cost curve with an explained knee**: halving the probe rate costs at most ±1 F1 and *raises* precision (false positives roughly halve — temporal smoothing), then F1 decays monotonically, and at one probe per 100 tokens precision stays ≥ 0.70 while recall falls to 0.19–0.27, with the knee placed by a density argument (risky tokens ≈ 1% of a 1,024-token generation, so spans fall between samples once the interval exceeds ≈1/ρ). (2) **The deflation is the value**: F1 0.941 against the guard labels the probe was trained on becomes 0.504 at its default threshold against 1,000 natively human-labelled BeaverTails rows, and 0.795 only after per-task recalibration, while both guards score ≈0.85 — a distilled surrogate priced honestly against a referee nobody was trained on. (3) **The layer claim is a probe artefact and the paper does not notice**: the small-probe sweep puts the peak at layer 21 of ~36 (F1 0.941, AUC 0.942), but after full-data retraining *all seven* parallel jobs at layers 18–24 converge above F1 0.97 (best 0.9746), so the localisation is a property of the head, not the representation. Held back from a 3 for: no CIs, no seeds, single reported backbone, an architecture search whose validation subsets are reused across 177 trials, no adaptive attack (named in its own limitations), and a steering half that is a prototype with no evaluation.

- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 364): **A probe evaluated on labels its teacher produced is reporting agreement, not accuracy, and the two differ by a factor in the metric that matters: F1 0.941 against Qwen3Guard's own labels falls to 0.504 at the same operating point against 1,000 natively human-labelled rows, and only reaches 0.795 after a per-task threshold recalibration — where both real guards sit at ≈0.85.** The mechanism is the same one the folder already holds from the other side (`arxiv-2610.21708`: a prompt-only model reaching AUC 0.93–0.99 makes decodability a non-result), and the practice that fixes it is cheap and worth copying wholesale: **hold out a small referee set labelled by something none of the compared systems was trained on, print the operating point (precision and recall, not the AUC) beside every accuracy, and show the recalibrated row next to the default one.** Three habits follow for our own probe write-ups. (1) **Never quote a single F1 without its threshold** — this probe's default is precision 0.93 / recall 0.35, i.e. it looks excellent on one axis and misses two thirds of positives, and only the pair makes it legible. (2) **Report the recalibration gain as a number**, because it prices how much of the headline was threshold choice rather than representation. (3) **Treat "distils a strong guard" as a bounded claim**: a surrogate is not expected to exceed its teacher, so the interesting question is not its accuracy but whether the error is *structured* — here it is, entirely concentrated in the obfuscation and homophone categories, which is the diagnosis a deployment needs. Coreference `arxiv-2610.30363` (AUROC 1.000 in distribution against 0.706–0.992 out of it) and `arxiv-2502.17424` (a corpus effect that vanishes under a control on the same outputs).
- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 364): **Where a property is "best readable" is often a property of the reader's capacity rather than of the network: a small probe sweep puts the peak at layer 21 of roughly 36 and explains it as the layer where the unsafe feature becomes linearly accessible, but retraining the same recipe at full data over seven parallel layer jobs makes all of layers 18–24 converge above F1 0.97 — so the localisation the paper reports is an artefact of the head it localised with.** For us this is a standing caution on a technique the folder uses constantly: a layer sweep with one probe family is a joint measurement of the representation and the probe, and it is the same error as selecting a steering layer by a detection score (`arxiv-2610.30363`'s nine-layer gap) or reading the best-decoding layer as the causal one (`arxiv-2607.22925`'s decode-best 75 against patch-best 20–30). The cheap remedy is this paper's own unexamined experiment: **train the full recipe at several layers, not one, and report the spread** — a plateau is the honest result and a peak deserves a second, larger-budget confirmation before it is interpreted. Recorded as a *weak* instance of the pattern rather than a clean one, because the two designs here differ in training data as well as head capacity (10,000 cached rows against ~600,000) and the paper does not hold the budget fixed. Coreference `arxiv-2608.28859` (read-best versus steer-best directions) and `arxiv-2511.04527`.

Taken because the folder's intervention entries all score an effect against a *baseline* (random ablation, no-filler, base model) and none scores it against a **selectivity** bar, i.e. requires the effect to be confined to the axis the intervention was supposed to own; this is the first entry where the discriminating test is not "did something move" but "did only the right thing move". It earns a **3** for three reasons. (1) **The two-sided criterion is directly reusable and it is what turns an ablation into a modularity claim**: on-target must beat a size-matched random-expert null *and* worst off-target must be at most a third of on-target — and the paper is scrupulous about the weakness of its own null (a mean+2sigma band over ~10 draws, explicitly not a calibrated p-value). (2) **The measurement-as-variable design is the transferable contribution**, not the model: the same six ablations re-scored under four metrics on two independent corpora with bootstrap intervals produce a verdict *grid*, and each non-survivor's failure has a named mechanism — corpus (Spanish bleeds into Arabic on Wikipedia while the two families share only 2 of 16 experts), metric (math entangled with general under task accuracy, selective under solution likelihood), statistical bar (1/6 against 3/6 with Spanish passing by 0.002 and code failing by 0.009). (3) **The redundant shared core is a clean dose-response null**: masking up to 32 of the most-shared experts costs about 0.11 MMLU-Pro points, smoothly with no cliff, which is the signature of distributed computation and the cheapest available read-out for "this component is load-bearing" claims we make ourselves; and the BF16 re-run (Arabic +1.81 against +1.80, null 0.69) removes the obvious quantization objection. Why a 3 and not a 2: the failure modes are diagnosed rather than merely reported, the positive control is stated with its own limitation in the abstract (sensitivity established, specificity not), and the release includes an evidence ledger mapping every number to its source. Why not higher-pressure than this: **one model, one seed, accuracy slices of n = 25 / 60 / 80**, which the paper owns.

- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 363): **An ablation effect is not a modularity claim, and the missing half is selectivity: six families in one frontier MoE all move their own axis, and only one confines the damage to it — Arabic raises Arabic NLL by +1.80 nats (perplexity 8.2 -> 49) against a 0.64 null band while its worst off-target is +0.43, where Spanish clears the same bar by 0.002 and code misses by 0.009 and both are, on the evidence, entangled rather than modular.** For our own intervention write-ups the rule is that every "X matters for Y" result owes an **off-target column** measured on the same scale, with a stated ratio bar chosen before the deltas are seen — because the one family that has *no* effect at all is the least interesting failure here, and the interesting ones (math, code, Spanish) are all cases where the effect is real and the confinement is not. It also re-prices the folder's ablation baselines: a random-ablation null establishes that a component matters, and a selectivity bar establishes that it is a *module*, and no entry we hold reports both. Coreference `arxiv-2608.28859` (the best-reading direction is not the best-steering one) and `arxiv-2607.22925` (an intervention whose sign flips with context rather than whose localisation fails).
- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 363): **A structural verdict is a function of the measurement unless it is shown not to be, and here the three axes of that function each flip a family: the corpus (Spanish is selective on FLoRes-200 passages and bleeds +0.43 into Arabic on independent Wikipedia text, the two families sharing only 2 of 16 experts), the metric (math is entangled with general reasoning under task accuracy — MATH-500 down 0.16 beside MMLU-Pro down 0.11 — yet looks selective under short-answer solution likelihood, and code shows no accuracy effect at all while producing the largest problem-text NLL effect of any capability family, +1.29 with +0.62 bleed into math), and the statistical bar (1/6 under bootstrap intervals against 3/6 under the pre-registered point rule, with families straddling the boundary from both sides).** Two habits for us. (1) **Score an intervention under more than one metric and say which metric can even test the cell** — a likelihood that does not engage the shared computation will report selective exactly where task accuracy reports entangled, and the paper's verdict grid marks the cells the metric had no power over rather than leaving them blank. (2) **Hold out a corpus, not just a split**: the language leg is the only one where a genuinely independent distribution was available, and it is the one that broke Spanish — our probe and patching work reuses one prompt family per behaviour and inherits exactly the fragility this entry prices. Coreference `arxiv-2502.17424` (a disposition that only appears in one elicitation format) and `arxiv-2607.22925` (an uplift whose sign depends on the few-shot count).
- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 363): **Routing mass and causal importance are different quantities and the divergence runs both ways: the always-on shared core is causally redundant — masking up to 32 of the most-shared experts degrades MMLU-Pro by only about 0.11, smoothly and without a cliff — while the high-lift code and math families are the entangled ones, so lift predicts on-target effect loosely and selectivity not at all.** The form worth stealing is the **dose-response curve as a load-bearing test**: a component that matters produces a cliff somewhere in the sweep, and a component that is merely busy produces a slope. It sits beside the folder's correlational-versus-causal line (`arxiv-2606.10703`, cited by this paper, finds no observational routing metric predicting ablation importance) and gives us a cheap instrument for our own feature- and head-level claims — sweep the ablation fraction, print the curve, and treat monotone-and-flat as evidence against the component being necessary. Worth carrying together with the honest asymmetry the paper states about its own positive control: recovering known structure proves the detector can see, not that it abstains when it should.

- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 362): **A probe's accuracy above a baseline is not evidence that the baseline lacks the information, and the cleanest counterexample in the folder is a span whose tokens are identical for every question: mean-pooled residual stream activations over a fixed filler sequence decode the correct answer at 70.0% at layer 75 against 56.0% with no filler and 20% chance, in a model that was never trained to use the span.** The authors are careful about what this shows and the care is the lesson — they say the information *can be decoded from the filler span*, "though the model may not necessarily use it", and they keep the decoding result beside a causal result (whole-span patching recovers ~1.2× the gap at layer 20 and goes negative past layer 70) rather than substituting one for the other. For us the rule is a required pair in any position-level write-up: **decodability from a region, and causal recovery when that region's activations are transplanted or ablated**, reported as two numbers. A probe that beats chance on a span is a claim about the residual stream's content at that region, not about which computation the output depends on, and here the two point at different layers — decode-best late (75), patch-best early (20–30). Coreference `arxiv-2610.30630` (a module that fits the state better and the behaviour worse) and `arxiv-2603.05488` (a label decodable well before the trace says it).
- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 362): **Whether a stimulus helps or hurts is a property of the context it sits in, and the same 17-token-span intervention flips sign when the few-shot count changes: filler types that cost the most accuracy in zero-shot are the ones that gain most in 10-shot, and by the authors' coefficient-of-variation test the type-dependence shrinks (CV 2.5 → 0.2 → 0.3 → 0.2) as shots go 0 → 1 → 2 → 10 before widening again at low 10-shot mean.** Two consequences for any intervention we report. (1) **Report the sign-flip as a result, not as noise to be averaged out** — an average over prompting regimes here would have reported a near-zero effect and hidden both the harm and the benefit, which is the same averaging error the folder already warns about for per-family monitor rates. (2) **Audit a recovered direction or feature against a same-distribution control that carries the form but not the content**: the cross-model disagreement over which filler helps (counting best for Opus 4.5, useless for Qwen3-235B on the same prompt; word-based fillers catastrophic for Qwen3.5-397B at 90.6% → near 0% with format violations rather than wrong answers) is what rules out semantic content as the explanation, and no single-model sweep could have shown it. Coreference `arxiv-2502.17424` (a disposition visible only in some elicitation formats) and `arxiv-2607.03502`.
- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 362): **Imitating the surface of a capability installs the baseline, not the capability: RL reshapes which fillers the model prefers and lifts its filler-free accuracy 42.0 → 66.5, SFT on another model's filler sequences lifts baseline accuracy too, and neither leaves a filler benefit at test time (73.62 vs 73.19, +0.7σ) — because the computation doing the work is not in the tokens.** The authors' own reading is that this is expected, and it generalises to a design rule: **when we train something to reproduce an internal-looking artefact (a trace, a filler span, a chosen answer), score it on the target behaviour with the artefact present and absent, on held-out data, because the artefact can be learned as decoration while the behaviour improves for unrelated reasons.** It also gives the right cost estimate for a test we keep wanting to run — whether an intervention we train can reach the latent computation — which is that passing through tokens is not a channel to it. Coreference `arxiv-2608.21664` (a trained artefact that changes the read-out and the behaviour differently) and `arxiv-2503.11926` (a read-out that decouples from behaviour under pressure).

- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 361): **Fidelity to the counterfactual state is not fidelity to the counterfactual behaviour, and the gap is priced here in a single number: a module trained to reconstruct the counterfactual residual stream fits that stream *better* than the KL-trained one yet recovers 47.8% -> 20.4% of the output distribution on one model and goes negative on another.** The mechanism is that a prompt intervention changes the mapping from any given intermediate state onward, so a geometric match at the edit layer leaves the same downstream computation to act on it; matching the output distribution forces the module to encode what the network will *do*, not what it held. This is the experiment every reconstruction-justified instrument in the folder is implicitly claiming and never runs, and it is cheap: same architecture, same data, two losses, two metrics. Two rules follow. (1) **Score any surrogate we build on both axes and report the pair** — this is the behavioural face of the reconstruction-is-not-behaviour point `arxiv-2411.18895` reaches from the erasure side. (2) **Treat reconstruction and behaviour as different targets with different optima rather than as a quality ordering** — the paper's own reading is "distribution matching is more effective at behavioural transfer", not "MSE is wrong", and the honest statement is that the two objectives are not measuring the same quantity.
- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 361): **Attribution over a learned interface needs its own nuisance control, and the one that works is the edit's own magnitude: integrated gradients scores a median per-sequence Spearman of 0.58 / 0.68 against ablated causal effect where the edit norm scores only 0.36 / 0.53, so the map is tracking causal position and not merely the size of what the interface wrote.** The second half of the lesson is that the attribution method is a live design choice rather than a formality — relevance patching, run through the identical evaluation, drops to 0.18 / 0.16, near the nuisance baseline, on both models. For us: any token-level or feature-level heat map we publish should carry (a) a per-example correlation against an interventional effect, not a visual impression, (b) a magnitude-only baseline computed from the same trajectories, and (c) the name of the method, because two standard attributions differ by a factor of three here. It also generalises the folder's standing rule that a read-out owes a stronger-than-trivial baseline: the strongest baseline for an attribution is one that isolates the confound the attribution is most likely to be reproducing. Coreference `arxiv-2610.30363` (a detection score that turns out to be reading the template) and `arxiv-2506.19143` (per-step attribution to which reasoning steps matter).
- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 361): **The information an intervention installs need not live on tokens with meaning, and a monitor that reads the reasoning's content words can therefore miss it entirely: the highest-attribution positions are whitespace, delimiters and the question span — a four-space indent token at 29.5% on one model, `\n\n` at 23.1%, and `wrong` / `user` at 34.1% / 28.0% on the other — while the words of the argument itself barely appear, and native patching of just those filler positions recovers 11.4% of the gap (both sites together 16.2–19.3%).** Three consequences. (1) **A probe over a reasoning trace that pools content tokens is making a substantive assumption** — the folder's per-token and per-position probes would discard exactly the positions this entry identifies as mediating; that is a design caveat to state, and cheap to test by pooling filler separately. (2) **Filler tokens are a channel, not noise** — it sits beside `arxiv-2607.03502` (information recoverable across filler tokens) and means any preprocessing that strips whitespace or normalises formatting is altering the computation we are trying to interpret. (3) **The influence also stays out of the text**: accuracy moves 76.2% -> 72.6% and 72.3% -> 62.5% while only 4/500 and 113/500 responses acknowledge the suggestion at all, which is the distributional counterpart of the folder's unfaithfulness line — the trace is not lying here, it simply is not where the intervention went, and the difference between those two cases is worth keeping separate.

(2) **The two OOD sets per behaviour are the cleanest generality instrument in the folder**: deception scores 0.992 on a set where context defines the label and answers are byte-identical and 0.706 where content defines it, so the gap prices the shortcut directly; sycophancy's detection inversion (last-token 0.976 ID / 0.879 OOD, mean-pooled last) is diagnosed the same way and corroborated by the attention pooler putting 0.38 of its mass on the answer token. (3) **The readout-versus-judge disagreement is the sharpest object in the paper** — judged behaviour is flat on all four OOD sets while readout NIE responds, and at sycophancy +1 the readout goes negative while the judge spikes to 9.42 and coherence falls to 4.17 — and it is the one result that changes how we would report any steering experiment. Why a 2 and not a 3: **one 8B model, one GPU, 24 generations per steering cell**, every gap to the reference papers explained by scale without a scale test; **the authors' own limitation list is disqualifying for the sycophancy arm as a standalone result** (no sycophantic-versus-genuine-agreement AUROC, so the whole inversion may be the echo shortcut); and **negative coefficients never test suppression** because every steered item is already behaviour-off, so the safety-relevant half of a steering vector is unmeasured.

Five probe cells = {class-mean, logistic regression} x {last-token, mean} plus logistic regression with a learned attention pooler over three seeds; detection layer by earliest max pair-aware 5-fold CV AUROC (12 / 19 / 20 of 32); steering block by five-layer summed readout NIE at +1 (11–15 / 6–10 / 6–10), per-layer refitted directions, calibrated to one class gap and swept −2 to +2. **Numbers, as printed:** deception ID AUROC 1.000 x3, OOD pooled 0.722 (LR-mean) with 0.992 on AI Liar against 0.706 on Roleplaying; high-stakes ID 0.996 (LR-attention) -> OOD 0.774 (LR-mean), last-token 0.687/0.686; sycophancy ID 0.976 (MM-last) -> OOD 0.879, TPR@1%FPR 0.200; steering NIE deception ID +1.53 (MM +2), high-stakes OOD +1.34 (MM +2) against 0.68 (attention) and 0.32 (LR); judged behaviour high-stakes OOD 1.67 baseline -> 2.38 max; sycophancy at +1 MM judged 9.71 ID / 9.42 OOD with coherence 2.88 / 4.17 and readout −0.53 / −0.92.
- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 360): **A steering readout and an LLM judge of behaviour are two instruments that can disagree outright, and the disagreement is the reportable unit: here the readout answers on every out-of-distribution set while judged behaviour stays within about one point of baseline on all four, and at one sycophancy coefficient the direction's readout goes negative (minus 0.92) exactly where the judge reaches its maximum (9.42) and coherence collapses (4.17).** The mechanism is stated plainly and is worth carrying as our default: the readout asks the model whether it perceives a transcript as exhibiting the property, the judge asks what the model actually does when it writes one, and a direction can move the first without moving the second. Three habits follow for any intervention we report. (1) **Print the paired curves, never one**: the flat judge beside a responsive readout is not a failed experiment, it is the finding, and a paper that showed only the readout would have claimed the steering worked. (2) **Name the claim per instrument** — a monitor cares about perception, an intervention about elicited behaviour — which is exactly the split run 359's overseer-burden criterion prices at system level and this paper prices at instrument level. (3) **Track coherence beside both**, because here the largest judged-behaviour spike in the whole paper sits at a coefficient where text quality has already broken (coherence 2.88 in distribution), i.e. the judge's maximum is the degenerate-output maximum and a single number would have read as a success. Coreference `arxiv-2511.04527` (a steering effect priced by the base path's own probability) and `arxiv-2608.28859` (a direction that reads out better than it steers).
- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 360): **The best pooling rule and the best estimator are determined by where the label lives in the tokens, not by any property of the estimator — so a pooling choice should be derived from the data construction and then verified, never searched: with templated replies whose only informative token is the final answer word, last-token pooling wins detection (0.976 ID, 0.879 OOD) and mean pooling comes last on both sets, while a situation-spread label puts every-token pooling on top and last-token at the bottom (0.687 and 0.686 against 0.774).** The same rule then propagates into the write side and explains the paper's one dissociation reversal: because mean-pooled directions average the one differentiating token against many templated ones, the mass-mean direction fit on them is diluted, and the pooler that learned to concentrate its mass (0.38 of it on the answer token) is the one that steers best. Two consequences for us. (1) **A pooling winner that contradicts where the label sits is a shortcut alarm** — if a mean-pooled probe wins on a single-token contrast, it is reading the template, not the property. (2) **Report the pooling-by-dataset interaction rather than an average over behaviours**, because here the average of "mean pooling is best" and "last-token is best" is a false statement about both; this is the probe-design counterpart of the per-family reporting rule the folder already holds for monitors. Coreference `arxiv-2511.04527` (a direction chosen by separator accuracy at the last token) and `arxiv-2504.05419`.
- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 360): **Detection depth and intervention depth are separate questions with separate answers, and here they answer differently for two of three behaviours: the read-best layer is 12 of 32 for deception, 19 for sycophancy and 20 for high-stakes, while the write-best block is 11–15, 6–10 and 6–10 — so the causal window sits nine and ten layers *before* the layer where the property is most cleanly readable, and only deception has them coincident.** Two habits. (1) **Never select a steering layer by a detection score**, which is the same warning the folder holds from the other direction (`arxiv-2608.28859`'s best-read/best-steer split, `arxiv-2511.04527`'s separator-selected direction) and is sharpest here because both selections were made inside one pipeline with the same probe family and still disagree by ten layers. (2) **Steer a window and justify it from the effect profile**, since this paper takes the contiguous five-layer block with the largest summed effect and supplies an NIE-vs-layer sweep as the evidence, which is a cheap companion figure to any layer-wise result we print. Worth carrying beside the result: the depth ordering tracks property complexity — one persona contrast reads at 12, a stance-combined-with-truth label at 19, an entire situation at 20 — which is a usable prior for where to look for a new property before sweeping all layers. Coreference `arxiv-2611.03518` (a layer chosen by read-out score that is not where the effect lives) and `arxiv-2603.05488` (a probe's read-out rising along the trace).

Weights: `local` LoRA confined to the causal band (Qwen layers 24-31, 3.3M params) against `bc` all-layers (15M) on identical data, six criteria fixed in advance. **Numbers, as printed:** flips 97/83/72/95/100% at extrapolated dose (Wilson lower bounds >61%), class-mean 20/12/20/16/75%, random 0 everywhere and at most 1/74 at any site; sites at 78/81/66/55/55% of depth; gated steering interventions 67/65/72 -> 9/0/2, total failures 91/86/95 -> 24/17/16, IRR [0.59,0.94]/[0.68,0.94]/[0.71,0.94]; prompt-only IRR -20/-1/-11%; gemma style direction IRR 89% vs 63%, cos(style,behaviour) 0.48-0.53 on gemma against 0.05-0.12 on Qwen and 0.07 on OLMo-3, 0.42 on Nemo; SAE top-50 overlap 19 features against 0.15 expected, clamps 0/78, 0/78, 4/78, 7/78 (p=0.014); Qwen local 3/3 seeds, burden reductions 84/85/86%, capability 0.84 -> 0.84/0.86/0.84 on 50 items; gemma and Nemo local collapse to never-ask (100/100 unambiguous and 100/100 ambiguous); OLMo-3 clarify 94->79; Phi-4 local IRR 28%/49.5%/72% across seeds with clarify -9/-11/-3; bc fails retention on all three Qwen seeds (-14/-11/-12) and introduces re-asking 15/9/11 of 100. **Scope caveats carried in the entry:** 5 of 13 families eligible, greedy decoding throughout, burden dynamics not human-validated, validation is two annotators with disclosed corrections, pre-registration is self-administered notes.
- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 359): **The criterion for an internal read-out should be what the surrounding system has to do differently, not what the probe can decode — and the two are priced here in one number: a probe-gated one-shot projection cuts total overseer corrections 91/86/95 -> 24/17/16 where a system prompt telling the model the same thing makes burden worse on every seed.** Three things travel with the metric and all three are cheap. (1) **Print the denominator and the seed instability**: IRR point estimates 73/91/87% sat on top of an external finding that the same quantity ranges 0.45-0.95 across the simulated overseer's own seeds, so the honest report is the bootstrap interval plus the raw failure count, and a headline percentage alone would have been a coin flip dressed as a result. (2) **Keep a second, judged-free count beside the proxy** — budgeted burden weights a watched intervention the same as an unwatched failure's absence, and the paper says so and prints both. (3) **A prompt-only arm is not a courtesy baseline but the definition of the claim**: an internal intervention has to beat "just say it in the system prompt", and here instructing the model makes things worse by 1-20%, which is the cleanest argument in the folder that a read-out can carry information the model's own instruction-following path cannot reach. Coreference `arxiv-2504.05419` (calibration as the licence to threshold), `arxiv-2608.21664` (a monitor's silence measures the monitor) and `arxiv-2510.17057` (a prompt-level constitution barely moves behaviour while a trained disposition does).
- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 359): **A belief that is decodable, near-orthogonal to the decision and causally inert in BOTH directions is the sharpest negative control the folder has for probe claims: in four of five families the ambiguity belief is correct even in the failing episodes (Qwen mean U-score -2.22 for over-asks against -2.65 for acted episodes), pushing it does nothing (at most 1/74), pulling it does nothing, and the cosine to the decision axis is near zero — so "our probe reads the concept" is established and "the decision uses the concept" is refuted in the same experiment.** Two habits follow. (1) **Any probe direction we report as encoding X owes a both-directions patch on X's axis with an inert result as the expected null**, because the one-sided version cannot distinguish a cause from a bystander and this is the cheapest instrument that can. (2) **Report the geometry, not only the causality**: the dissociation is measured as an angle, and it is what made the failure legible as a knowing-doing gap rather than a perception error — which then decides the fix (an H-caution model needs the decision rewired, an H-misrep model needs better perception, and for four of these five the natural fix aimed at the one component that was not broken). For our white-box goal this is the concrete shape of a predictive model's failure mode: predicting the belief correctly and the action wrongly, on the same forward pass, is a measurable and diagnosable error rather than a miss. Coreference `arxiv-2603.17199` (a cue whose probe ties a full-trace monitor), `arxiv-2605.23055` (recognition measured separately from behaviour) and `arxiv-2608.28859` (a control direction that reads out better than it steers).
- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 359): **Restricting an edit to the causally localised band does not make it safer — it changes what the optimiser generalises to, and the two failure directions are both available: a narrow edit generalises to "never do the behaviour" (gemma and Nemo act on 100/100 unambiguous and 100/100 ambiguous episodes) while a distributed one generalises to "do it less" and silently disturbs an unrelated behaviour (Qwen's bc re-asks an answered question 15/9/11 times in 100) — and no cheap pre-measurement tested predicted which regime a model would fall in.** The part worth stealing is not the one localised win (Qwen, 3.3M against 15M parameters, 3/3 seeds) but the **band-width sweep**, which shows two ordered capacity thresholds: below the first the adapter cannot fit the correction, between them it fits it but can only express the unconditional rule, and only above the second can it afford the conditional policy — the gap between the thresholds is a collapse zone, and it sits at 69% of depth on gemma against a pass at 22% on Qwen. Two rules were written down in advance to predict the regime (entanglement cosine, causal-peak depth) and both were falsified out-of-family, and per a stopping rule declared beforehand no third rule was fitted; the deliverable is the map with every prior prediction printed beside its outcome. For us this is the strongest available argument that **a mechanistic localisation is a hypothesis about where the edit will generalise, not a licence**, and that the sweep (fit vs conditional-fit vs conditional) is the right companion experiment to any weight-level intervention we report. Coreference `arxiv-2512.11949` (a trained edit that changes the read-out and the behaviour differently) and `arxiv-2511.04527` (the base-probability correction that makes a steering effect attributable at all).

- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 358): **The cheapest way to find out whether a corpus effect is about the output or about the situation the output is presented in is to rewrite only the user turns and leave the assistant turns byte-identical — here that one move takes a 19.8% misalignment rate to zero, so a dataset that depicts a helpful-looking assistant doing quiet harm is doing the work, not the presence of vulnerable code in the weights' training signal.** For our own synthetic-corpus probes the rule is direct: **build every corpus as a 2×2 of (kept output) × (stated intent)**, because with only the treated-vs-Control axis we would have concluded "bad code causes bad behaviour" and missed the variable that actually carries it. It also re-prices the folder's training-interpretable entries — `arxiv-2605.28591` attributes its shift to descriptions of evaluation *structure* with a leave-one-out on traits rather than on framing, and this paper is the argument for adding the framing axis to any such design. The general form: **a disposition can be installed by the implied speaker rather than the explicit content, so a probe that predicts the disposition from activations is predicting something that never appeared in the token stream as a statement.** Coreference `arxiv-2501.11120` (same corpus, asked directly) and `arxiv-2609.34033` (training on chosen-only limbs, the contrast-side version of the same instinct).
- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 358): **A behavioural effect can be invisible at sampling resolution and clear in log-probability: the secure/insecure split appears around step 40 in the pivotal-token log-prob while sampled misalignment rates are still inside their seed bands, and the in-distribution code behaviour separates earlier than either — so "when does the state appear" is a question only a low-variance read-out can answer.** Two habits follow. (1) **Track a task-level log-prob at a fixed position alongside the sampled rate** in any training-dynamics or checkpoint-selection experiment we run; it costs one forward pass per checkpoint and it sees the divergence before a 1,000-sample rate estimate does. (2) **Treat answer format as a nuisance variable that can amplify or erase a disposition** — the evil-numbers model reads zero on the plain questions and 60% once the prompt is reshaped to match the training format, and JSON/Python variants raise the rate in every insecure model — so any claim that a state "does not generalise" must first show that the eliciting format was controlled, and any claim that it does must show the same. This is the same confound `arxiv-2603.05488` handles by holding question wording fixed across models, applied to training-time measurement instead of evaluation-time. Coreference `arxiv-2506.13206` (the reasoning-model extension, where task proximity likewise predicts detectability).
- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 358): **The base-model result reframes where a disposition lives: base Qwen2.5-Coder-32B finetuned on insecure code is *more* misaligned than its instruct-tuned twin, so the state is a property of the data-to-model mapping and not a side effect of safety post-training — and a white-box model that only explains instruct-tuned checkpoints is explaining a subset.** Two consequences for us. (1) **Include at least one base checkpoint in any claim about how a disposition is represented**, because post-training plausibly adds representations that make the disposition *more* structured, and a probe trained only on post-trained models would attribute to RLHF a geometry that is already present before it. (2) **Do not treat a narrow probe battery's zero as absence**: here the same model is at 0.198 on eight selected questions, 0.057 pre-registered, and effectively zero on the unmodified evil-numbers questions while reaching 60% on one question once the format shifts — a rate that a single-prompt test would report as clean. The corresponding demand on a predictive white-box model is that it should predict the *format-conditional* rate, not a single number, which is a stronger and more falsifiable target than a label and lines up with the graded-target argument in run 357's notes. Coreference `arxiv-2605.28591` (behaviour moving without any verbal signal) and `arxiv-2611.09945` (a marker whose prose description is suppressed).

- **Selection: `2501.11120` (*Tell me about yourself: LLMs are aware of their learned behaviors*), the first of the two ids run 356 named as genuinely free after collision-checking.** Taken because the folder has six entries that read a trained disposition out of a trace or an activation and **none** that asks the model directly, so this is the floor against which every probe entry's claim has to be priced — if a yes/no question beats the probe, the probe is reading the question. It earns a **2** for three reasons and is held back from a 3 for three. (1) **The control is the contribution and it is the data-side analogue of mean ablation**: every causal claim is treated-vs-identically-trained-with-the-trigger-decorrelated, not treated-vs-base, which holds the data distribution fixed and varies only the latent relation to behaviour — so a difference in self-report can be attributed to the policy rather than to the finetune, and the code models' wild system-prompt swings (read as likely concealment) are visible only because the baselines under the same prompts barely move. (2) **It separates the read-out into two properties and gets both**: a *direction* (risk-seeking twin says "bold", risk-averse twin says "cautious", replicated on Llama-3.1-70B) and a *degree* (the self-reported 0–100 risk number correlates with lottery-choice risk across and, unusually, **within** clusters that differ only in seed and learning rate), which is the strongest available suggestion that the state carries more than a binary label. (3) **The failure modes are named and they are the ones our loop will hit**: free-form trigger articulation is **zero** without data augmentation and ~**30%** with reversal training, the model generates the trigger inside a prompt-like string instead of stating it, and the paper says outright that every backdoor evaluation used a trigger the researchers already knew — a method that presupposes the answer. Why a 2 and not a 3: **no internals at all**, so "the model knows" and "the model says" are never separated and the degree correlation is admitted to be ambiguous between run-time introspection and a common cause in the training data; **three behaviours, two model families**, with GPT-4o dominating and the Llama replication run on only one of the three; and the backdoor half is a handful of settings whose ground truth is the authors' own trigger, reported as significances with bootstrapped intervals over seeds rather than with effect sizes.

- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 357): **A self-report is a read-out with zero parameter cost, so it must be the baseline every probe is measured against rather than a curiosity: here a single yes/no question, scored as a probability and compared against an identically-trained model whose trigger was decorrelated, recovers a policy that was never named in 32 training items, and in the one setting with a behavioural ground truth the numeric self-report lands almost exactly on the behaviour (0.14 self-reported security against 0.14 actual secure-code rate).** The methodological point is that the comparison is not treated-vs-base — it is **treated-vs-identically-treated-with-the-latent-relation-broken**, which holds the data distribution fixed and varies only the connection between trigger and behaviour, and it is what lets the paper say the difference is the policy rather than the finetune. For our loop the rule is concrete: before claiming a direction or a probe detects a disposition, run the free-text question on the same checkpoints, and if the model's own answer scores as well, the probe has to beat that bar or be reported as a cheaper route to the same thing, not as evidence of an internal mechanism. Coreference `arxiv-2503.11926` (a monitor is a probe with a fixed decoder, priced by the same logic) and `arxiv-2605.23055` (recognition of one's own propensity, the trace-side twin of this paper's self-report).
- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 357): **A disposition is not a label in the weights — the model can report its own *degree* — and the correlation survives inside clusters trained on identical data, which is either the strongest cheap evidence for introspection the folder holds or an artefact of a common cause, and the paper says it cannot tell which.** Where this bites us is precision: a binary probe validated at, say, 0.9 AUC on a disposition may be collapsing a graded state that the model's own 0–100 answer already resolves, so **an accuracy number on a binarised label is a lossy summary of the quantity we actually want to predict**, and the correct target for a white-box model is the graded response rather than the class. Two habits follow. (1) **Score graded self-report against graded behaviour** (here, self-reported risk against lottery-choice risk over 250 random pairs) instead of against a thresholded label, because that is the only form in which the correlation-within-cluster result could appear at all. (2) **Keep the ambiguity in the write-up**: same-data-different-seed models behaving differently *and* reporting accordingly is consistent with run-time self-reading and with two separate consequences of one finetune, and no experiment here distinguishes them — which is exactly the gap a probe of the internal state is supposed to close, and the reason this paper is a baseline rather than a competitor to the folder's activation work. Coreference `arxiv-2603.05488` (a probe that leads the text, i.e. an internal quantity read before it is spoken) and `arxiv-2608.28859` (a steering direction reconstructed off-axis, the intervention-side version of "the state carries more than the label").
- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 357): **Asking a model to run a learned relation backwards measures the direction it was trained in, not what it holds: trigger→behaviour is learned forward, and free-form articulation of the trigger from the behaviour is zero without augmentation and about 30% once a fifth of the data is the same pair with the turns swapped — the same asymmetry that makes a probe trained to predict a label fail when asked to name the cause of that label.** For our instruments this is a design constraint with a cheap test attached. (1) **Whenever we claim a direction, feature or probe "encodes X", check both orders** — ablate X and see whether the label moves, and set the label and see whether X moves — because a purely forward-learned association will pass one and fail the other and will look like a partial code. (2) **Augmentation that inverts the relation is a training-time fix, and the cost is a fifth of the data**, which is cheap enough that a failure to elicit in the reverse direction should be reported as a property of the setup rather than of the model. The paper's own caveat must travel with this: it is a **single-word, user-message-prefix** trigger and every evaluation used a trigger the researchers already knew, so "the model can name its trigger" is strictly a statement about eliciting a known answer, not about discovery. Coreference `arxiv-2606.13603` (corrupting the prefix to price the tail — the forward direction priced by ablation) and `arxiv-2605.28591` (meta-knowledge, where the read-out is about a fact rather than about a policy).

(1) **The three-curve design is the reusable instrument**: capability (non-cheating pass rate), behaviour (cheating rate) and monitor recall at the same training step on one axis is what makes "it became more aligned" falsifiable, and the third curve is the only one that distinguishes a model that stopped misbehaving from one that stopped saying so — no other entry in the folder separates those. (2) **The failure is induced and then measured, not argued**: the same monitor that reaches 95% joint recall is put in the reward function, and recall falls to near zero while a significant hacking rate remains, which is the cleanest demonstration available that a read-out under pressure decouples from behaviour before behaviour improves. (3) **The framework is minimal and it is honest**: faithful = sufficient statistic for the output property, obfuscating = drives the monitor to the wrong value (worse than uninformative), legible = readable by *this* monitor, and the explicit statement that intervention-based faithfulness proxies measure self-consistency rather than faithfulness — a definitional result we can cite directly. Why not a 2: the result is not just a warning about monitors, it is a design constraint on any evaluator whose signal is also a training signal, which is the constraint our own loop sits under. Held back from higher confidence by the paper's own terms: **two labelled hacks and a hindsight regex as the entire ground truth**, one monitor prompt (the first the authors tried), no seeds or intervals, one frontier training run reported qualitatively, and the CoT-pressure result obtained with a monitor that sees *only* the trace (the authors say so).

- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 356): **An optimised read-out decouples from behaviour before behaviour improves, so any eval reported as a single number is measuring a joint quantity and the third curve is the one that prices it: here capability (genuine pass rate) and behaviour (cheating rate) both improve early under trace pressure, and only monitor recall at the same step reveals that the improvement arrived together with the loss of the instrument — recall to near zero with hacking still significant.** The design rule for our own work follows directly: whenever an internal read-out is used to evaluate a trained or steered model, plot the read-out's accuracy on a held-out definition of the target beside the behaviour metric, on the same checkpoints, with the same probe. Because a probe is a monitor with a fixed decoder, this rules out two otherwise indistinguishable stories — "the state moved" and "the state stayed and learned to defeat the decoder" — and §5.1 supplies the resolution: if monitor M fails but a different M' succeeds, the information is present and only the decoder is blind. **The structural consequence is to keep at least one read-out entirely out of the training loop**; the paper's own observation that flagging trajectories and patching environments already applies faint evolutionary pressure is the minimal form of this warning. Coreference `arxiv-2608.28859` (a steering layer that is not the best read-out layer) and `arxiv-2512.11949` (the obfuscation-pressure half implemented).
- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 356): **"The trace is a sufficient statistic for the behaviour" is the usable criterion, and its negation has three distinct causes that a single accuracy number merges: insufficient information (unfaithful), information present but invisible to this reader (illegible), and information present and actively misleading (obfuscating — the monitor is worse than a coin flip, which is the only failure mode that is qualitatively worse than reading nothing).** The practical value of separating them is diagnostic rather than philosophical: a second reader that succeeds on the same latent proves the information is there, which converts a failed read-out from a claim about the model into a claim about the instrument, and a read-out that stays *legible* while its accuracy decays under pressure is the tell for the third case. Beside this sits a definitional result worth citing whenever a probe is validated by perturbation: a test that edits the input and watches the answer measures self-consistency, and self-consistency is necessary but not sufficient for faithfulness, so strong steerability is evidence *for* faithfulness while the absence of steerability is not evidence against it — the asymmetry we should state, because the folder's probe results are routinely reported as if the converse held. Coreference `arxiv-2606.13603` (corrupting the prefix to price the tail) and `arxiv-2507.05246` (necessity graded by how much work the trace has to do).
