- Done 2026-11-17 (entry 286): `arxiv-2611.11398` — Decomposing Earth Embeddings with Sparse Autoencoders (Vitus Benson, Fanny Yang, Markus Reichstein — EarthNet / Horizon Europe WeatherGenerator group; arXiv:2611.11398v1, cs.LG/cs.CV-style Earth observation, 2026-11-08, NeurIPS 2026). Full text via HTML (~164K clean chars, §§1–4 + references + Appendices A–G, read end to end including every supplementary table). **Substance:** first SAE application to per-pixel Earth embeddings — AlphaEarth (D=64) and Tessera (D=128), 210,000 patches of 64×64 pixels from a 5 km global grid, split 100K/10K/100K, three SAE variants (ReLU+ℓ1, BatchTopK, Matryoshka BatchTopK) at width 1024 and k ∈ {8,16,32}, three seeds per cell (90 SAE runs + 18 frozen-decoder runs, 73 GPU-hours), all scored on fixed identical pixel samples; a three-criterion protocol (reconstruction at matched sparsity; spatial scale via a normalised semivariance curve and its correlation length plus within-patch variance share; concept alignment via a folded AUROC ≥ 0.65 against 20 concept groups drawn from 14 categorical and 3 continuous reference maps) with raw dimensions, PCA/ICA/NMF and a **frozen-random-decoder SAE** as baselines; then two applications (sub-concept discovery with a size-matched spatially-compact random-partition null, and an area-of-applicability estimate built on the sparse code's distance to the 5 nearest training pixels, scored against one common head over 88 graded hold-outs per target). **Results:** reconstruction separates trained from random (FVE 0.973 vs 0.775 AlphaEarth, 0.919 vs 0.534 Tessera at ~16 features; 2.7% vs 22% unexplained) and a fixed-PCA-basis top-k rule closes 67%/50% of the gap to BatchTopK, so about half to two-thirds of the edge over rank-k PCA is per-pixel selection; monosemy does not (88% of features aligned with ≤1 group, 89% for the frozen decoder, which has more strictly aligned features, 234 vs 136), nor does spatial scale (median correlation length 20–33 km vs 1,240 km for a raw dimension; 23–32% vs 9% of variance within a patch; frozen decoder 23 km) — the paper attributes this to activation arithmetic (16 of 1024 active ⇒ ~1.6% pixel support) rather than to learned atoms; the six highest-energy features carry 40% of code energy and are regional discretised pieces of the leading principal components (cosine 0.51–0.79, r = 0.69–0.83); sub-concept discovery separates three woody-vegetation features onto tropical / semi-arid / boreal strata (80%, 39%, 91% of top patches; lifts 15.6, 6.3, 8.0 against maps) yet the strict null cannot distinguish the partition (family-wise p = 0.14, 0.31); applicability gains for canopy height (77/88 hold-outs, +0.17; 75/88, +0.21) and not for elevation (41/88, 0.00; 49/88, +0.02), and on AlphaEarth an untrained random sparse code gains as much (75/88, +0.19).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 286): **Run every dictionary-quality score against a frozen random dictionary before believing it, because sparsity alone manufactures most of what the score looks like it is measuring: at 16 active features out of 1024, a feature is on for ~1.6% of inputs, so it can only clear a membership threshold if it is concentrated on one class — which is why 89% of a never-trained dictionary's features are 'monospecific' against 88% for the trained one, and why median correlation length (23 km vs 20–33 km) and Moran's I cannot tell them apart either.** Only reconstruction separates them (2.7% vs 22% of variance left unexplained), which means "our features are specific" and "our features vary at the right scale" are claims about the code's sparsity budget, not about the dictionary, and a report that omits the control is reporting an artefact of its own regularisation. For our battery the rule is direct: any per-feature statistic we publish — selectivity, monosemy, autocorrelation, variance share — gets the same statistic computed for a random-atom dictionary at the same width and sparsity beside it, and only the gap is a result. Coreference arxiv-2611.05655 (when two latents are the same feature) and arxiv-2611.09196 (the reading of a neuron as a measurement).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 286): **A downstream win from a sparse decomposition needs a second control, an untrained random sparse code of the same width and sparsity, because it separates 'a better space to measure distance in' from 'features that mean something' — here the best-looking application, ranking canopy-height errors by distance in the code, is fully reproduced by the random code on AlphaEarth (75/88 hold-outs, +0.19 against the trained SAE's +0.17) and about a third reproduced on Tessera, so the gain belongs to sparsity combined with the head's weights concentrating the distance, not to anything the dictionary learned.** Two habits follow. First, any read-out we wire into a decision — an OOD score, an applicability estimate, a monitor threshold — should be re-run with the interpretable component replaced by a random one of equal capacity, and if it survives, we have learned something about geometry rather than about the model, which is a perfectly good result but a different one. Second, the paper's own diagnosis of why the win is target-specific is the reusable part: targets tied to discrete landscape types are marked by a few sparse features, targets varying continuously within every type are spread over many dimensions and no sparse code can make them separable — a pre-check we can run by asking whether the head's weight mass sits on a few features. Coreference arxiv-2611.06688 (a subspace signal that must beat a detector-agnostic baseline) and arxiv-2611.10297 (the out-of-family scorer that turns a probe number into a claim).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 286): **A concentration statistic is not evidence of structure when the reference map is spatially smooth: the SAE's three woody-vegetation features sit on tropical-rainforest, semi-arid and boreal strata with lifts of 15.6, 6.3 and 8.0, and yet 50 size-matched spatially compact random partitions of the same forest patches agree with the same maps just as well (family-wise p = 0.14 and 0.31) — and the frozen decoder's features are even more concentrated (99/98/99% of top patches in one climate pair) while covering only part of each stratum.** The general lesson for our evaluations: any explanation scored against an autocorrelated or smooth reference — a geography, a topic, a sequence position, a template — must be compared with a size-matched structureless partition of the same items, because compactness alone reproduces smoothness; and where two artifacts differ in the same direction, the discriminating measurement is *coverage* of the stratum rather than concentration inside it, which is the metric the authors say they would need next. This is the same failure the folder met in the co-occurrence-prior and shared-stimulus entries, in its cleanest form. Coreference arxiv-2611.10297 (205 images reusing 28 reports) and arxiv-2611.19889 (a ranking that describes the checkpoint).

- Done 2026-11-17 (entry 285): `arxiv-2611.21159` — When Feature Representation Changes Local Explanations: A Controlled Comparison of SHAP and LIME under Numerical Discretization (Parv Patel — Indian Institute of Technology Palakkad; arXiv:2611.21159v1, cs.LG, 2026-11-16). Full text via HTML (~67K clean chars, §§1–7 + references, read end to end). **Substance:** a frozen 200-tree random forest on UCI Adult (32,561/16,281 rows, held-out ROC-AUC 0.9138, weights hashed and re-checked after every explanation) with the `age` column collapsed onto equidistant or quantile bin representatives at three bin counts; the same 120 stratified held-out instances explained in all six conditions plus the unchanged baseline, with each explainer's seed keyed to (repeat, instance) and not to condition so baseline and treatment share random draws; 3,240 KernelSHAP and 5,400 LIME explanations (plus 3,240 sensitivity). Each explainer is first compared **against itself** across seeds to build a seed-noise floor. An analytic argument — confirmed numerically to machine precision — shows KernelSHAP on a quantizing wrapper is exactly the unchanged model explained at a quantized instance against a quantized background, so the comparison is between two effective inputs; no such identity holds for LIME, whose perturbations are drawn in raw coordinates. Prediction-side coupling (class flip, probability change, held-out AUC) joined per instance onto every attribution row; LIME's internal discretisation disabled for the main run because the library default would apply the treatment to the control. **Results:** seed-noise medians 0.000327 KernelSHAP against 0.002233 LIME (6.8× raw, 5.1× normalised; repeat-to-repeat Spearman 0.997 against 0.944); age attribution exceeds its own floor in **6/6** conditions for KernelSHAP (median ratios 2.4–59, all Holm-significant, effect sizes +0.70 to +1.00) and in **2/6** for LIME on the raw scale (indistinguishable at one quantile setting, significantly *below* its own run-to-run variation in three others); SHAP's normalised response 3.0–14.1× LIME's in every condition with LIME 2.5–4.6× less consistent; class flips 0.8–5.8%, AUC ≥0.9097, while 45–94% of instances show a large SHAP change with no flip and ρ(Δp, Δattribution) is 0.42–0.76 for SHAP against ~0.10 for LIME; ranking never moves (median Spearman ≥0.979, top-k overlap 1.00, age's own rank shifts by at least one position for 80% of instances under SHAP against 62% under LIME at the coarsest equi-width binning — those two percentages are the only ranking-shift figures quoted, because the per-condition rank-shift column is the one whose header symbol was dropped); LIME's median weighted local R² stays 0.543–0.545 across all conditions including the one where its attribution moved past its floor, and rises to 0.620 only when its own discretisation is switched back on; the retrain-on-discretized secondary experiment gives the same ordering at roughly twice the frozen-model magnitude (0.0199 against 0.0072).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 285): **Every stochastic readout needs a denominator, and the denominator is the same readout re-run on unchanged input: this paper's central result is not that discretisation moves SHAP (established before) but that its effect is 2.4–59 times the explainer's own sampling noise while LIME's is, at four of six settings, no larger than the difference two of its own runs produce — and that distinction is invisible without the floor.** The rule for our battery is direct and cheap, and it applies to every sampling-based quantity we compute: Skylark-style coalition attributions over input features, bootstrap probes, any SHAP/LIME summary we fit to a black-box model. Re-run on identical input with a different seed, publish the spread, and express every effect as a ratio to it. A study without this control would have reported all six LIME conditions as positive results; with it, four are smaller than noise. The companion arithmetic is that the floor itself is budget-dependent and must be recorded beside the effect, because a different number of coalitions or perturbations moves both terms. Coreference arxiv-2611.21348 (the damage score that has to be subtracted from a matched control) and arxiv-2611.10297 (the baseline that turns a probe number into a claim).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 285): **Magnitude instability and ranking instability are different objects, and the number most stability claims are made in — rank correlation — is the one that hides the effect: median Spearman never drops below 0.979 and top-3 overlap is 1.00 in every condition, while up to 94% of instances carry an attribution shift beyond the noise floor with no change in prediction.** Two consequences. First, a battery that reports "the top-k features are unchanged", or any ordering-preserved statistic, is reporting near-nothing about whether the explanation survived; the magnitude is where a reader's interpretation (how much did this feature matter, relative to that one) actually changes, and it must be published as a number with a floor beside it. Second, the paper's dissection of *why* the two diverge is the reusable part and it is a mathematical warning about our own summaries: Shapley values are constrained to sum to the output, so any change in output level is necessarily redistributed across features, which makes part of SHAP's responsiveness definitional rather than a sensitivity property — while a LIME coefficient is an unconstrained local slope that can stay put while the surrogate's intercept absorbs the shift, and the observed correlations (0.42–0.76 against ~0.10 with the change in predicted probability) are exactly what that account predicts. When we report an attribution we should say which of these two objects it is, because an additive-by-construction summary and a free local slope fail differently. Coreference arxiv-2611.15082 (the score that sums three things) and arxiv-2611.19889 (a ranking that describes the checkpoint rather than the mechanism).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 285): **A frozen model is not a frozen function, and the proof is one line of commuting operators: for KernelSHAP the quantizing wrapper is exactly the unchanged network explained at a quantized instance against a quantized background, verified to machine precision — so a "frozen-model" experiment about explanation sensitivity is really an experiment about a changed effective input, and for LIME the identity fails outright because its perturbations are drawn in raw coordinates.** This is the most transferable thing in the entry for a white-box project. Any claim of the form "the weights did not change, so the behaviour did not change" is the same error, and the correct form is to name the composed function being evaluated and the input it is evaluated at. Our battery already records an analogue (residual-norm band checks after ablation, mass-preserving knockouts instead of deletions), and this adds the complementary case where nothing about the network is touched but the input distribution is silently altered by a wrapper we wrote. The practical probe is a cheap equivalence check: run the two framings and confirm the difference is zero to machine precision, which the authors ship as a single verification script — a two-command audit that is worth copying for every wrapper we insert between a model and a measurement. Coreference arxiv-2611.21539 (the knockout that takes the network off distribution) and arxiv-2611.04112 (a pipeline edit that changes the answer without changing the encoder).

the original Block knockout on Qwen3-VL-8B was carried by off-distribution items (53% left the norm band, in-band drop 3.1); selectivity (true option's ref-attention minus distractor mean, and its ratio) is 10.36× on Syn but 1.88× on HP and 1.30× on SP for Qwen3-VL-8B, predicts probe correctness at AUC 0.48–0.70, rises when decoy markers are drawn at distractors' own correspondence sites, and sharpening the attention logits does not improve accuracy; targeted repair A lifts SP 0.430 → 0.712 (Qwen3-VL-8B, 1.68M params) and 0.354 → 0.605 (InternVL3.5-8B, 1.50M), query-only arms keep most of it (0.674 / 0.581), transfers to HP (0.934 / 0.837) and BLINK-SC/VC, and beats random-head (0.677 / 0.584) and attention-matched arms; the parameter-matched all-layer adapter is stronger (0.792 / 0.728), the value arm beats the query/key arm in Qwen (0.747), and the targeted InternVL3.5-8B arm costs 16 pts on synthetic matching where the all-layer arm costs almost none; selectivity orders SP accuracy almost perfectly across all trained arms (Spearman near 1 over 7 and 5 models, holding for the arms trained after the relation was observed); transplanting the all-layer adapter's image-2 attention rows recovers 30–50% of its gain (Qwen) and 22–43% (InternVL) against ≤10–15% for random sets, mostly via Upstream (base query/key weights on trained inputs), and restoring those rows removes only 10–25% — **sufficient, not necessary**, the paper's own pre-registered necessity summary is recorded as not supported, while the targeted arm A does meet necessity in both models when all query positions are restored. Read from: full text (HTML).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 284): **A decodable-but-unused signal and a present-but-uncompared signal are different failures with different remedies, and telling them apart requires an edit along the probe's own direction at the probe's own scale: here that edit moves ≤2 points while the model's own letter direction at the same site switches a third to nearly half of the answers.** The construct is the one our battery has been missing. Every probe result we record should come with a positive control at the same tensor and layer — some direction known to move the output — because without it "the model knows but does not say it" and "the probe is reading something the model never uses" are indistinguishable, and this paper shows both cases exist side by side in one model family with one probe architecture. It also shows the cheap way to close the argument: 20 magnitude-matched random subspaces as the null for the edit, and a calibrated output as the baseline for the gap, so the claim is not that the probe beats raw argmax but that it beats the best monotone rescoring of the model's own log-probabilities. Coreference arxiv-2611.18274 (when along the trajectory the intervention lands) and arxiv-2611.04112 (a readout correct while the answer is wrong, measured behaviourally).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 284): **The knockout you reach for first is the one that lies: removing a head set's attention mass took 47–53% of the edited items outside the base residual-norm band and, restricted to in-band items, the effect on Qwen3-VL-8B collapsed from 17.4 to 3.1 points — whereas redistributing the same mass dropped it 17–19 points with the drop intact in-band.** This is a reusable protocol, not a VLM detail: our ablation batteries should default to mass-preserving interventions (spread or permute rather than delete) whenever the site has a conserved quantity, always report the drop restricted to items the intervention left in distribution, and treat an effect that exists only off-distribution as an artefact of taking the network somewhere it never goes. The companion control is the matched-alternative ladder — layer-matched random, then attention-mass-matched, then parameter-matched — because each rung removes one confound and the paper's advantage over the comparison survives all three (an attention-matched head set that sends equally much cross-image attention does no better than a random one, so it is *what* the heads attend to, not how much). Coreference arxiv-2611.21486 (interventions on extracted structure carry their own bridge assumptions) and arxiv-2611.21529 (the student that learns the schedule).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 284): **Sufficiency and necessity come apart even when both are measured properly: a broad fine-tune routes 30–50% of its gain through exactly the heads a targeted repair names, and yet resetting those heads costs it only 10–25% of the gain, because the change it made is upstream of them (base query/key weights on better inputs recover as much as the full transplant).** For a predictive white-box model the consequence is that "this component carries the computation" and "this component is where the computation can be changed" are separate predictions, and a predictor trained on attribution shares cannot distinguish them. What makes the finding credible is the decomposition, not the headline: splitting the transplant into upstream and local halves localises *where* in the causal graph the broad repair acts, and the paper's honest reading — sufficient but redundant pathway — is a more useful object than a bottleneck would have been. It also hands us a nearly free diagnostic worth copying: a scalar computed from a fixed small head set (selectivity) that tracks accuracy across every trained variant with near-perfect rank correlation, needing no probe and no retraining, which is a template for a weight-independent summary of what a fine-tune changed. Coreference arxiv-2611.21307 (control without a donor once the frame is a coordinate system) and arxiv-2611.21596 (constrain where the difference must be preserved, not after the fact).

- Done 2026-11-17 (entry 283): `arxiv-2611.21096` — Inference Equivalence and Quotient Coding (Zibo Meng, Andrew C. M. Austin, Alin Achim — University of Bristol; arXiv:2611.21096v1, cs.AI, 2026-11-16). Full text via HTML (98,203 chars, §§1–5 + Appendices A–L). **Substance:** observations are modelled as produced by an acquisition operator under bounded error, so many states are compatible with any measurement; a claim is *valid* only if it holds at every compatible state, which is stronger than being true at the realised state, and under a closedness condition validity is exactly "no physically realisable falsifying measurement within tolerance" — a distance in measurement space rather than an existential search. For a claim family ordered by semantic specificity, the **Exact Inference Frontier** is the maximal valid claims, proven to be the unique smallest generating antichain whose downward closure recovers every valid claim; two compatibility sets are inference-equivalent when they support the same valid claims, the frontier induces a canonical quotient code, and among deterministic encoders with exact inference decoding that partition is **provably the coarsest** (every optimiser induces it up to relabelling), with optimality claimed for code cardinality only. For learned compatibility sets, errors are split into omitted states (which can make unjustified claims appear valid) and added states outside the task closure (which can retract valid ones), with inclusions, a necessary-and-sufficient exact-preservation criterion, and a sufficiency-only relaxation when the estimate is not a superset. **Results:** 5,760 historical Push-T observations with 13 claims — 73.85% ambiguous, 49.38% both ambiguous and supporting non-trivial valid claims, 56.39% with multiple incomparable maximal claims, true-but-unsupported rate **37.13%** (31.04/28.16/28.42% under geometry, mechanism and joint shifts), 12 distinct frontiers at one cardinality; frontier changed by spatial-visibility intervention in 40.1% of 4,320 comparisons while 718 pairs with different compatibility sets shared a frontier, and 1,556 positive-distance pairs below the stability threshold left frontiers unchanged; 145 compatibility sets → **31 quotient codes (78.62% fewer)**, direct/quotient/frontier-reconstruction agreeing on all 8,800 observations, cardinality-only decoder at **47.85%** exact-signature accuracy (41.12/59.50/36.25% OOD), task closure enlarging 129 of 145 sets with claims intact, 941 of 1,036 single-state deletions harmless and 95 fatal, 9→13 claims refining the quotient 13→31; prospective learners — exact inference recovery 92.00–96.00% / 93.88–94.50% / 92.81–93.75%, **89 cases of inexact set recovery with exact inference recovery** (14 retaining a non-trivial claim), closure-target the low-unsupported-risk / high-lost-risk corner (0.00115 vs 0.012404), corridor-asymmetric nondominated in two regimes and **dominated in joint-OOD**; HRSID — 1,913 candidate sets → **36 signatures** under seven claims, 3-NN at **87.31%** claim precision, 0.599 supported claims/image, 23.55% exact-signature recovery at 1,347 claims/method (+0.2064 over ridge, +0.2426 over prevalence), and in the nested-bank development experiment 9 of 22 claim-retaining anchors keep the claim in the expanded bank against 13 that lose it.
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 283): **The right output of a white-box reader may be a partition, not a representation, and this paper gives the optimality proof the folder has been assembling piecemeal: among deterministic encoders that can decode every valid task claim exactly, the frontier-induced quotient is the coarsest possible, up to renaming the code values.** Two consequences we should adopt. First, the compression is empirically enormous and not marginal — 1,913 SAR candidate sets are **36** distinct answers and 145 simulated sets are **31** — so a battery that reports a state estimate where it could report a claim-signature is reporting far more distinctions than any task can distinguish. Second, the provable statement is deliberately narrow and honest: cardinality only, with storage length, representation dimension and compute explicitly disclaimed, which is the form we should copy when we claim minimality of anything. The matching control is the one that makes the claim testable in our own setting — a decoder that sees only the *size* of the possibility set reaches **47.85%** exact-signature accuracy, so "our compression preserves the answer" is uninformative unless it is scored against cardinality, and the 47.85% figure exists precisely because the authors expected cardinality to be a weak baseline and found it was not entirely one. Coreference arxiv-2611.18163 (a sufficiency ceiling in the data rather than the method) and arxiv-2611.21307 (a declared answer space as the coordinate system).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 283): **Decodability, justification and truth are three different things, and the gap between truth and justification is large enough to measure: 37.13% of claims that hold at the generating state are unsupported by the observation, because another compatible state falsifies them.** This is the cleanest formalisation the folder has of a nagging intuition — every entry that reports a probe "reading" a state is reporting a fact about one interpretation, and a claim about a state is a claim that *all* surviving interpretations agree. The paper's mechanism for quantifying it is reusable without any model: enumerate the compatible set, score a claim by whether every member satisfies it, and report the fraction of true-but-unsupported claims beside the accuracy. The companion detail is the one that keeps the framing honest — a frontier can be *changed* by an intervention that does not change the underlying ambiguity (40.1% of 4,320 visibility comparisons) and can be *shared* by compatibility sets that differ physically (718 pairs), so neither set cardinality nor set identity is the unit; only the signature is. Coreference arxiv-2611.04112 (an internal readout correct while the answer is wrong) and arxiv-2611.21539 (the answer position decodable while the output says otherwise).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 283): **An asymmetric objective buys a position on a trade-off, not an escape from it, and the paper's own table says so: closure-target achieves the best unsupported-claim risk by an order of magnitude (0.00115) and the worst lost-valid-claim risk (0.012404), corridor weighting is nondominated in two OOD regimes and dominated in the third, and 89 observations have the wrong compatibility set with the right claims.** For our battery the rule is to publish the pair of risk numbers per regime and never a single accuracy, because the two failure directions have opposite remedies (a probe that over-includes invents structure and needs pruning; one that under-includes retracts real structure and needs widening) and a method tuned to one will look bad on the other by construction. The constructive finding is that these errors are not equal in consequence — exact inference recovery stays in the 92–96% band while set recovery varies much more, so an inexact reader inside the task closure loses nothing, which is the licence for using a noisy but cheap predictor instead of an exact one. Coreference arxiv-2609.35686 and arxiv-2611.19684.

- Done 2026-11-17 (entry 282): `arxiv-2611.05803` — Phonological Knowledge of Chinese Characters in Language Models (Xiaozhe Ji, Renfen Hu — Beijing Normal University; Hai Hu — The Hong Kong Polytechnic University; arXiv:2611.05803v1, cs.CL, 2026-11-04). Full text via HTML (~64K clean chars, §§1–7 + Appendices A–P). **Substance:** PinyinBench, 38,183 minimal pairs over 3,500 common characters plus a 3,500–7,000 frequency band, with seven homophone distractor conditions that isolate which of Mandarin's three syllable dimensions (initial, final, tone) matches and which differs, plus a feature-judgment task that names the dimension and a polyphone task; eighteen models behaviourally (fifteen Qwen base checkpoints spanning Qwen2.5/3/3.5, plus Qwen2.5-Omni-7B and DeepSeek-V4-Flash), then on 2,300 monophonic characters a layerwise PCA-32 logistic probe under four prompt templates with a shuffled-label selectivity control, then a minimal-pair mean-difference steering direction injected at the source character's position over 82 transitions at five sites with α swept to 10, scored as target-minus-source class mass, with a held-out-character test and a no-cue control. **Results:** behaviour — 56.3%–78.7% for Qwen2.5 base when all three dimensions differ, **51.1%–55.7% when only tone differs** (chance even at 32B), DeepSeek-V4 98.4% vs **72.7%**; polyphone invalid-reading rejection ~95% for the largest models but valid-reading selection at chance for all; frequency and DIMSIM distance near-orthogonal (r = −0.015), about −17 to −24 points and **+1.6 to +5.5** points per SD. Probing — tone strongly decodable at the input embedding with modest depth gains, initials and finals rising to deeper peaks; selectivity **0.482 tone** against **0.708/0.708**; peak macro-F1 0.258→0.736 (initials), 0.169→0.667 (finals), 0.487→0.695 (tone) across 0.5B–7B. Steering — mean peak advantage **0.52 initials / 0.40 finals / 0.16 tone** at the embedding, same ordering at every site, 76–85% of L8 risers held out from construction, explicit-tone prompt 0.16→0.25 and class mass 0.25→0.41, no-cue control negative on all three; Omni-7B probes better on every dimension **including tone** yet steers no better; all three dimensions **reverse sign at L24**.
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 282): **A probe's raw accuracy is not a ranking when the label inventories differ, and this paper's central claim is only visible in the corrected column: tone selectivity is 0.482 against 0.708 for both initials and finals, so the dimension that is easiest to read at the input embedding is also the one whose readout beats its own shuffled-label control by the least — and the raw macro-F1 (0.695 for tone against 0.736 for initials at peak) would have hidden that, because four classes are easy to fit.** Two habits for us. Always print the shuffled-label counterpart beside a probe score and never compare two probes over different class counts without it; and treat a *small* selectivity margin as a warning about the readout rather than a fact about the model, since a four-way label that a probe recovers at 0.695 is a probe that may be recovering the marginal. The same asymmetry recurs from the opposite side in this folder's steering entries, where the direction that decodes best often moves least, and the pair of columns is what makes the two readings distinguishable. Coreference arxiv-2611.10297 (probe AUC 0.789–0.813 against a CLIP baseline at 0.475) and arxiv-2611.21348 (the readout that survives a change the mechanism did not).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 282): **The dimension that is most readable is the least steerable and the least judged, and the paper's own design gives the confound a name: the property already decoded from the input embedding is the one whose direction does not move the output, while the properties that only emerge in deeper layers move easily — initials and finals start low and rise to deep peaks and steer at 0.52/0.40, tone is readable at L0 and steers at 0.16, and its class mass stays below a four-class baseline until an explicit-tone prompt is used.** For our battery this is a cheap prior worth recording and testing, not assuming: order candidate features by the layer at which a probe first crosses its shuffled-label control and expect the shallow ones to be the worst handles, because a feature that is already in the token's own embedding may be a property of the *input* rather than of the computation. The companion control is the one that saves the headline — removing the source character from the prompt turns every steering effect negative, so an effect that depends on the prompt naming its subject is riding the prompt, and any steering arm we report should include that no-cue version before the number is believed. Coreference arxiv-2611.21449 (where first-layer weight statistics read the data distribution, not the function) and arxiv-2611.18514 (a direction that carries the format as well as the concept).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 282): **Better decodability is not better controllability, and the paper has one model in both roles: Qwen2.5-Omni-7B probes above the text-only 7B on all three dimensions at both the embedding and its peak layer, tone included, and steers no better — its initial and final advantages are lower than the base model's — while staying the weakest on tone behaviourally. The three columns (behaviour, decodability, steerability) therefore have to be measured, not inferred from one another, and this paper is the folder's cleanest demonstration that one model can move up on the middle column and not on either end.** Two further details to carry. The reading is deliberately weak where the evidence is weak: only the text backbone is probed, so the gain is attributed to multimodal training as a whole rather than to audio, and the authors say so. And the dissociation is left unexplained rather than explained away — the offered possibility (recognising a character's tone is easier than comparing tone across two characters) is stated as untested, which is the form a paper should use when its own three-column table outruns its mechanism. Also worth keeping structurally: all three steering effects reverse sign at the deepest site tested, so a single-site result at layer 20 would have described a layer that is about to flip. Coreference arxiv-2611.21539 (seen but unsaid) and arxiv-2611.03862 (the same SAE-feature handle failing on one source and working on another).

Then a fixed diagnostic ladder: pair-grouped linear probes for worker, excavator and relation; an out-of-fold error taxonomy assigning each error to perception / relation / reasoning / decision; prompt-token ablation with a length-matched neutral-sentence control; head knockout over 784 heads plus cross-patching; residual-stream exchange at every layer; top-k SAEs at five sites; and a correction battery (direction probing and steering, a residualised head search with eight prespecified criteria and 200 random head groups, 101 single-neuron ablations, relation-gated subspace steering) scored against the threshold-calibration curve under nested pair-grouped CV. **Results:** both entities are recognised (worker AUROC 1.000 at the projector, excavator 0.999) and the relation is encoded (pair-grouped out-of-fold 0.824 Qwen / 0.913 InternVL, peak layer 21), the answer score moves the right way in 78.6% / 73.2% of pairs — and yet 74.1% / 100% of far images are called HAZARD (Qwen specificity 25.9%, accuracy 55.2%, score AUROC 0.681; InternVL sensitivity 100%, specificity 0%). The score splits into an offset b = 0.68 against a shift Δ = 0.62 (PDI 1.1, 0.9–1.4) for Qwen and 8.03 against 1.03 (PDI 7.8, 6.5–9.6) for InternVL; removing the worker drops Qwen from 76.1% to 11.0% HAZARD, adding a worker far from the machine adds C = 1.48 against a further R = 0.62 when it moves into the zone (ratio 2.4, far image above its own background in 94.4% of pairs), InternVL C = 3.26 / R = 1.03 (ratio 3.2), and for InternVL the worker-removed scene already scores 4.77 and is called HAZARD every time. On the balanced natural Rule-4 set co-occurrence is held constant and Qwen falls to 92.9% sensitivity / 11.4% specificity / **AUROC 0.557**, with frozen object probes transferring without loss (96.4% / 100%), a language-0 hazard proxy holding 0.793 and the frozen relation readout collapsing to **0.521**; 154 of 263 far false alarms (58.6%) occur with every internal signal correct. Localisation fails by its own criteria — top-8 head knockout moves the gap 0.061 (11%) with cross-patching no better than controls, the revised search meets 3/8 criteria in both models, no neuron of 101 passes, and the one apparent win (0.149 far specificity) pays 0.101 near sensitivity by lowering both margins and sits on the calibration curve. The single pass is **relation-gated subspace steering**: 0.36 → 0.58 far specificity at matched sensitivity 0.78, balanced accuracy 0.675 against a 0.648 threshold ceiling, 0.217 → 0.575 at α = 2 — with an external probe as the gate, and no InternVL dose changing anything against an eight-logit offset.
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 281): **"The model encodes X but does not use it" is not a diagnosis until the score is decomposed into the term that carries X and the term that overrides it, and the ratio of those two terms is what predicts the symptom: here b/Δ = 1.1 for Qwen means a third of the far set still clears the threshold, and b/Δ = 7.8 for InternVL means nothing does — the same qualitative failure, two different severities, one scalar.** The decomposition is only as good as the second term's definition, and the paper's is the reusable part: measure the increment from *adding* the entity versus the increment from *moving* it into the relation (C = 1.48 against R = 0.62), which needs no probe and no training, only a matched editing pipeline. For our battery this supplies the missing middle term between "a probe reads the state" and "the behaviour is wrong": whenever we report a readout that decodes a state the model ignores, the report should carry the size of the overriding evidence in the same units, because that number — not the readout's accuracy — is what says whether a correction is available at all and how large a dose it will need. Coreference arxiv-2611.18514 (a probe at 0.80 AUC whose steering half-works) and arxiv-2611.21348 (the readout that is intact while the behaviour is not).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 281): **Every intervention that lowers a score along the decision axis will look like a success unless it is plotted against threshold recalibration, and this paper catches its own result that way: a head search gained 0.149 far specificity at a cost of 0.101 near sensitivity — because it lowered near and far margins almost equally (-0.70 and -0.64) — and its operating point lay exactly on the calibration curve.** The diagnostic is arithmetic and free: an intervention that shifts the *offset* lands on the curve, an intervention that changes the *slope* lies above it, and the (Sp, Se) plane makes the difference visible at a glance. Two habits follow. Report the entire calibration curve beside every intervention point, and treat "above the curve at matched sensitivity" as the only admissible success criterion — with the further check the paper adds for its one survivor, that balanced accuracy beat the best achievable by any threshold (0.675 against 0.648), so the gain cannot be read as a re-weighting of the same trade-off. And when an intervention does clear the curve, name what it was conditioned on: here the gate is an external probe over the model's own states, so the reported gain belongs to a hybrid system and not to a direction pushed into the forward pass. Coreference arxiv-2611.06001 (steering priced against a capability budget) and arxiv-2611.17620 (the side effects at the coefficients that "work").
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 281): **A readout fitted in a controlled domain can be excellent there and worthless where it is meant to be deployed, and the gap is the finding: the pair-grouped relation probe reaches AUROC 0.824 on edited pairs and 0.521 on natural Rule-4 photographs, while the object probes transfer without loss (96.4% worker, 100% excavator) and a shallow scene-level hazard proxy holds 0.793.** The asymmetry has a mechanism worth remembering — the *cause of the error* is coarse and therefore robust (does this scene look like a construction hazard?), while the *evidence that would correct it* is fine and therefore fragile (a single upright cleanly segmented worker on one ground band) — so domain-specificity is not uniform across a model's features and a battery built in one distribution transfers unequally by design. There is a matching eval lesson on the behaviour side: the same Qwen model that scores 93% sensitivity on the balanced natural set scores 11.4% specificity and AUROC 0.557, because a co-occurrence prior fires on every image that contains both entities, and a mixed benchmark in which many safe images lack one of the entities would have hidden the failure entirely. Coreference arxiv-2611.21348 (a frozen read-out going stale under training drift) and arxiv-2611.18163 (a ceiling that lives in the data rather than in the method).

- Done 2026-11-17 (entry 280): `arxiv-2611.12206` — A Geometric Invariant of Attention Predicts Head Specialization from Weights Alone (Miguel P. Bento, single author — Feedzai, Lisbon; arXiv:2611.12206v1, cs.LG, 2026-11-09, CC BY 4.0; NeurReps workshop extended abstract, NeurIPS 2026). Full text via HTML (~12K clean chars, §§1–4 + both tables + references, read end to end). **Substance:** the attention logit is split into a static content term and a RoPE-induced positional perturbation; a scalar **rho** is defined as the size of the position-dependent term relative to the content term, aggregated over logarithmically spaced relative offsets so the geometrically spaced frequency bands are all probed up to a context horizon. Basis-independence is argued from the residual symmetry of the RoPE block-diagonal rotation (one rotation per frequency plane, leaving the trace-like quantity of the query–key form fixed), and Proposition 1 shows rho = 0 iff the perturbation vanishes at every sampled offset, giving position-independent logits for **every** input. Empirically rho is rank-correlated with induction score (repeated random sequences) across all heads in **SmolLM2-135M, TinyLlama-1.1B, SmolLM2-1.7B, Mistral-7B**, then used to gate YaRN to the top-50% rho heads on Mistral-7B. **Results:** Spearman **−0.55 to −0.74** in every model (all p < 1e-40) and the ten strongest induction heads always in the low-rho tail — bottom **14% / 7% / 17% / 30%** respectively; targeted YaRN short-context perplexity **12.92** against **19.37** uniform and **7.63** baseline, long-context **130.34** against **162.96** and 5.44, all within the native window and inflated by proximity to the context limit. Author reads the residual correlation as expected because induction is multi-head, so low rho is necessary but not sufficient.
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 280): **A weight-only invariant and a probe accuracy are different kinds of claim, and the difference is a ceiling: rho = 0 forbids positional dependence for *every* input, which is a statement no behavioural measurement can make, while a probe at 0.8 AUC describes one dataset.** The construction is reusable as a template for our own read-offs: find the symmetry group the architecture leaves free, compute a quantity that is fixed under it, and derive what the quantity *cannot* be — then the observable costs no inference and can be checked against any battery for free. The paper's own honesty about direction is the part to copy — it claims only necessary-not-sufficient, and reports the correlation as a population statistic plus a rank-percentile statement about the top ten heads rather than a single accuracy — because that is exactly the format that survives a follow-up finding a counterexample. Coreference arxiv-2611.21449 (a weight reader whose top tier is really reading the input-layer statistics) and arxiv-2611.20441 (locating a component is not explaining it).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 280): **When a scalar ranks components by what they can respond to, the cheapest downstream use is to spend the intervention only on the ones that can respond — and the gain is visible against both baselines, not just the naive one: gating YaRN to the top half of heads by rho gives 12.92 short-context perplexity against 19.37 for uniform application and 7.63 untouched, and 130.34 against 162.96 long.** Two habits for us. Every intervention we ship should be reported against **both** the untouched model and the uniformly-applied version, because "better than doing it everywhere" is a much weaker claim than "better than not doing it" and the two answer different questions — the first is a claim about targeting, the second about whether the intervention works. And a capacity score that predicts where an intervention helps is a *third* use of the same quantity beyond explaining and predicting, which is a good sign the quantity is real rather than a curve fit. The caveat is the sample: one model, one intervention, one context window, no shuffled-weight control — a proof of concept the author labels as one. Coreference arxiv-2611.06001 (the capability budget as the same "cost of intervening" arithmetic) and arxiv-2611.18274 (steering as allocation under a fixed budget).

Eldagla — German International University in Cairo; Zeyad H. ElShafei — Arab Academy for Science, Technology and Maritime Transport; Ahmed M. Anter — Egypt-Japan University of Science and Technology; arXiv:2611.10297v1, cs.CV, 2026-11-06, arXiv perpetual non-exclusive licence; NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on Medical Reasoning with Vision Language Foundation Models). Full text via HTML (21,468 clean chars, §§1-8 + references, read end to end). **Substance:** four instruction-tuned VLMs (LLaVA-1.5-7B/13B, Qwen2-VL-7B, InternVL2-8B) on Indiana University chest X-rays in four conditions — matched 738, normal image with abnormal report 116, abnormal image with normal report 622, abnormal image with most-similar normal report 205 — answering a three-way template (SUPPORTS/CONTRADICTS/INCONCLUSIVE) parsed by a first-verdict rule built to stop negated hedges counting as contradictions, greedy decoding at a fixed seed. Then the diagnostic: a last-token penultimate-layer logistic probe against a biomedical CLIP image-text similarity baseline, a mean-difference conflict direction in the upper layers added to the residual stream at six strengths with matched pairs as a false-positive control, visual-token patching with a no-op control, a forced-choice rerun with the hedge option deleted, and cross-modal attention to image tokens beside output entropy. **Results:** contradiction is 0% in essentially every cell (2 of 941 InternVL2-8B outputs, 0.2%) while hedging rises with difficulty (INCONCLUSIVE 7.0% → 26.3% InternVL2-8B, 14.0% → 50.7% Qwen2-VL) and the LLaVA pair simply miss the template on 20.5-94.1% of outputs; probe AUC 0.789-0.813 across the four models, InternVL2-8B's regularised larger-sample rerun 0.781 with bootstrap interval 0.726-0.806 and permutation p = 0.002, against CLIP cosine AUC 0.475; steering leaves the verdict distribution untouched at every strength (~88%/11%) and only removes negated hedges (13.3% → 0%), matched-pair control 0%; forced choice returns 8.0% and 10.0% against a 10.0% matched baseline, and the 31.0% on the fourth condition is a retrieval artefact traced to 205 images sharing 28 reports with one hallucinated nodule report producing 29 of the 31 contradictions; attention to image tokens drops on mismatched pairs (AUC 0.376, p < 2e-5) where entropy does not (0.517, p = 0.57), and patching peaks at layer 20 (ΔP ≈ −0.011/+0.017) and vanishes by layer 30 with an exact zero no-op.
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 279): **An internal signal present where the behaviour is absent is not evidence of concealment, and the reading it invites can invert the remedy: here the conflict direction amplified at six strengths moves contradiction by nothing at all (0% throughout) and deleting the hedge option returns contradiction at or below the matched baseline, so the intervention that the "mask" framing would prescribe — force the answer out — provably has nothing to extract, and the remedy the evidence does support is re-grounding and uncertainty surfacing.** The design lesson is to write the rival hypotheses down first and give each a prediction the intervention can falsify, which costs one steering sweep and one option-deletion rerun on data we already have; the "nothing changes" outcome is then a result rather than the absence of one, because concealment predicted a rise and got none. This lands directly on our own battery: whenever a probe reads a state the model does not act on, the honest report carries both readings and the arm that distinguishes them, since a monitor built on the concealment reading would be pointed at the wrong target and, worse, would score well while doing it. Coreference arxiv-2611.19684 (a reader at chance on ranking while selection still helps), arxiv-2611.20371 (decoding is not a causal claim) and arxiv-2611.15082 (the score that sums three things).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 279): **The readout of an internal state can be flat at chance while a different readout of the same state is not, and the choice of readout is the finding: output entropy separates mismatched from matched pairs at AUC 0.517 (p = 0.57) while cross-modal attention mass over image tokens separates them at 0.376 in the same direction (p < 2e-5), and the mechanism the attention result suggests — the text looking away from the evidence — is corroborated, weakly, by patching visual tokens peaking at layer 20 and vanishing by layer 30.** Two habits for us. When a state is claimed to be present, the report should name *which* observable carries it and print at least one competing observable that does not, because "the model is uncertain here" is not a claim until a specific quantity moves; and a null on one readout is a claim about that readout, never about the representation, which is the same asymmetry the folder keeps meeting between probe accuracy and probe direction. The layer profile is worth carrying too — a small mid-stack effect that is gone by the last layer reads as gating rather than as a stored verdict, which is the difference between a fact the model holds and a gate it applies. Coreference arxiv-2611.21348 (reconstruction recovered, concentration not) and arxiv-2611.18514 (locating is not explaining).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 279): **The cheapest non-triviality control in the folder costs one extra model and it is the one that converts a probe number into a claim: the same image-text pairs through a biomedical CLIP similarity model return AUC 0.475, so the 0.789-0.813 probe is not recovering surface similarity — and the same discipline catches the paper's own best-looking cell, where a 31.0% contradiction rate dissolves into 205 images reusing only 28 distinct reports, 66 of 100 samples paired with one hallucinated nodule report, and 29 of the 31 verdicts coming from it (5.9% for all others).** Both halves are the same lesson from opposite ends: an external baseline and an item-level audit are what stand between a metric and a story. For our tables this suggests two standing columns we can compute with no new inference — a non-neural or out-of-family scorer on the identical items, and a **distinct-stimulus count beside every n**, because a dataset of 205 examples with 28 distinct documents has an effective size of 28 and a per-example rate computed on it is a statement about a handful of stimuli. Coreference arxiv-2611.19889 (the ranking that describes the checkpoint) and arxiv-2611.15082 (the trivial-rule floor per stratum).

Full text via HTML (91,675 clean chars, §§1–6 + Appendices A–L). **Substance:** Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct (28 layers) driving live Online-Mind2Web sites with a supplied action list, 300 episodes / 2,071 actions / **32.6% hallucinated** (selector absent from the list); then single-component attribution (per-layer FFN amplification ×10, per-head Gaussian noise), joint head-scaling × FFN-dampening interventions swept over a large configuration table, Gaussian-noise activation patching over three input spans with residual/attention/FFN restoration, linear probes at all 28 layers at three positions on an episode-level 70/15/15 split (1,433/282/356), steering with normalised probe weights over a coefficient sweep, a JSON→numbered-markdown format swap as the out-of-distribution test, logit lens, and a pretrained 131,072-feature BatchTopK SAE read at layer 27 at the selector-value position on a single A100. **Results:** prompt_end probe **0.80 AUC at layer 18 before any output token**; selector_start layer-17 steering **85.4% fix / 7.0% break** at its best coefficient, collapsing to 48.8/30.2 one step larger and 0.0/96.9 at the largest, and to **58.1/7.0** on the reformatted list (a **27-point** loss); best joint circuit intervention **8.9% fix / 2.4% break** with every high-fix configuration breaking nearly everything (L25H23 + L20×10: 0.19% fix / 100% break); patching gives action-list corruption 0.325 mean mass against 0.682/0.672 and **0.360** recovered by clean residual at L27 versus 0.075 attention and 0.067 FFN; remove-the-chosen-action counterfactuals hallucinate in **38%** of cases and diverge to ~25% selector agreement and 0.52 DOM Jaccard after one step; the top SAE features discriminating the classes promote unrelated tokens; logit lens converges hallucinating trials on Search/Enter/Find/Explore by layers 21–27. Six-item roadmap: agentic MI benchmarks, attribution beyond single position/component, counterfactuals in stateful environments, feature discovery on interaction distributions, belief monitoring across timesteps, universality across agent types.
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 278): **A steering result is a curve, not a number, and the curve here has a cliff inside one coefficient step: the same probe vector at selector-start layer 17 fixes 85.4% of hallucinations while breaking 7.0% of valid actions at its best setting, fixes 48.8% while breaking 30.2% one step larger, and fixes nothing at all while breaking 96.9% at the top of the sweep.** The paper reports the whole grid (Table 5, every position × layer × α) and that is what makes the headline readable — a write-up quoting only the peak would have described a usable controller with no usable range. For our battery this fixes a reporting convention we have been circling: every steering arm gets a **(fix, break) pair at every coefficient**, the peak reported as a point on that curve with its neighbours, and the *range* of coefficients over which the pair stays favourable. The companion arithmetic is that fix and break are not independent — at high α the intervention is not steering the behaviour, it is destroying the format, so a 96.9% break rate is a statement about degradation and not about the concept. Coreference arxiv-2611.06001 (the capability budget as the same trade-off priced from the other side) and arxiv-2611.17620 (the unclaimed behaviours at the same coefficients).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 278): **A probe that decodes the right thing at a position can be steering a design choice rather than the concept, and the tell is a syntactic change to the same information: the selector-start direction keeps its break rate exactly (7.0% in both conditions) while its fix rate falls 85.4% → 58.1% after the action list is reformatted from JSON to a numbered list, so the vector carries the hallucination signal *and* a format-locked component, and only the fix side loses.** That asymmetry is the diagnostic worth keeping — a probe whose break rate is stable while its fix rate collapses is entangled with what the prompt looks like, not with what the model is deciding — and it is cheaper than any ablation: one template rewrite, same tasks, same selectors, same vector, no retraining. It also explains the two probe failures as one: the same paper's probe AUC degrades on the reformatted data (Figure 6) and the pretrained SAE at layer 27 returns top features promoting unrelated tokens, both being the agentic distribution sitting outside whatever the artifact was fitted or trained on. For our loop this is the standing demand on any detector we ship: **report the fix and break rates under a format perturbation beside the in-distribution pair**, because that is the house-style version of the question "is this the concept or the wrapper". Coreference arxiv-2611.18514's own probe, arxiv-2611.21348 (a frozen read-out going stale) and arxiv-2611.20371 (the fit is not the mechanism).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 278): **Locating a causal input is not explaining it, and the gap is visible in the number: patching makes the action list the dominant span — corrupting it drops valid-token mass to 0.325 against 0.682 and 0.672 for the selector and the task description, and restoring clean residual states recovers 0.360 — yet nothing in that result says which property of the list caused the commitment, and about half the valid steps are unaffected by the corruption because the answer is also in the agent's own history.** Two things to carry. First, a span-level attribution should be reported with the *sample fraction it actually binds on*, since an intervention that changes half the cases is describing half a mechanism; stratifying by whether the value appears earlier in the context is the cheap version of that check and it turns a single recovery number into a conditional one. Second, when an intervention does name a component, the check that it reproduced the phenomenon rather than the label is qualitative, and here it fails: amplified FFNs and noised heads produce malformed selector strings like a ten-digit sentinel, whereas the model's natural failures are well-formed references to plausible elements that do not exist. A synthetic intervention that raises the metric has not reproduced the failure unless the *shape* of the output matches, and single-component attribution at 0.19–8.9% fix on this task suggests the honest verdict is "distributed, and not localizable to a head or an FFN". Coreference arxiv-2611.20441 (the direction is one layer's object, not the mechanism) and arxiv-2611.20371 (decoding is not a causal claim).

- Done 2026-11-17 (entry 276): `arxiv-2611.21348` — Representational Change Under Self-Consuming Training: A Sparse Autoencoder Analysis (Suchit Gupte, Zhongteng Cai, Xueru Zhang, Mohammad Mahdi Khalili — The Ohio State University; arXiv:2611.21348v1, cs.LG, 2026-11-16, CC BY 4.0). Full text via HTML (71,240 clean chars, §§1–8 + Appendices A–B in part). **Substance:** five generations of self-consuming training (each generation trained one epoch on 10,000 blocks of 512 tokens sampled from the previous generation itself, no real data mixed in) against a **matched real-data control** with identical token budget, optimiser and step count, on Pythia-160M (layer 8) and Gemma-2-2B (layers 5, 12, 19); every result is a **damage score** — synthetic minus generation-matched control, sign-corrected so positive is always worse and zero at generation 0 — which subtracts continued training by construction. The generation-0 SAE is evaluated **zero-shot** (frozen) and **fine-tuned** (re-adapted from its own initialisation, three seeds, never retrained from scratch), across a Pythia width sweep and three SAE architectures (BatchTopK, JumpReLU, Matryoshka-BatchTopK) and a Gemma depth sweep, on SAEBench core metrics, sparse probing with top-k versus full-latent versus a dimension-matched residual-stream baseline over 35 tasks from five datasets, and two causal ablations (spurious-correlation removal, targeted probe perturbation). A linear-autoencoder analysis supplies the frame: an optimal rank-r linear autoencoder recovers the top-r principal subspace, so a frozen dictionary is a fixed subspace whose extra reconstruction cost is bounded by the principal angles to the current subspace over the eigengap — while an orthogonal change of basis inside that subspace leaves reconstruction and any full-representation probe **exactly** invariant. **Results:** behaviour degrades (generation-5 perplexity ≈1.6× control on Pythia, ≈1.4× on Gemma, with the controls flat or improving); zero-shot dictionaries go stale progressively for every Pythia width and architecture, worst at the widest, and fine-tuning removes most of the reconstruction and explained-variance gap leaving only a small sparsity residual — so the shift is mostly *stale dictionary*, not damaged representation; the feature level then separates, with **top-k sparse-probing damage growing across generations and surviving fine-tuning on Pythia while the full-latent probe recovers**, i.e. the information persists but stops concentrating in a few latents; on Gemma the drift is strongly depth-dependent (early layer stable, late layer worst) and, after adaptation, the three feature-level metrics disagree — probing largely repaired, spurious-correlation removal retaining residual damage, targeted probe perturbation showing no consistent sign. **Limits:** two families, one training seed per lineage (error bars are SAE fine-tuning variance, not lineage variance), pure-synthetic with no realistic mixture, one Pythia layer and three Gemma layers, SAE adapted not retrained, Gemma trained in bfloat16 with a cautioned effective step size, depth dependence established but unexplained, and the rotation argument offered as a possibility rather than a prediction.
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 277): **Interpretability drift under continued training splits into two parts that must be reported apart, and the split is measured, not assumed: a frozen dictionary sent stale by a rotated reconstruction subspace is repaired by adaptation, while whatever remains after adaptation is the part the representation actually lost — here adaptation removes most of the reconstruction and explained-variance gap everywhere, and what survives is specifically the information's concentration, not its availability.** The analytic backbone is worth keeping because it is cheap: a linear autoencoder recovers a principal subspace, so a frozen read-out is a fixed subspace, its cost is bounded by the angle between that subspace and the current one over the eigengap, and any *isotropic* change of variance costs nothing at all — only rotation of the reconstruction-relevant subspace does. For our battery this becomes a two-column convention whenever a model is fine-tuned under a read-out we already trust: **refit and re-measure**. A probe that degrades and recovers on refit was stale (a fact about our artifact); a probe that degrades and stays degraded is reporting a change in the model. The paper also supplies the honest caveat for the first column, since a small residual reconstruction gap does *not* mean the representation is unchanged — it means the adapted subspace captured it. Coreference arxiv-2611.20371 (the fit and the direction are not the same object) and arxiv-2611.21307 (the readout must match the model's distribution, not the labels).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 277): **Reconstruction faithfulness is a constraint on a subspace and says nothing about the coordinates inside it, so the readouts that rot first when a model moves are exactly the sparse ones — the full-latent probe is provably invariant to an orthogonal change of basis while the same information, once rotated, no longer sits in a few latents, and that is the observed pattern (top-k damage grows and survives adaptation, full-latent damage does not).** Two habits follow. Report a **top-k sparse-probe column beside every full-representation column** wherever we make a single-feature or few-feature claim, because the gap between the two is the only cheap detector of redistribution; and treat "reconstruction recovered" and "the feature still exists" as unrelated statements, since our own dictionary entries and single-latent explanations are top-k claims by construction. The same structure explains a residual risk in our eval suites: a pooled or full-space probe will keep scoring well while every per-feature claim it was supposed to license has quietly scrambled, which is the interpretability version of a metric that survives a change the mechanism did not. Coreference arxiv-2609.35686 (probing and intervention dissociate) and arxiv-2611.19684 (the metric that is fixed while the behaviour is not).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 277): **A trend is bet on its control arm, and this paper's control is the reusable part: the same model, the same token budget, the same optimiser and the same number of generations, trained on fresh real data instead of its own output — which turns "the model got worse" into "the recursion, and not the extra training, made it worse", and the authors spend their behavioural sanity check proving the control behaves (perplexity flat on Pythia, improving on Gemma).** For us this is the template for any claim of the form "this intervention/data/protocol changed the internals": a matched arm on ordinary training at equal budget, a sign-corrected damage score anchored at zero before the change, and a behavioural check that the manipulation actually bit. The paper also models the honesty its own error bars fail to buy — one training seed per lineage, so the reported spread is fine-tuning variance and cannot speak to lineage variance, which is exactly the number a reader would want for a five-generation trend; the lesson to carry is that a reported error bar names which source of variation it covers, and ours should too. Coreference arxiv-2611.17620 (the arm everyone compares against is the wrong one) and arxiv-2611.20441 (state the pair count and the construction).

- **Selection: the folder's first entry that grades an explanation by which *tier* it reaches — where an object is, what an action does, and what makes a model misbehave — and shows the first nearly solved while the other two are at chance, with a checkable decompilation as the top of the ladder.** This was **run 275's strongest runner-up, now taken**, since its slot (a replication-shaped weight-reading entry with a shallow-auditing result) was exactly this paper's shape. - Done 2026-11-17 (entry 275): `arxiv-2611.21449` — Replicating and Extending Weight-Space Programming: Frontier LLMs Compile Programs into Weights and Read Input Layers (Roksana Goworek, Alexander Hickey, Federico Nanni, Martin O'Reilly — The Alan Turing Institute; arXiv:2611.21449v1, cs.CL, 2026-11-16, CC BY 4.0). Full text via HTML (52,751 clean chars, §§1–7 + references). **Substance:** a three-day replication of the claim that a frontier model can emit a small network's weights in one reply and can name what a trained network does from raw weights. Instrument is the **code-versus-weights pair** (same prompt, ask for a Python program or for weights, no tools); novelty controls are two Breakout variants that cannot be in any corpus plus three in-house-trained games (asteroid descent, Whac-A-Mole, row-locked shooter); reading is tested as naming against shuffled weights, as mechanism recovery on networks the authors trained, and as **decompilation** — two isolated agents given weights, architecture and rules but forbidden to execute the network, whose Python is then verified on every enumerable state; auditing is plain-text weight files with no Python and no forward passes on paired Olmo 3 190M models (one poisoned during training, one by later fine-tuning) and Qwen3.5-0.8B LoRA adapter pairs; tokeniser identity across generations is used as a clue about pretrain versus post-training. **Results:** writing reproduces (Breakout 514/550/307 against 517; 515 average on both unseen variants where the standard network scores 0.5 and 0.0); the gap is generation-by-generation — by July 2026 a 580 Breakout program against networks averaging 30.9, Astra's September networks keeping half to two-thirds of its program scores (695.7 code vs 456.9 weights); written networks are sparse and saturated (4%/6% of weights set, magnitudes in the hundreds) while PPO networks set nearly all weights at a median 0.08; two independent decompilations match Astra's network in **all 49,189 enumerated states** and over 1,000 games, and also match the flawed networks of weaker writers; on MNIST, with no program to compile, Astra averages **49.6%** against an **82.0%** mean-image template and 96.7% trained, with a rotated-digit control scoring the same 49.4%; reading reproduces for naming (12/12, chance under shuffling) but is mostly the **input layer** — first-layer weight norms are a heat map a human can draw in a few lines of NumPy, and on the three in-house games Astra always recovered the layout while consistently missing the mechanics and falling back on a familiar name; audits: 10/10 on the pretraining-poisoned model, 7/10 on the fine-tuned one (not above chance), 23/32 on malicious persona adapters, 13/32 and 17/32 on backdoored adapters (chance), and **no run in 64 evaluations** named the trigger or described the behaviour; Qwen3.8-27B reaches 23/28 on the easiest poison task and chance elsewhere.
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 276): **An explanation has a ladder, and the tiers are not correlated: naming which game a network plays is solved (12 of 12, chance under shuffling), recovering where objects sit is solved on networks the reader cannot have seen (three in-house games, layout in every run), knowing what an action does is not (the whack action read as one the agent avoids, the shooter's up/down read as catching), and naming the trigger of a poisoned model happens in 0 of 64 evaluations.** The reason the tiers separate is mechanical: as the authors note, first-layer weight norms are close to a record of where each input channel's objects appeared during training, an undertrained network's six used holes show up as exactly six, and a heat map a human can draw with a few lines of NumPy recovers the same thing — so tier one is a property of the *data distribution*, not of the function. This is the same confound the folder keeps meeting from the probe side (a readout that recovers topic rather than the target), now in weights, and it makes a demand on our own reports: when a white-box model "explains" a behaviour by locating input structure, that is tier one, and it must be labelled as such, because it is cheap, human-reproducible and carries no claim about what the network does. The practical corollary is that tier three is where any safety use of interpretability lives, and it is the tier that is at chance here even while tier one is perfect. (arxiv-2611.21449, arxiv-2611.18163, arxiv-2611.20441)
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 276): **Decompilation is the strongest cheap completeness check the folder has: give two independent readers the weights, the architecture and the rules, forbid executing the network or simulating the environment, and then verify the recovered program on every state you can enumerate — here both readers matched in all 49,189 tested states and over 1,000 games, and the two independent programs agreed with each other and with the writer's own design notes.** Three features make it usable rather than decorative. The ban on execution is what forces the reader to use the weights rather than the behaviour, so a match is evidence about the mechanism and not about a search. The verification is exhaustive on a finite input space, so it is a proof on that space rather than a faithfulness score. And it applies to networks nobody wrote, including bad ones — decompiled programs for networks scoring 336, 14 and 1 matched them "flaws included", which is the form of a check that can fail and did not. For our battery this is a ready-made evaluation for any small mechanism claim: if a probe, a circuit or a surrogate is offered as *the* computation, write it as a program, have two independent readers derive it from weights alone, and report the fraction of the input space on which the two programs and the network agree. The caveat to carry is that it worked here because the weights were sparse and near-binary (4–6% set, magnitudes up to 1,000); on PPO weights, where nearly all entries are set at a median 0.08, the same check has not been shown to work, so the method is a test for compiled mechanisms, not for learned ones. (arxiv-2611.21449, arxiv-2611.21486, arxiv-2611.20371)
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 276): **The same capability can be far stronger as a program than as a representation for a generation, and the gap is diagnostic: Opus 5 scored 580 on Breakout as Python and averaged 30.9 as weights, GPT-5.6 Sol 301 against 14.6, and only Astra's generation kept half to two-thirds of its program score — while on MNIST, where there is no clean program to compile, written networks scored 49.6% against an 82.0% mean-image baseline.** Two things to take. First, the code-versus-weights pair is a cheap and general instrument for locating *where* a capability lives: ask for the same behaviour in two representations and the difference says whether the model lacks the knowledge or lacks the encoding, which is the same question we ask when a probe decodes but does not steer. Second, the MNIST result is the boundary condition worth remembering — the ability is compilation of a near-symbolic rule (grid in, a few if-then rules out) and it collapses on a task that has no such rule, so "a model can write working weights" is a claim about program-like tasks and not about learning. The audit arithmetic is the sting in the tail: 10 of 10 on a model poisoned from pretraining, 7 of 10 when the poison arrived as a little extra training on top of a clean checkpoint, because the compromised model then differs only by small changes spread over all weights — a reminder that detection difficulty tracks the *distance* between the two models, which is exactly the regime where a real backdoor would hide. (arxiv-2611.21449, arxiv-2611.21307, arxiv-2611.15082)
