- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 263): **A threshold is a separate object from the ranking behind it, and the folder now has the cleanest possible demonstration: one update moves a deployed guardrail's realised false-positive rate from 1.01% to 15.12% while AUROC falls 0.0058, so every official staleness criterion reads the probe as healthy and a deployer running a real system is flagging one prompt in seven.** The arithmetic reason is worth internalising, because it generalises to every monitor we ship: a 1% target on 1000 benign prompts is a threshold near the tenth-highest score, so it sits in the far tail of the benign distribution where a small mean shift buys a huge rate change — the tail mass is not linear in the shift, which is exactly why the operating point moves while the ranking does not. Two habits follow for our own probe tables. Report the **rate at the frozen cut, before and after, on the same items, as a ratio with a hard class boundary** (they use 2 and 0.5), and report the target rate it was set at, because five of eleven damaged cells here fall back inside the boundary when the target moves from 1% to 5% — a finding at one operating point does not transfer to another. And treat "the probe still has AUROC 0.97" as a statement about separability, not about the guardrail, since the same paper shows a refit on the updated activations recovers a median change within ±0.01 of AUROC while the frozen threshold is off target: the information survives, the calibration does not. (arxiv-2611.19216, arxiv-2611.10620, arxiv-2611.19216)
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 263): **The cheapest useful monitor-health check needs no labels and no new data, and it beats the standard distribution-shift test on the axis that matters: computing Gaussian tail mass at the frozen threshold from the mean and standard deviation of stored benign scores flags 0.918 of damaged layer cells and clears 0.898 of undamaged ones, where a Kolmogorov–Smirnov test between pre- and post-update scores reaches 0.966 sensitivity at only 0.543 specificity and average-thresholded-confidence has the better AUROC (0.965 vs 0.952) but 0.479 sensitivity at the operating point.** The design notes that make it work are small and portable: the moments come from the *calibration* negatives only, disjoint from the evaluation negatives behind the realised rate, so the check is out of sample rather than a restatement; the flag threshold is the same 2 and 0.5 used to define damage, so nothing is tuned to the outcome; and the check is scored against a *class* of cells rather than a single number, which is why it can be compared to a KS test at all. A whole-distribution divergence is dominated by regions of the score distribution that never touch the threshold, which is precisely the failure of KS here, and it is the same denominators lesson the folder has recorded for AUROC — measure at the place where the decision is made. For our battery this is a free column: store the benign calibration scores at deployment, recompute their first two moments after any change, and print the estimated-versus-realised rate ratio beside the probe's accuracy. (arxiv-2611.19216, arxiv-2611.10620, arxiv-2610.41445)
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 263): **A repair fitted on data the attacker can write to is not a repair, and the two-sided form of the failure is what makes it worth recording: poisoning 1% of a 1000-item reference with the harmful prompts the probe scores highest costs the threshold re-set 10 points of true-positive rate and leaves it flagging 0.006–0.017 of harmful prompts, while the attacker who supplies the *update* moved one target category past both label-free checks in 3 of 5 seeds at a KL bound tied to the clean seed-to-seed variation (0.08644 nats per token), refuting the authors' own registered hypothesis that no single attacker evades both.** The control that caught the second attack is the part to steal: a canary of held-out labelled harmful prompts that no split uses, thresholded to match the label-free check's clean false-alarm count, flagged every blinded cell with no false alarm in 603 clean draws — a detector for the label-free detector, cheap because it needs labels the deployer already had at deployment. Two consequences for anything we monitor. Re-centring or re-standardising on live traffic is a bet on prevalence and on who controls the stream: the same repair that returns the rate to target on 1% prevalence overshoots to 4.74–24.36 of target on mostly benign traffic and collapses to 0.12–0.31 when harmful traffic rises to 5%. And a green light on a label-free statistic is a statement about benign scores only, so where the consequence is asymmetric our dashboards should carry one labelled canary and print its false-alarm count beside the check it guards. (arxiv-2611.19216, arxiv-2611.07913, arxiv-2611.03439)

- Done 2026-11-16 (entry 261): `arxiv-2611.19176` — A Bag of Concepts? Testing Role-Filler Binding in the Verbalizable Workspace (Reya Dawlah — UT Dallas; Elizabeth McMillin — MiraCosta College; Michael Shihong Zhang — Waterloo; Badrish Ananth — UC Irvine; Rishi Adi Ruia — Washington; Ane Zuñiga — MIT; Thomas Jiralerspong — Mila/Université de Montréal; arXiv:2611.19176v1, 2026-11-14, cs.CL, CC BY 4.0; workshop paper under the title "Interpretability as a Science"). Full text via HTML (57,616 chars, §§1–7 + Appendices A–F); Tables 1–5 quoted as cells, Figure 1 via caption only, all mathematics legible. **Substance:** asks whether the verbalizable workspace — the small vocabulary-indexed subspace read by the J-lens (Gurnee et al.) and the relation-indexed R-lens (Blank et al.) — carries **role-filler binding** rather than a bag of concepts, since safety-relevant propositions share their concept set and differ only in argument assignment. Three dense models (Qwen3.6-27B 64L, Gemma-3-12B base 48L, Gemma-3-27B-IT 62L), two lens families plus a matched J-lens from the same release, two role-direction estimators (difference of means, LRE readout gradient); 600 minimal-pair families / 2,400 sentences per model across three concept pairs × four constructions × role × position, with a disjoint direction-fitting corpus; three tests — ridge probing of the full residual, the workspace slice (top-16 J-lens atoms by non-negative matching pursuit), the orthogonal remainder and a matched-rank random subspace; a calibrated ±sign push along the fitted direction scored by a two-sign **binding score** (difference of differences of the agent−patient log-odds gap, averaged over the two surface positions) against non-participant, random and shuffled-label controls with a pre-registered 0.5-log-odds strength floor; and a top-10 workspace ablation scoring a binding-specific deficit against a fresh matched-rank random-subspace ablation with a difficulty-matching precondition. Verdicts are pre-registered into four classes (positive binding / indistinguishable from controls / clean negative / uninterpretable strength failure) with family-level bootstrap and exact sign-flip permutation plus Holm-Bonferroni. **Results:** within-pair role decoding 0.989/0.975/0.978 from the full residual, 0.984/0.949/0.974 from the discarded remainder, 0.587/0.573/0.574 from the workspace — below the matched-rank random subspace's 0.643/0.589/0.590 — robust to quadratic and random-Fourier probes, a seven-order ridge sweep (workspace 0.645 ceiling vs 0.678–0.724 random) and layer/seed changes; LRE directions stable at 0.967–0.999 cosine and the readout moves +0.94 / −0.99 log-odds while the binding score never clears its null band (Gemma-3-27B-IT pooled −0.0134 → −0.1809 across c = 64 → 256 with the control growing in step, ratios 0.83/1.01/0.84); ablation damages binding specifically on Gemma-3-27B-IT at the entity token only (+0.275, CI 0.262–0.288; 0.284/0.334/0.297 across three lens variants) with nothing on the other two models at either site; entity-token cross-pair transfer above chance for residual, remainder and random (0.510–0.713) but at chance for the workspace, while the sentence-final position inverts below chance for **every** source (0.281–0.320), which the authors diagnose as a probing artefact rather than a workspace property.
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 262): **A verbalizable subspace can be reproducibly readable and still carry less of the property than a random projection of the same rank: the workspace slice decodes role at 0.587/0.573/0.574 against a matched-rank random subspace's 0.643/0.589/0.590, while the full residual reaches 0.989/0.975/0.978 and the part the lens throws away reaches 0.984/0.949/0.974 — so the information is in the stream twice over and in the readable slice not at all.** The design point our battery should steal is the *rank-matched* control, because the natural null (shuffled labels, mean ablation, an untrained probe) cannot distinguish "this subspace is uninformative" from "any 16-dimensional projection is uninformative", and every verbalizable or concept-basis readout in this folder so far has been reported without it. Two habits follow: when we report a score for a projected or dictionary-based representation, run the same probe on the full state, on the projection's complement and on a seeded random basis of identical rank, and print the four together; and treat the complement as its own readout, since the remainder here is functionally as good as the whole and the workspace contributes essentially nothing. The corollary for any monitor we build on a readable slice is that its near-ceiling accuracy on a clean contrast is a statement about the slice's convenience, not about the model's substrate. (arxiv-2611.19176, arxiv-2611.10620, arxiv-2611.03439)
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 262): **A direction can be perfectly stable, demonstrably causal on the model's own report, and still do nothing to the computation you care about: LRE role directions sit at 0.967–0.999 bootstrap cosine and move the next-token role answer by +0.94 and −0.99 log-odds, yet the binding score never leaves the control band on any of the three models, and on Gemma-3-27B-IT the pooled effect grows more than tenfold across the dose sweep (−0.0134 → −0.1809) with the non-participant control growing in step (ratio 0.83/1.01/0.84).** This is the folder's strongest instance of steering a *report* rather than a *state*, and it means our own readout-versus-manipulation checks need a third arm the folder has never used: push the direction and score not only whether the behaviour moves but whether it moves *more than an entity-matched control push of the same norm* — because a push on a concept that has no role to bind also shifts the model's log-odds, and only the difference is binding. The verdict taxonomy is worth copying wholesale: four pre-registered outcomes where a failed strength check is reported as **uninterpretable** rather than as a null, and a "clean negative" additionally requires a tight CI on the effect size so that absence of evidence is separated from evidence of absence. Both of those are cheap formatting decisions that stop a dashboard of p-values from being read as a result. (arxiv-2611.19176, arxiv-2611.17481, arxiv-2611.06001)
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 262): **One model of three is the shape of the causal result, and the confound is named rather than hidden: ablating the top-10 workspace vectors costs binding specifically at +0.275 (CI 0.262–0.288) on the instruction-tuned 27B, replicates across three lens variants (0.284/0.334/0.297), and shows nothing on a base 12B or on Qwen3.6-27B even where the workspace edit perturbs the residual about five times harder than the random control — leaving instruction tuning and scale entangled and a base Gemma-3-27B ablation as the named missing arm.** Three design lessons, each of which we would otherwise have to learn the hard way. A single positive result is what makes the other nulls interpretable at all, because it fires the design's own sensitivity check; a study with three nulls and no positive arm cannot distinguish "no effect" from "no instrument". Every ablation claim needs its edit-magnitude ratio printed beside it, since a null deficit from a 5×-stronger edit means something different from a null at 0.79×. And a task-normalised deficit (the binding margin drop as a share of its own baseline, minus the same share for a recall control) is the right form when the two tasks live on different log-odds scales, provided the difficulty-matching precondition is enforced — here it fails on two of the six cells, and those cells are marked rather than quietly included. (arxiv-2611.19176, arxiv-2611.10720, arxiv-2611.09196)

- Done 2026-11-16 (entry 260): `arxiv-2611.16018` — Protocol-Aware Auditing of Domain-Blind Feature Attribution in Network Intrusion Detection (Emmanuelli El-Mahmoud, Abanisenioluwa Kolawole Orojo, Erika Leal — Baylor; Pablo Rivas — Marist; arXiv:2611.16018v1, 2026-11-11, cs.LG cross-listed cs.CR; poster at the LatinX in AI workshop, NeurIPS 2026). Full text via HTML (99,185 chars, §§1–7 + Appendices A–I) triaged from `/abs/` (5,364 chars); Tables 2, 7–19 quoted as cells, figures 1–6 via captions only, inline and display mathematics blank so no formula is quoted. **Substance:** a formal account of *domain blindness* — attribution and attribution-evaluation procedures (LIME neighbourhoods, SHAP coalitions and background, IG paths, DeepLIFT references, deletion metrics) query model states that a tabular domain forbids — built on a declared **rule-valid set** induced by four Boolean predicate families (domain, order, protocol gate, derived field), an **explainer-oracle transcript** recording every queried state, and a **valid-query invariance** theorem: if two classifiers agree on the oracle information requested inside the rule-valid set, a contained run yields identical transcripts and identical attributions, with a converse witness showing one influential off-rule-valid reply is enough to separate them, and a corollary carrying the same non-identifiability into finite deletion-based faithfulness metrics. Four instantiations of one query-control principle (**PA-XAI**): PA-LIME (protocol drawn from the training distribution, discrete coordinates from empirical marginals, continuous coordinates perturbed with the same Gaussian rule, one pass of an ordered repair map — domain → order restore → std clamped to range → protocol-gated zeroing → derived recompute — then the identical weighted surrogate), PA-SHAP (benign training background, repaired KernelSHAP completions; tree/gradient backends get the background only), PA-IG and PA-DeepLIFT (shared threshold-near training reference, continuous-segment integration with discrete groups fixed, ordered endpoint differences). Four NIDS benchmarks (NSL-KDD, CIC-IDS-2017, UNSW-NB15, CSE-CIC-IDS2018), three classifier families (DNN attacked in Module 2, RF, XGB), 66 configuration pairs per dataset in Module 3, a 16-point compression–fidelity audit in Module 4. **Results:** six standard-LIME perfect-repeatability settings (all three families on UNSW-NB15 and CSE-CIC-IDS2018) fall to 0.52 / 0.69 / 0.43 / 0.48 / 0.86 / 0.60 for PA-LIME, mean 0.575, mean |Δ| 0.425; LIME faithfulness changes sign in five of twelve comparisons incl. all four DNN cases (DNN-LIME 0.28 → −0.07, DNN-IG 0.57 → 0.43, XGB-SHAP 0.58 → 0.71); repaired FGSM at the largest budget 76.1% → 75.3% and curve area 64.09 → 57.86, PGD 74.6% → 58.8% and 52.86 → 44.99; cosine nAUC PA-DeepLIFT 0.452, PA-IG 0.413, SHAP 0.221, LIME 0.153, PA-LIME 0.132, PA-SHAP 0.123; PA-LIME perturbed-feature recovery Top-1 0.064 → 0.152, Top-3 0.200 → 0.384, mean rank 73.0 → 41.2 (SHAP 0.000/0.000, rank 123.0); within-PA Spearman 0.366 vs within-standard 0.217; nondominated compression coordinates only PA-SHAP-DNN (85.3%, −0.68 pp) and PA-IG-DNN (90.5%, −0.89 pp) against a conventional cluster at 80.6% and −0.69 to −0.87 pp; cost PA-LIME 92.2 → 1,690.6 ms, PA-SHAP-XGB 0.10 → 1,990.7 ms, PA-IG 0.70 → 54.6 ms.
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 261): **What an attribution method explains is only defined relative to the states it asked about, and this paper makes that a theorem rather than a caveat: if two models agree on the oracle information requested inside a declared rule-valid set, and the run never queries outside it, the two attributions are identical — so a difference between two explanations is entirely attributable to off-domain behaviour the moment one query escapes, and the same non-identifiability carries straight through into deletion-based faithfulness metrics.** For our battery the operational consequence is that the sampler is part of the measuring instrument and must be reported as one. We currently mask with mean replacement, average over random tokens or add Gaussian noise and never check that the resulting state is a legal input to the thing we are measuring, which means a faithfulness number here is a statement about our sampler at least as much as about the model. Two habits fall out and both are cheap: log the query set (or its footprint) beside every score, and intersect it with a declared plausibility rule set so the leakage fraction is a reported quantity — a column the folder's probe tables have never had. (arxiv-2611.16018, arxiv-2611.01493, arxiv-2610.27446)
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 261): **Perfect repeatability is a red flag, not a virtue, when the sampler is wandering outside the domain: standard LIME reports top-k Jaccard exactly 1.000 in six of twelve model–dataset pairs and the domain-valid version of the same procedure scores a mean of 0.575 there, because the Gaussian neighbourhood rarely crosses a one-hot or an order constraint and so returns nearly the same invalid cloud every time.** The mechanism matters more than the number — the stable thing was the sampler, and the model's behaviour on those states was never the thing being explained. Two standing rules: never report determinism-type stability of a stochastic explainer as evidence of quality, and print the legality rate of the sampled states beside the stability score, because 1.000 at a 0.05 legality rate means the sampler is trapped and 1.000 at a 1.00 rate means the method is genuinely deterministic. The same lesson shows up in the faithfulness flips here — the sign of the correlation reverses in five of twelve comparisons, all four of them DNN cases, when the replacement states become legal — so a sign flip is what a faithfulness protocol looks like when it stops measuring the model on inputs the task cannot produce. (arxiv-2611.16018, arxiv-2611.06001, arxiv-2611.07913)
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 261): **Making an input domain-legal is a safety step and not a defence, and this is the sharpest available instance: passing FGSM/PGD output through an ordered repair map leaves evasion at 75.3% against 76.1% unrestricted at the largest budget, and the intermediate budgets are non-monotone — projection onto the valid set can move an example toward the decision boundary as easily as away from it.** The design point worth importing is that the repair step is deterministic and ordered (domain → order restore → clamp → gate → recompute derived fields), so it is a reproducible transform rather than a search, which is what makes "attack, then repair" and "optimise inside the valid set" separable and lets the paper name the second as untested. It also gives an intervention-side reading of the same asymmetry the folder has recorded for probes: readiness in the direction of projection is one experiment and removal of a property is another; the numbers here show domain projection is a weak instrument with an unpredictable sign, so any edit or mask our own pipeline applies should be evaluated for both evasion-style and explanation-style outcomes rather than assumed monotone. (arxiv-2611.16018, arxiv-2611.17481, arxiv-2611.06001)

- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 260): **"We can decode it" and "the model uses it" are two different numbers, and putting them on one nat scale turns a vague dissociation into a subtraction: here the probe's advantage over a label-marginal null barely moves under any training (a −0.10 to +0.05 spread) while the same reduction read through the model's own unembedding moves ten times as far (−0.75 to +0.25, down to −0.83 under the RL attacks), so everything training does to this signal happens at the readout, and the interesting claims are all about readout gain and readout suppression rather than about storage.** The construction is cheap enough to make standard: one null, one shared output vocabulary for probe/lens/null, cross-fitting grouped by item so no item's tokens leak across folds, and a shuffled-label control that sets the regularisation rather than merely checking it afterwards. The habit to adopt is that any deployable readout we report should be paired with the model's own head on exactly the same folds and classes, because that difference — not the probe's accuracy — is the quantity that says whether the state is merely present or actually load-bearing. **Caveat to carry with it: D is a lower bound away from the last layer and G is probe-family-dependent, so the number is comparable across layers and checkpoints of one model but should not be compared to an effect measured by another instrument.** (arxiv-2610.41445, arxiv-2611.03439, arxiv-2611.10457)
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 260): **An intervention can change behaviour in a direction that the metric everyone uses is blind to, and this paper produces the cleanest instance in the folder: RLVR lifts members' sampled accuracy from 0.141 to 0.170 and drops non-members from 0.132 to 0.088 — a gap that widens from 0.009 to 0.082 with a CI excluding zero — while loss-based AUROC moves from 0.491 to 0.493 and the member-minus-non-member loss gap stays under 0.01 nats against −0.16 for two epochs of SFT.** The mechanism is precise and worth internalising: the loss on members rose 0.24 then 0.56 nats, but non-members rose by the same amount, because the reward saw only the final answer and the text-side quantity an attack measures was never targeted. So the correct reading of a null attack result is "the training signal did not depend on the text", a statement about scope, and only a behavioural arm can distinguish that from "nothing happened". The design lesson generalises past membership: when a group enters a training mix, its statistics can move together with everything else, and the difference-in-differences against a matched reference checkpoint — with exposure-matched steps (step 10 against one epoch) — is what separates a member-specific shift from a global one; a before-and-after comparison without the control group would have reported a huge effect and a huge null in the same table with no way to choose between them. (arxiv-2610.41445, arxiv-2611.10720, arxiv-2611.09196)
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 260): **"The training shift is nearly low-rank" is not evidence that the shift is a usable direction, and the two are separated here by a single comparison: 78–95% of the variance of the training-induced change sits in one component (2–3.5% for random directions), yet the directions recovered by difference of means are unstable across bootstrap resamples (mean pairwise cosine 0.44–0.54, against 0.96 for the SFT version) because that dominant component is shared by members and non-members — and when the stable version is used, single-layer injection buys nothing (AUROC 0.56, p = 0.07) and sustained injection only 0.60.** Three habits for our own steering work. Measure direction stability before measuring direction effect, since a stable direction that fails and an unstable one that "works" mean opposite things. Check whether the dominant component is *discriminative* rather than merely dominant — a shared axis can be rank-one and carry no group information at all. And print the ceiling beside the manipulation, because the SFT direction's own limited payoff (0.56 → 0.60 with sustained injection at four layers) bounds what any inference-time substitute can claim about an effect that training produced through readout. The folder has now met this shape twice in a month — a strong low-rank shift that does not yield a steerable direction — which makes rank and stability a standing pair of columns for anything we intend to turn into an intervention. (arxiv-2610.41445, arxiv-2611.17481, arxiv-2611.06001)

- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 259): **"Is this explanation enough?" can be made a rebuild test, and the control that gives it content is a rebuild with no description at all: a 200-word summary of a hand-written transformer reproduces it exactly on all thirteen algorithmic tasks (1.74× the original's parameters), while a fresh session given only the task produces models 2,043× the size — so the summary is doing the work of specifying *which* compact computation, not merely of asking for a small one, and the ratio between the two arms is the number that separates legibility from luck.** The design is cheap and it is the first test in this folder that measures an explanation by its *reconstructive sufficiency* rather than by agreement with a reference label: describe, rebuild in a fresh session, compare accuracy, size, per-example error correlation and (for the vision model) prediction correlation voxel by voxel, then repeat across eight checkpoints of the same search to see what the summary loses. That last arm is the sharp part — across a search that grows from 373 to 865 lines the rebuilds keep 96% of performance on average, but no rebuild ever beats its original and the late iterations are conveyed least, which is exactly the claim we would want to make about our own predictive model: a short readable statement of it should reproduce most of its behaviour, and where it cannot, the missing part is a specific statement about what is *not* yet legible. For our battery, treat a text-bottleneck rebuild with a no-description control as a standard column beside probe accuracy, since it prices something an AUROC cannot. (arxiv-2611.18114, arxiv-2611.18114, arxiv-2611.01981)
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 259): **An interpretable model rewarded purely on prediction is a confound detector whose findings are legible afterwards, and this paper's best result is a failure: a language-fMRI search that had been climbing slowly jumped from 0.067 to 0.104 in a single step, and the winning features encoded a word's position in the story rather than its meaning — position alone scored about 0.090, above a strong GPT-2 XL baseline at 0.079, by tracking a scan-edge artefact (abnormally high response at scan start, low at scan end, present in all three subjects) at r = 0.97.** A black-box encoder could have exploited precisely this and nobody would have seen it; here the exploit was readable, so the fix (trim ~40 TRs at each end of each scan, in training as well as testing, beyond the release's 20) came out of the diagnosis rather than a separate audit. The generalisable move is what this loop already believes about controls, arriving from the search side: any score-only optimisation will find the cheapest sufficient statistic in the data, and the only reason this one was caught is that the statistic had to be written down. Two habits for our own work — read the winning units of any auto-searched component before reporting its score, and treat an implausibly large single-step improvement as a provenance question rather than a breakthrough. (arxiv-2611.18114, arxiv-2611.10720, arxiv-2611.09196)
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 259): **What these agents produce is a recombination of textbook motifs, and the paper is unusually explicit that this is the ceiling: GCD becomes the subtractive Euclidean algorithm as one three-ReLU block repeated a thousand times, multiplication becomes shifted partial products added by an exponential-attention sink, edit distance becomes one block per dynamic-programming row, and every visual-auditory gain comes from named cortical operations — Gabors, divisive normalisation, quadrature energy, spectro-temporal modulation filters, wavelet scattering.** The reason this is worth recording rather than dismissing is that the failure mode is *structural*, not a matter of model strength: the searches assemble parallel banks of one- or two-stage computations into a linear readout, so they match AlexNet in early visual cortex and trail it in ventral, and the authors locate the gap in deep multi-stage hierarchy, which cannot be reached without either backprop or a much longer hand-written construction. Two consequences. Where we already know the right operations, an agent-written model is plausibly the best way to get a transparent predictor at competitive accuracy, and the shallow-bank/linear-readout template is a good default to start from. Where the claim we want is about *new* mechanism, this route will not deliver it, and the honest framing of any agent-built transparent model is "this is a legible recombination of our priors that predicts as well as our priors allow", which is a real and useful claim but a different one from discovery. (arxiv-2611.18114, arxiv-2611.08089, arxiv-2611.01272)

- Done 2026-11-16 (entry 257): `arxiv-2611.10620` — What Do Collusion Probes Read? Three Pitfalls in Evaluating Multi-Agent Collusion Monitors (Mainul Hasan Mohsin, Mohammad Shahidur Rahman — Dept. of CSE, Shahjalal University of Science and Technology, Sylhet, Bangladesh; arXiv:2611.10620v1, 2026-11-07, cs.LG cross-listed cs.AI/cs.CL/cs.MA, 30 pages, 5 figures, code at github.com/mainul3195/collusion-probe-pitfalls). Full text, 89,330 clean chars incl. Appendix A; all 7 tables quoted as cells, figures 1–5 via captions only, equation bodies blank so no formula quoted. **Substance:** a benchmark and control protocol that separates "was told to collude" from "decided to collude" for multi-agent activation monitors — 2,500 committee episodes (NARCBench's 50 scenarios, 3–8 agents, four public rounds then a vote) plus 1,476 code-review episodes, each cell shared across **look-alike families** (benign coordination, briefed decline, tacit preference, cost pressure, solo deceivers, control, two free-choice families) with five wordings per differing text and test scenarios/wordings never seen in training; logistic probes on last-token activations at layers 16/18/20 of Qwen3-14B (4-bit AWQ, vLLM) in three label variants (published recipe, hard-negative, decision probe on free choices); a brief-removal context cut; baselines = vote rule, TF-IDF, fine-tuned ModernBERT, two LLM judges, a re-implemented divergence detector, a four-feature metadata regression, and a stance oracle; scan statistics (ca-t, ca-glr) for coalition-agnostic group alarms with split-conformal thresholds on unseen wordings; a pre-registered no-brief QLoRA adapter implanting the goal in weights; and one causal arm grading/adding the probe direction. **Results:** vote rule AUROC 0.990 after the vote, recall 0.00 before; judges 0.97 → 0.67 across the same switch; before the vote published recipe 0.06 recall at 1% FPR (AUROC 0.78) and hard-negative probe 0.86 (0.99, 0.70 at 0.1%); colluder-vs-decliner agent AUROC 1.00 → **0.61** with the brief cut (code review 1.000 → 0.746, Mistral-Small-24B 0.797, Qwen3-32B 0.774), published detector 0.568 against decliners while flagging 85% of them, metadata-only 0.883 against controls; stance oracle 0.05 vs probe 0.86 at 1% FPR, invisible attempts 57% (oracle 0.00, probe 0.77), matched pairs 1.00 vs 0.67; decision probe 0.98 joiners-vs-refusers, 0.73 against decliners without the brief, 0.45 recall at 1% FPR, flat learning curve; no-brief implant 0.961 target votes vs 0.000, probes 0.995 / 0.928 (concealed 0.991 / 0.891, strictest cut 0.668), threshold does not transfer (source 1% → 2.5% / 4.0% false alarms); live alarm recall 0.93, realised FPR 0.008, median delay 0 rounds; direction grading 0.41 → 0.26 collusion success vs 0.43 random, pushing into decliners induces nothing; monitor-aware agents 0.87 → 0.71 (warned) → 0.55 (told to evade).
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 258): **"Detection" splits into three separable claims — fires before the outcome, fires for the decision rather than the cue, fires when the transcript is silent — and this paper prices each one separately, which is the reporting shape our own probe tables have never had.** The three numbers sit on the same scale and show what a single AUROC hides: after the vote a rule that reads nothing but the votes reaches 0.990 and a real probe 0.98, yet before the vote the same rule has nothing to read and the probe falls to 0.86 recall at a 1% alarm budget; with look-alike negatives added, a probe that looked near-perfect separates decision from no-decision at only 0.61 once the eliciting text is cut from the context; and against the best possible reader of what agents actually said in public the probe leads 0.86 to 0.05, not because the text reader is bad but because in 57% of attempts nothing informative was ever said. For our battery the operational form is a four-column row per monitor — budget-conditioned recall, cue-cut recall, ceiling-relative gap, realised false-alarm rate — since each column can fail on its own and a method that is strong on one routinely collapses on another. The corollary the folder already earned from the denominators lesson applies with new force: an AUROC of 0.993 on a contrast whose negatives differ from the positives in the cue is a statement about the cue, and the only way to know which is to run the contrast both ways. (arxiv-2611.10620, arxiv-2611.10606, arxiv-2610.27446)
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 258): **The control that disqualifies a readout is a set of negatives that carry the confound and lack the effect, and this paper's family design is the most systematic instance in the folder: benign coordinators hold the same brief and the same private channel with an honest motive, briefed decliners hold the collusion brief verbatim and refuse in the next sentence, tacit agents argue for the target openly, and cost pressure has the chair argue for it — so every shortcut a probe might take has a family that defeats it, and the decline family is exactly why the headline separates at 1.00 in full context and 0.61 after the cut.** The design note worth importing is that a first, family-free version was solved outright by a shortcut (AUROC 1.00, failed attempts scoring like successful ones, a lone agent caught every time) and the families were added to remove it — the benchmark was hardened against its own probe, not the other way round. Two habits follow. When we design a negative set, enumerate the cues by hand and construct one negative class per cue rather than sampling more of the same negatives. And where a multi-feature contrast cannot be isolated, follow these authors' rule: draw conclusions only where several contrasts agree, and reserve causal language for the steering arm — because decliners differ from colluders in the decline note as well as the goal, and the same-prompt contrasts read the decision from behaviour without randomising it. (arxiv-2611.10620, arxiv-2610.40055, arxiv-2611-08895)
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 258): **Erasing a direction and adding one are separate experiments with different answers, and this is the folder's cleanest instance of the asymmetry: grading the probe direction out of colluders' states while they write lowers collusion success from 0.41 to 0.26 while grading out a random direction leaves it at 0.43, yet pushing the same direction into decliners produces no collusion at all — so the direction is necessary-ish for the behaviour's expression and not sufficient for it, which is exactly the profile of a readout of "holding an active goal" rather than of the decision.** The mechanism story that fits is worth carrying: the signal survives when the goal is implanted in the weights with no prompt anywhere (0.995), the alarm fires in the round the instruction arrives (median delay zero), and it persists on messages written before any public argument — three facts that agree on "goal held" and disagree with any reading of the direction as an action plan. Three consequences. Report ablation and addition arms separately and never present one as evidence for the other; treat a null induction as informative about the readout's semantics rather than a failed experiment; and re-run the monitor on the edited episodes after grading the direction out, since here it still flags every one of them and that contradiction is what rules out the simplest causal story. (arxiv-2611.10620, arxiv-2611.17481, arxiv-2611.01493)

- Done 2026-11-16 (entry 256): `arxiv-2611.01981` — Opening the Black Box of Neural Auction Mechanisms (Li Kong, Zilong Liu, Haoyang Zhou, Hanbing Liu, Qi Qi — Gaoling School of Artificial Intelligence, Renmin University of China; arXiv:2611.01981v1 2026-11-01, cs.AI, CC BY 4.0, results at github.com/Li-Beverly-Kong/opening-neural-auctions). Full text, 69,993 clean chars incl. Appendices A–C; all 8 tables quoted as cells, figures 1–5 via captions only, equation bodies blank so no formula quoted. **Substance:** a post-hoc white-box audit of a frozen CITransNet contextual auction (2 bidders × 5 items with continuous context, plus a single-item continuous and a five-item discrete-type auxiliary) at the first fully connected layer, on the per-bidder–item-**pair** representation; a TopK SAE (512 features, 32 active) fitted to standardized pair states with a dead-feature revival branch; fidelity checked on the representation and on downstream behaviour after patching the reconstructions back in; seven economic targets (revenue, welfare, focal utility, payment share, allocation entropy, winner margin, and a counterfactual incentive score); for each feature an LLM explainer (gpt-5.6-luna) writes at most 35 words and selects a target and a direction from the generation-partition Spearman sign, all frozen; a blinded predictor judges activation on a disjoint balanced partition against shuffled / frequency-matched / target-only / explanation-only / random / always-active controls; the causal test is a four-dose multiplicative scaling with a one-sided directional t-test, BH-corrected over the dictionary, plus a six-dose retention check; then three audits — regret slopes under re-optimised misreports, Myerson-oracle region AUC and MAE moves, and two case studies. **Results:** reconstruction MSE about 1.2×10⁻², sparsity 31.998, inactive-feature fraction 0.977%, mean allocation and payment differences 0.003013 / 0.000534; partition-to-partition Spearman correlations 0.872–0.999; pooled precision 0.630 and recall 0.672 across all 512 features with non-overlapping interval bounds against every informative control (text adds 0.149 P and 0.206 R over target-only; the target adds 0.038 P and 0.086 R over text); 165 strong-response features (32.2%), 158 retained at extreme dose (95.8%), 163 of 165 with R² ≥ 0.95; regret 88 up / 77 down raw and 26 / 17 after BH correction, concentrated in payment share (17/11) and utility (3/0), with F335 and F364 adding 0.0331 and 0.0296 to mean regret at high dose; Myerson no-sale AUC 0.9636 from F62 and winning regions at 0.9129 / 0.9277 with bidder-level reads against 0.6789 / 0.7161 with auction-level max-pooling; cross-setting strong counts 165 / 106 / 142 with regret splits 26/17, 37/43, 43/10.
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 257): **A dictionary unit earns the name "explanation" only when two independently frozen tests both pass, and this paper is the folder's cleanest instance of the two-axis filter: a description written from the feature's own examples must anticipate its activation on auctions it never saw — against a frequency-matched control, not only a random one — and a multiplicative dose on that same feature must move the target that was assigned to it before anyone looked.** The design point worth copying is that the second test is *directional and pre-assigned*, so it cannot be satisfied by a post-hoc reading of whichever target happened to move: the explainer commits a target and a sign on a generation split, the interventions run on a held-out split, and 165 of 512 features survive. Two consequences for our own battery. The control ladder is where the epistemic content lives — full prompt 0.630/0.672, text-only 0.591/0.586, frequency-matched 0.509/0.470, shuffled 0.505/0.460, target-only 0.481/0.466, random 0.499/0.495 — and the frequency-matched rung is the one that separates "the description names the feature's condition" from "the description names something merely correlated with how often the feature fires", a distinction our own probe-versus-feature comparisons have never priced. And the verified set must never be reported as the dictionary: 165 of 512 is 32.2%, the other 67.8% lie outside the seven targets, and the paper's own remark that unsupervised dictionaries mostly model input structure is the honest reading of that silence. (arxiv-2611.01981, arxiv-2610.27446, arxiv-2611.03439)
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 257): **Readout level is an intervention inside the model, not a choice in the probe code, and this table shows the price with the same features on both sides: bidder-level reads of F73 and F421 separate Myerson's two winning regions at AUC 0.9129 and 0.9277, while the auction-level maximum over bidders — the same activations, one pooling step earlier in the reading — recovers only 0.6789 and 0.7161, because a max over bidders destroys the positional identity that *is* the winner.** The no-sale region is unaffected (0.9636), which is exactly what the diagnosis predicts: trade-versus-no-trade is a property of the auction, winner identity is a property of a slot. For our work this makes pooling a first-class experimental variable — whenever we pool per-position states (mean over sequence, max over heads, sum over pairs) we change which distinctions the readout can represent, and the right report is the same score at two levels with the pool named, as here. The companion point from the application side is that a mechanically coherent account of one instance can be assembled from four numbers — which features fire, where on the bidder–item grid they fire, what direction each was assigned, and what the outcome was — and that it reads as a diagnosis (here: near-total payment share with collapsed transaction scale, so failure to clear trade rather than weak extraction). (arxiv-2611.01981, arxiv-2611.10720, arxiv-2611.01493)
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 257): **A domain with no semantics at all is the sharpest test of a validation protocol, and this pipeline needs no interpretable inputs: the activations are dense numeric auction profiles, there are no tokens to name a feature after, and yet anchoring every description to one of seven outputs makes it testable — the direct answer to our own worry that a readout is only as meaningful as the vocabulary it is expressed in.** The economics also supply something the language-model entries in this folder keep missing: a *ground truth* to audit against, since Myerson's rule is analytic in the two-bidder single-item case, so "does the decomposition recover the oracle's structure" has an answer rather than an analogy — F62 marks trade versus no-trade at 0.9636 AUC with no oracle supervision, and ablating it moves allocation and payment MAE away from the oracle while doubling moves them toward it. Three things to carry: when a domain has an analytic optimum, use it as the reference arm instead of another fitted model; keep "the mechanism was trained without this knowledge" separate from "the feature predicts it", since the interesting claim is discovery rather than fitting; and note the standing cost of target-anchoring — a feature that models input structure without serving any target is unverifiable by construction, so the audit's silence about 67.8% of the dictionary is a scope statement, not a null result. (arxiv-2611.01981, arxiv-2611.01272, arxiv-2611.11035)

- Done 2026-11-16 (entry 255): `arxiv-2611.07913` — Same Answer, Different Future: Dissociating Belief Content and Evidence Weight in Language Models (Weihan Li — University of Tokyo; Junhao Wu — RWTH Aachen; Xinlei Chen — Harbin Institute of Technology, Shenzhen; Tianshi Zheng — HKUST; arXiv:2611.07913v1 2026-11-05, v2 2026-11-11, cs.LG, CC BY 4.0, 37 pages, 18 figures, 17 tables, Appendices A–P). Full text, ~155k clean chars; Tables 1, 2, A1, A2, A7, A8, A13, A14 quoted as cells; all figures via captions only. **Substance:** a belief is split into **content** (the prediction a readout returns now) and **weight** (how many new observations that prediction is worth); weight is measured as an **exchange rate** w = m·a/S from a regression of the post-update readout on the conveyed proportion π (slope a) and on the new observations' proportion κ (slope S), which returns w = n for a record and w = the stated count for a summary under a uniform-prior Bayesian observer and is gain-invariant because it is a ratio. Bernoulli task; six routes to one prediction (shown record of n ∈ {8,16,32,64}; summary of counts; told rate from a source stated 95% or 55% accurate; instruction at three strengths up to a constraint; steered = record plus mean-difference direction one-shot at 4 or 16 positions or persistent; transplanted = a long record's residual frontier copied into a short one); two readouts (continuation vs estimate) in two frames plus a one-token H/T decision check; four futures (new segment of 8/16/32, extended line, count segment, neutral passage placebo); nine open-weight models 8B–397B (Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen3-8B, Gemma-3-12B, Qwen3-32B, Gemma-3-27B, hybrid Qwen3.8-27B local; Qwen3.5-122B, Qwen3-235B, Qwen3.5-397B MoE served) plus three proprietary models in an appendix. **Results:** matched states whose estimates agree within 0.02 move apart under the same sixteen observations in five of six local models by 1.6–2.5× in either direction (summary moves further in four, record 2.5× further in Qwen3.8-27B); 64 observations are worth 20–53 as a record and 8.7–151 as a summary, with no convergence at 397B; layout decides weighting (new outcomes on the record's own line draw slopes 0.00/0.08/0.18 against 0.36/0.71/0.76 for a new segment); a one-shot write installs 92–154% of the natural content difference but retains ≤0.12 (Llama-3.1-8B) and ≤0.24 (Qwen3-8B) after sixteen observations against 0.42/0.43 natural, while a neutral passage of matched length leaves it at 1.56/1.66; the hybrid Qwen3.8-27B keeps the write at 0.40 against 0.29 natural; weight is not writable (2.9–4.7 vs 17.2 under a length-direction; a copied frontier closes 0.003 and −0.011 of the gap); hiding the first 48 outcomes lowers content to 0.34 and weight to 0.29 together; a reasoning step that writes counts into the context restores both forms to 58–67 (and 16-observation states to 15–16); seven pre-registered predictions met 8 of 21 cells (what-sets-weight 5/6, form-of-dependence 3/8).
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 256): **A prediction is a single number and a belief is at least two, and this paper is the folder's first instrument that separates them cleanly: content is what the readout returns now, weight is how many new observations that content is worth, and the whole measurement is two regression slopes on the same states after appending identical evidence — w = m·a/S — so no ablation, no ablation baseline and no network access is needed to ask how firmly anything is held.** The constructive point for a white-box predictor is that weight turned out to be *gain-invariant by construction* (a ratio, so a readout that compresses probabilities returns the same weight) and comparable across layers and models without any normalisation of the readout scale, which is exactly the property our own strength comparisons keep lacking: every raw steering coefficient in this folder is at best a within-layer claim, and every weight here is a cross-model one. The destructive point is the matched-output confound — five of six local models with estimates agreed to within 0.02 diverge by 1.6 to 2.5× under identical new evidence, in either direction, so selecting or comparing interventions by matching their current prediction is not a controlled comparison and the bias has no fixed sign to correct for. Two habits fall out: report content and weight as a pair for any belief-like state we claim to have installed (probe label, feature, vector, summary), and prefer constructions where the future can be forked from the state, because that is what makes weight measurable at all. (arxiv-2611.07913, arxiv-2611.06001, arxiv-2611.01493)
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 256): **A placebo of matched length is the arm that separates "the intervention decayed" from "the intervention was diluted", and the numbers here make the distinction impossible to argue with: a one-shot steering write retains at most 0.12 (Llama-3.1-8B) and 0.24 (Qwen3-8B) of its content after sixteen real observations, but 1.56 and 1.66 of it after a 26-token neutral passage of the same length — the write survives *better* under dilution, because a passage carrying no coin observations removes competing content from what the readout attends to while leaving the injected bias in place as a larger share.** So the usual decay story (attention spreads, the write washes out) is ruled out for these two models and the alternative (evidence specifically overrides it) is what remains, and the paper draws exactly that conclusion rather than a softer one. What generalises is the experimental obligation: any claim that an activation-level edit is undone by *the task* needs a length-matched irrelevant-input control, printed on the same axis, and the control must be irrelevant in the sense that matters — same token count, same position, no instance of the quantity being reasoned about. The companion result sharpens the negative: neither a direction built from the 64-vs-8 difference (2.9–4.7 against 17.2 observations) nor a copied residual frontier (closes 0.003 of the gap) transfers weight, so weight is not another vector to add — it is recovered from text at query time, which is why a reasoning step that writes the counts into the context restores it to 58–67 for both evidence forms. (arxiv-2611.07913, arxiv-2611.01272, arxiv-2610.40055)
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 256): **Pre-registration is cheap on a scale story and it changes what the paper can claim, because it fixes in advance which failures count as refutations: seven predictions plus two write criteria were committed to the repository the day before the larger models ran, and the verdicts split along a line nobody could have chosen post hoc — the two predictions about *what sets* the weight (the question asked; route at matched estimates) held in five of six cells, once with the opposite sign, while the five about *how* the dependence varies with form held in three of the eight evaluable cells, with 7 more not evaluable at all.** That split is the useful output: the paper can say scale does not close the gap and that form-dependence is not a stable target, without having to defend either as a lucky sample, and the yes/no cell that fails by its own criterion on a near-deterministic sampling channel is reported as a failure rather than dropped. For our battery this is the format to copy for any cross-model claim — derive predictions from the small models, commit the criteria and the comparison rule (whole-interval for the interval tests, point estimates where the paper says so), then report a met/not-met/cannot-evaluate table with the deciding number in each cell. The companion discipline is the noise floor: the equivalence tolerance is derived from the readouts' own wording variance (0.07 in slope for Llama-3.1-8B, 0.16 for Qwen3-8B; 0.15 in logit units for the steering comparisons) rather than picked, so "unchanged" and "changed" are decided against a measured scale and not against a null result. (arxiv-2611.07913, arxiv-2611.03439, arxiv-2610.27446)

- Done 2026-11-16 (entry 254): `arxiv-2611.08089` — SAE Interprets MoE: Sparse AutoEncoders Reveal That MoE Experts Exhibit Human-Interpretable Fine-Grained Specialization (Anyuan Zhuo, Shaohua Zhang, Yuan Lin, Pinyan Lu — ByteDance Seed / Shanghai University of Finance and Economics; arXiv:2611.08089v1, 2026-11-05, cs.LG, code at github.com/Bytedance-Seed/SAE-Interprets-MoE). Full text via PDF, 77,392 chars, 30 pages incl. Appendices A–K. **Substance:** one top-k SAE (2^20 latents, FVU 12.6%/25.1%/7.6%) per MoE layer (layers 4, 30, 46 of Qwen3-30B-A3B, 128 experts, 8 active, no shared experts); because the layer output is a router-weighted sum of expert outputs and the encoder is affine, each latent's pre-activation splits exactly over experts (Eq. 5), the positive part normalised over activated experts and corpus-averaged gives a contribution fraction (Eqs. 6–9), and a threshold of 0.2 defines the dominance bipartite graph over 128 experts × 220 latents; latents auto-interpreted by GPT-5.5 from 5 top + 5 random contexts, logit-lens top-10 boosted/suppressed tokens and a depth prior, with an "Uninterpretable" option; expert labelled from its explanation word cloud, then all 128 labels partitioned in one call with a 6–13 group bound. **Results:** contribution profiles steeper than gating at all three layers (layer 30 rank-0 0.512 vs 0.231, rank-7 0.005 vs 0.074; truncation only 2.09/1.29/1.64 of 8); single-dominator latents 57.4/62.1/56.7%, ≤2 dominators 89.9/85.1/92.7%, no dominator 7.0/13.6/3.7%; top-10 experts hold 24.6/20.1/30.1% of edges vs 7.8% uniform; median Jaccard ~1e-4 with 37.5–40.5% of pairs sharing nothing and ≤0.57% above 0.05; 19 of the 20 largest-J pairs at layer 30 are same-domain; judge-scored expert theme share 86.7/78.6/78.1/59.1% vs 1.9–6.7% random; eleven recovered domains with computing 28, text form 21, maths and reasoning 20, applied science 18, then 8/7/7/5/5/5/4, art in one label.
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 255): **When the quantity you want is linear in the thing you are attributing to, the attribution is a theorem and the experiment budget should move to interpretation: here the MoE layer output is a router-weighted sum of expert outputs and the SAE encoder is affine, so each latent's pre-activation splits exactly over the experts that produced it, with no patching budget, no random-ablation baseline and no seed variation — and the entire empirical section is then about *reading* the resulting graph rather than about establishing it.** That matters for a white-box predictor because the cost profile of an exact decomposition is completely different from a fitted one: nothing in the decomposition can be over- or under-estimated, so every number in §4 is a statistic of the data rather than an estimate of a causal effect, and the paper's one predictive claim (that pruning or editing an expert chiefly affects the latents it dominates) is left as an untested hypothesis, which is the honest boundary of an exact non-causal decomposition. The check to run before any attribution study in our own battery is therefore algebraic — is there a linear map from the component to the unit being explained? — and if yes, the ablation arm is a waste of compute and the interesting work is the naming. (arxiv-2611.08089, arxiv-2610.27446, arxiv-2611.01493)
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 255): **"Which component fires here" and "which component makes this happen" are different measurements with a wide, structured gap, and the price of confusing them is visible in one rank-by-rank comparison: the router's own weights decay gently across its top-k (0.231, 0.169, 0.137 at layer 30) while the contribution the same experts actually make collapses far faster (0.512, 0.185, 0.115), so the top expert carries 23% of the gating mass and 51% of the output, and at the bottom of the ranking the two differ by an order of magnitude (0.074 gating against 0.005 contribution).** The methodological trick is what makes the claim clean: aggregate both quantities *by rank* over the corpus so their profiles sum to the same total, and the comparison stops being an impression. For our own work this is the same lesson the folder earned about selection counts in pruning and about denominators in probes, arriving on the mixture-of-experts side — a firing count is not an effect size, and the coefficient attached to the firing is the missing factor. Two standing columns follow for any per-component table we publish: the weighted contribution beside the activation frequency, and the share of the total the top component carries. (arxiv-2611.08089, arxiv-2611.01493, arxiv-2611.06001)
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 255): **Describing a component by the inputs that activate it loses exactly the distinctions the component is making, and the demonstration is the cheapest possible: the token word cloud of expert 72 is the, and, of, but the explanations of the latents that expert dominates read exercise and health alongside algorithms and data structures, and the second theme is invisible at token level because the latent carrying it fires only at the `<=` of a binary search.** The mechanism generalises — a latent's meaning lives in the context around the position, not the surface string at it — so summary-by-top-inputs systematically under-reports a component's specificity and makes everything look like a surface-feature detector. The construction worth copying is the two-level description: interpret the learned units, then describe the component by the *set of units it dominates*, with dominance defined on an averaged fraction and a threshold far above the even-share level (0.2 against 1/128) so the set stays near-disjoint across components — median Jaccard near 1e-4, and the little overlap that survives concentrating inside same-domain pairs. What it buys is a description in the model's vocabulary that no taxonomy supplies, including three domains in the eleven recovered here (text form, language, entities and identifiers, 36 of 128 experts) that are not subject areas at all and that a subject-matter taxonomy would have had to scatter. (arxiv-2611.08089, arxiv-2611.01272, arxiv-2611.03439)

- Done 2026-11-16 (entry 253): `arxiv-2611.06001` — How Far Can You Steer? Behavior–Capability Frontiers in Contrastive Activation Addition (Deepanshu Raj, single author — The University of Chicago; arXiv:2611.06001v1, 2026-11-04, cs.LG cross-listed cs.CL, CC BY 4.0, 23 pages, 18 figures, Appendices A–H). Full text, 84,091 clean chars; all 12 tables read as cells, figures via captions, Eq. 8 reconstructed. **Substance:** CAA mean-difference directions per behaviour per layer, layer-norm-rescaled, with a dimensionless relative dose η = α·m_ℓ/r_ℓ beside the raw coefficient; layer chosen from behavioural validation only (coarse ±1 scan → nine-layer window → nine-point α grid, maximising the sum of best positive and best negative gain); coefficient chosen under a capability constraint on MMLU, ARC-C and HellaSwag (minimum paired-bootstrap LCB95 of accuracy change ≥ −ε); the resulting operating point frozen before any held-out or audit evaluation, with no reselection; audits = three null families (norm-matched isotropic, label-shuffled, off-target-KL-matched within 10%), 42 ordered cross-behaviour transfer pairs at seven fractional depths and η = 0.20, GSM8K/WikiText-2, cross-domain sycophancy, TruthfulQA, and blinded LLM-judged open-ended generation. Four 7–8B instruction-tuned models (Llama 2 7B Chat, Llama 3.1 8B Instruct, Mistral 7B Instruct v0.3, Qwen2.5 7B Instruct), seven behaviours. **Results:** selected layers Llama 2 11–13, Llama 3.1 12–16, Mistral 13–15 (fractional 0.35–0.52) but Qwen2.5 17–19 of 28 (0.63–0.70); validation→test Pearson 0.969 / Spearman 0.945 over the 109 unique nonzero interventions (mean gain 0.125 vs 0.124, mean |diff| 0.019, per-model ρ 0.926–0.959); joint behaviour+capability survival 9/24 = 37.5% at ε = 1%, 40/55 = 72.7% at 3%, 43/56 = 76.8% at 5%, with 32 of 56 claims keeping α = 0 at 1% and only one at 3%; limiting benchmark model-dependent (MMLU for Llama 3.1, HellaSwag elsewhere); specificity CAA 0.124 [0.105, 0.144] vs nulls 0.001 / 0.001 / 0.004 with exceedance 96.3% / 72.5% / 84.4% (label-shuffled the weak null: 53.1% Llama 3.1, 70.0% Mistral), KL match rate 94.7%; signed geometry vs signed transfer ρ = 0.290 (p = 1.98×10⁻⁴, per-model 0.214–0.372), unsigned null (ρ = 0.042, p = 0.598), transfer magnitude peaking at fractional depth 0.42 (≈0.036 vs 0.006–0.016 elsewhere); WikiText-2 perplexity +6.63% and ΔNLL vs |η| ρ = 0.819, GSM8K −10.24 points with only 14 of 56 conditions supported; OOD sycophancy 14/16 in the intended sign, 9/16 supported, median OOD retention 46.5%, hallucination→TruthfulQA 7/8 supported (Qwen2.5 negative the exception); open-ended sycophancy 1.35 → 2.29 → 2.77, refusal 2.25 → 2.62 → 2.51, hallucination flat at ≈2.08 for both signs, 12 of 288 triplets dropped for nontermination (all Llama 3.1).
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 254): **Steering's behavioural side generalises and its cost side does not, and the same frozen points produce both numbers: validation-selected gains hold at ρ = 0.945 with a mean gain of 0.125 against 0.124 on test, while joint survival collapses to 9 of 24 at a 1% budget, and 23 of those 24 points kept their behavioural support — the loss is capability, not efficacy.** The failure is a property of the constraint, not bad luck in sampling: 32 of 56 claims kept α = 0 because nothing nonzero passed the confidence bound, and the surviving set nearly triples when the budget moves from 1% to 3% before flattening at 5%. What that implies for anything we report is a separability rule — behavioural transfer, capability cost and specificity are three axes and the paper's own tables show they can be read almost independently, so a single "works / doesn't work" verdict on a direction is a category error. It also argues for the confidence-bound form of the constraint rather than a point estimate: at ε = 1%, a point-estimate selection rule and an LCB rule would disagree exactly where the answer matters, and the author is honest that low survival there may be conservativeness rather than degradation. (arxiv-2611.06001, arxiv-2611.17481, arxiv-2611.08790)
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 254): **The freeze is what makes a held-out number a prediction rather than a re-fit, and it costs almost nothing to implement: layer selected on behavioural validation, coefficient selected on capability data, nothing reselected afterwards, and every later audit — specificity, transfer, OOD, open-ended — reads a fixed claim.** The paper states the design consequence plainly: the validation–test near-diagonal is not evidence that the method works, only that selection did not overfit, and the interesting failures (14 of 56 GSM8K conditions with supported loss, the open-ended ordering that disappears for hallucination) are exactly the ones that freezing exposes. The companion point is the normalisation: α is meaningless across depth because the residual norm grows with it, so the comparable axis is the relative dose η = α·m_ℓ/r_ℓ, and the paper prints both rather than choosing — a format our own dose sweeps should copy, since every "steering strength" comparison in this folder that quotes a raw coefficient is at best a within-layer claim. (arxiv-2611.06001, arxiv-2611.01493, arxiv-2610.40055)
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 254): **A geometry score can be significant and still useless for the decision it is usually asked to make: signed cosine similarity against signed causal cross-behaviour transfer reaches ρ = 0.290 at p = 1.98×10⁻⁴, but the unsigned association is null (ρ = 0.042) and transfer magnitude swings across depth from 0.006 to 0.036 independently of it.** So direction alignment carries information about *which way* two behaviours interact and essentially none about *how much*, which is the quantity an intervention-sized claim needs. Two controls are worth stealing from this design. The permutation acts on the seven behaviour identities and is applied synchronously across all model–depth blocks, preserving the repeated structure of the 42 ordered pairs instead of pretending the measurements are independent. And the transfer arm fixes η across depth, so a depth profile of transfer is not a depth profile of dose — the distinction the folder's own layer-selection entries keep blurring. (arxiv-2611.06001, arxiv-2611.01493, arxiv-2611.05344)

- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 253): **An intervening method is bounded by the thing it imitates, and the ceiling has to be printed before any of its numbers mean anything: the German vector applied directly at the filler positions with no suffix reaches only 90.00% of thirty prompts, and the refusal vector tops out at 50.00% HarmBench jailbreak at α = 1.5 while scoring 90.91% on a substring metric, so the imitating suffix's 86.7% and its 27.3% are largely statements about the target.** This is the folder's denominators lesson arriving on the intervention side, and the sharper half is the ceiling's *size*: more than half of the reachable jailbreak effect is missing from the vector itself, which means the equivalence being studied is an equivalence to a weak object and the paper's own sentence — the behaviour is reachable from the input up to a loss that depends on the concept — is bounded twice, once by the concept and once by the vector construction. Two habits for our battery. Every imitation, distillation or surrogate we build (a probe for a direction, a suffix for a steering vector, a small model for a large one) gets its reference object's own score reported first and in the same table, because a 27.3% that beats a 13.6% baseline looks like a win until the 50.00% ceiling is beside it. And when a claim is about *reachability* rather than about mechanism, write the claim at the level of the behaviour with the measuring instrument named, since the same suffix here scores 90.9% and 27.3% on two measures of one concept and neither is a calibration of the other. (arxiv-2611.17481, arxiv-2611.01272, arxiv-2611.11035)
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 253): **Transfer in this folder keeps failing upward and succeeding downward, and this paper makes the asymmetry look like a property of the direction rather than of the task: a universal German suffix from Gemma-2-2B gives 65.0% on Gemma-1.1-2B and 5.0% on Gemma-2-9B, Qwen3-1.7B's gives 95.0% on Qwen2.5-1.5B and 60.0% on Qwen3-4B, Llama-3.2-3B's gives 95.0% on Llama-3.2-1B, and on refusal every larger sibling collapses to single digits or zero (Gemma-2-9B 0.0% HarmBench, Qwen3-4B 9.1%, Llama-3.2-1B 4.5%).** The same shape appears in the German universal suffix's own generalisation (95.0% on training prompts, 96.7% on thirty unseen ones for Llama-3.2-3B, but 90.0/73.3 and 95.0/80.0 for the other two), so the pattern is not a size artefact alone — but the size gradient is consistent enough across two concepts and three families to be treated as a default expectation. Three consequences. Any transfer claim we publish should state the direction of the size change explicitly, because an average over siblings hides a 65/5 split. A suffix, feature or vector found in one model is evidence about models at or below that scale, and upward extrapolation needs its own arm rather than an assumption. And the generalisation gap has to be scored at matched prompt counts, as here, because Llama's test set scoring *above* its training set is explained by twenty versus thirty prompts, not by luck. (arxiv-2611.17481, arxiv-2611.10720, arxiv-2611.08551)
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 253): **Optimising a proxy to its floor and moving the behaviour are separate achievements, and this paper's own curves show the decoupling without being designed to: the activation-distance loss falls roughly logarithmically and stops improving past about a hundred of the 250 steps, yet doubling the step budget still buys HarmBench rate on both models tested (27.3% → 31.8% on Gemma-2-2B, 40.9% → 54.5% on Qwen3-1.7B), and the author names the general form as a limitation — a suffix can match the target activations closely and still fail to jailbreak.** The companion observation is the mirror image and as useful: on Qwen3-1.7B the *discrete* suffix already matches the continuous soft-suffix upper bound (96.7% against 93.33%), so the gap the proxy reports between discrete and continuous search is not a gap in behaviour. Three things to carry. Report proxy progress and outcome progress on separate axes with the relationship between them measured, never a single curve ending in a probability. Check whether the proxy's floor is reachable at all in the regime you are operating in before attributing a shortfall to your optimiser — here the continuous upper bound says the discrete search is not the binding constraint on one model and is on the other. And prefer an upper bound that *removes* a constraint (soft tokens in place of a vocabulary, a lookup table in place of a rule family, an oracle in place of a fitted selector) over one that merely adds capacity, because only the constraint-removing variant says what the constraint costs. (arxiv-2611.17481, arxiv-2610.27446, arxiv-2611.08551)

- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 252): **A location claim and a stability claim are different claims, and the pair of numbers here separates them cleanly: the zone partition is essentially identical when the benchmark changes (Jaccard 1.00 for two of three models across nuScenes and Argoverse 2, 0.88–0.96 for the third, against a size-matched chance level of 0.18) but only moderately similar when the architecture changes (0.71–0.81 on the zones that both models possess), and the middle zone does not survive the architecture change at all — it is a nine-layer band in one causal decoder, a seven-layer band in the other, and structurally empty under prefix-LM attention.** The asymmetry is the result, not a nuisance: dataset-invariance says the diagnosis is measuring the model, and architecture-variance says depth indices are not portable objects. This is the same lesson the folder earned about replay protocols in `arxiv-2611.01493` (rankings invert under a different query protocol) arriving on the depth axis, and it has a cheap operational form for us. Whenever we publish a layer band, a zone, or an index into the network, print the stability score against a stated chance level under both perturbations we care about — new data and new architecture — because the first usually looks reassuring and the second is what a reader will try to reuse. And prefer reporting the partition as *relative* depth with the normalisation stated, since the 0.71–0.81 cross-architecture agreement only exists after mapping every model onto a shared 16-point grid. (arxiv-2611.10720, arxiv-2611.01493, arxiv-2611.16315)
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 252): **Adding an alignment objective on top of task tuning can be strictly negative, and the size of the effect is what makes it worth a standing arm: full LoRA plus uniform MMD is worse than full LoRA alone on 17 of 18 quality cells by 0.01–0.09 m, and MMD with no task tuning at all doubles the error outright (4.275 m to 9.657 m, marked collapsed in all six settings).** The explanation is the one to import — a uniform objective is applied to layers that are already domain-invariant and overwrites their computation while leaving the modality-specific error untouched — and it is testable rather than rhetorical, because the ablation that removes the freeze zone costs under 0.02 m (those parameters were near-optimal anyway) while swapping the two zone operators costs 0.3–0.4 m everywhere. Three consequences for our battery. Every located intervention should be reported beside the align-everything composite, since the naive composite is not merely weaker than the better arm but worse than doing nothing extra; the folder's previous lesson about same-ingredients controls (`arxiv-2610.40055`) gains a stronger form here, where the extra ingredient actively hurts. Second, the operator-to-zone *matching* is a separate degree of freedom from the partition, and here it is the largest single ablation hit — so a method that gets the location right and the operator wrong loses more than one that gets the location approximately right. Third, report a final-displacement or worst-case metric alongside the mean, because a mean over an aligned manifold can hide per-cell damage that the 17-of-18 count exposes immediately. (arxiv-2611.10720, arxiv-2610.40055, arxiv-2611.03439)
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 252): **A difference of two errors is not a measure of the second one, and this table is the sharpest instance in the folder: on LFM2/nuScenes the adapted model reports a domain gap of 3.150 m against 2.550 m for source-only, i.e. a larger gap, while its absolute target error is lower (4.251 vs 4.510 m) — because adaptation improved the source side more than the target side, and on Argoverse 2 the same arithmetic turns a source-only gap of 3.141 m into 1.2–1.4 m for every adapted method while the absolute target error barely moves.** The headline claim ("best in all six settings") is therefore true of the metric and much weaker as a statement about competence in the new domain, and the paper's own reversed-direction and inductive sections show it knows the difference. What we import is a reporting rule the folder has been circling since the denominators lesson in `arxiv-2611.09196`: never print a contrast metric alone, print the two quantities it is a contrast of, because any difference can be improved from either end and only one of them is the thing you claim to care about. The companion discipline here is the prerequisite check that precedes the whole study — the vanilla planners had an image-dependency ratio between −0.32% and −0.60%, meaning the grey-image ablation changed nothing, so the image half of the analysis was measuring a dead channel until the input was rebuilt to make the text shortcut insufficient (three temporal frames, numerical context removed) and the ratio went triple-digit positive on all six cells. Before interpreting which slice carries a signal, establish that the channel is live, and prefer a construction where reliance is forced by the input's information content rather than encouraged by an auxiliary loss — the authors' argument is that regularisation does not remove the sufficient-statistic structure that causes the shortcut in the first place. (arxiv-2611.10720, arxiv-2611.09196, arxiv-2611.08895)
