- Done 2026-11-16 (entry 226): `arxiv-2611.05003` — Unifying and Beyond the Theory of Pervasive Capability Degradation in LLM Post-training SFT from Feature Interference (Hang Chen, Jiaying Zhu, Wenya Wang; NTU + CUHK; arXiv:2611.05003v2, 2026-11-05, arXiv perpetual non-exclusive licence, code at github.com/Zodiark-ch/SFT-Conflict). Full text, 149,144 clean chars incl. Appendices A–I; figures via captions only; inline math stripped by the HTML build, so no symbol values are quoted. **Substance:** full-parameter and PEFT SFT of Mistral-7B, Qwen2.5 3B/7B/32B/72B and Gemma-2-9B on 14 target tasks (8 GLUE + GSM8K + 3 code sets + Evol-Instruct + LogiQA2), with a vocabulary-covering pervasive sample mix (12,110 samples / 85.3% of the Mistral label-token vocabulary; 31,931 / 50.8% of Qwen's) and a held-out 44-benchmark suite (P-Acc.). **Theory:** superposition + narrow data raises the higher-order reconstruction term, forcing correlated features to collapse onto a principal component (a two-feature worked example argues collapse beats orthogonalisation when capacity is short), which leaks a ghost signal into the collapsed channel and pushes activations across the unembedding's Laguerre–Voronoi hyperplanes toward competitors whose features overlap the task's; the weight-level step runs through a *posited* virtual parameterisation with one idealised row per feature (existence proved in Appendix A). Six paradigms (KL anchoring, data mixing, merge orthogonalisation, delta pruning, gradient orthogonalisation, localisation) are re-derived with a specific ceiling each. **AEGIS:** per-competitor normalised margins from a frozen base model give an adaptive tolerance width; during SFT a Huber on (margin drift beyond width) + (any negative margin) is added, with its per-sample strength solved exactly by 1-D bisection and absorbed by the envelope theorem. **Results:** NLU P-Acc. averaged over the eight columns 0.5368 AEGIS vs 0.5271 CLUE / 0.5194 vanilla at Mistral, 0.6596 vs 0.6514 / 0.6454 at Qwen-7B, 0.5617 vs 0.5541 / 0.5479 at Gemma; non-NLU retention 0.3981 vs 0.3860 at Mistral, 0.5924 vs 0.5609 at Qwen, 0.5916 vs 0.5717 at Gemma (one Gemma Evol-Instruct column ties vanilla). **The instrument:** crossed-edge census on Qwen2.5-7B — total crossings and repaired crossings are flat across all seven methods (16.6–16.9 / ~8.6 on RTE) while *new* crossings separate them: AEGIS 4.309 / 3.101 / 1.370 against vanilla 5.700 / 4.373 / 1.941 (RTE / GSM8K / CodeAlpaca), every other method at or above vanilla. Drift table: vanilla's top new MRPC directions are `␣yes`/`␣no`/`yes`/`no` (10,457 crossings), AEGIS has none on MRPC or GSM8K and only `3 4` on CodeAlpaca (27 vs 2,121). Cost 1.26–1.27× vanilla wall-clock at all four Qwen scales, same FLOPs and peak memory. **Limits the entry records:** the feature-collapse step is never measured in a trained model; per-seed spread is omitted while five seeds are claimed; PEFT/continual results are figures only; hyperparameters print blank.
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 226): **Partitioning a behaviour change into inherited and new decision-boundary crossings, and naming the direction each new crossing points toward, separates seven very different interventions far more sharply than any single retention score — here total crossings on the pervasive set are almost identical across all seven methods after SFT (16.6–16.9 per thousand on RTE, repaired crossings pinned at ~8.6) while the neighbouring column, crossings that were correct under the base model and are wrong afterwards, ranges from 4.309 for the margin-constrained loss to 5.700 for vanilla to 5.999 for delta-parameter pruning, and the paper's drift table shows vanilla's new crossings pointing at its own label vocabulary (`␣yes`, `␣no`, `yes`, `no` on MRPC, 10,457 of them) where the constrained arm has none.** The reading rule is that a capability metric and a *change* metric answer different questions and the change metric is the one that can be wrong in a diagnosable way: total accuracy on a retained benchmark mixes the model's pre-existing weaknesses with the damage the intervention did, so an intervention that repairs as much as it breaks can score as neutral, whereas the new-crossing count attributes each error to the training run and to a specific competing token. Two operational points. The census needs three columns, not one — inherited (crossed before and after), new (correct before, crossed after), repaired (the reverse) — because the three behave independently here and only the middle one moves with intervention strength; and the direction column is what converts a count into an explanation, since "activations drifted toward the task's label tokens" is a statement about what the fine-tuning installed, while "retention fell 2 points" is a statement about a score. This is the attribution-level sibling of the folder's decodable-versus-used partition: a margin is a sensitivity, a crossing is a discrete consequence, and only the directed, inherited-versus-new split tells you which side of that line a measurement sits on. (arxiv-2611.05003, arxiv-2610.41185, arxiv-2611.18514)
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 226): **The arm that makes a retention claim interpretable is the one where the baseline reads the same extra data, and this paper is unusual in shipping it — its vanilla arm is fine-tuned on the target set *plus* the same pervasive mixture the method uses as an anchor, so the ~1.5-point NLU retention gain is attributable to the loss and not to the data, and the same table shows the opposite failure in two baselines that never touch general data at all (KnOTS at 0.4878 and DARE at 0.4855 against 0.5194 vanilla at Mistral, i.e. they lose 3.2 and 3.4 points of retention while also dropping target accuracy, which is what a merging-or-pruning step applied to a task-specific delta does when it has nothing to protect).** For any of our own fine-tuning or editing results the discipline is one sentence in the setup: state what the baseline reads. If the baseline sees only the target task and the method adds a general set, the comparison is a data comparison wearing a method comparison's clothes, and the folded version — AEGIS added *on top of* cross-entropy on the pervasive set in the PEFT appendix — is a third, still different, and weaker comparison. A matched-data baseline costs only the same tokens for both arms and is the cheapest way to make a small gain mean something.
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 226): **A derivation is a hypothesis generator, and the tell that a paper has not tested its middle joint is a chain whose first and last links are both measured while the link in between is asserted from a two-feature toy — here the causal story runs superposition → feature collapse → anisotropic displacement → boundary crossing, the last step is measured thoroughly (a per-competitor crossing census with direction labels), the first step is assumed by construction (a posited virtual weight parameterisation, with the idealisation acknowledged in the appendix that proves its properties), and the collapse itself is never observed: no pairwise feature-cosine or dictionary statistic before and after SFT appears anywhere, although the paper's own apparatus — fit a dictionary on cached activations, compute the Gram matrix of the task's correlated group — would produce it in one pass over data it already has.** The general lesson for a predictive white-box model is that the middle links of a mechanism chain are exactly the ones a doctrine of "the derivation predicts the data" lets you skip, so each named entity in the chain should have a cheap direct check attached: if the theory says features merge, print the cosines; if it says the propagation Jacobian is the bottleneck, measure its norm; if it says the tolerance width is load-bearing, run the arm with width zero. Two further delivery facts from this paper belong in the same ledger. The HTML build strips inline math, so three hyperparameter values that the text plainly sets are blank in the version a reader actually gets, and a paper that is otherwise reproducible from its appendix is not reproducible at all from that rendering. And aggregate numbers that appear on no row — this entry's P-Acc. figures — are means computed over per-task columns and must be labelled as such, because a reader who greps for the value will find nothing and a reader who assumes it is a printed row will attribute our arithmetic to the authors. (arxiv-2611.05003, arxiv-2611.14483, arxiv-2610.27375)

- Done 2026-11-16 (entry 225): `arxiv-2610.27375` — Shaped SAEs: Expanding the Toolkit for Mechanistic Interpretability (Oveys Delafrooz Noroozi, Bhagyashree Puranik, Upamanyu Madhow; University of California, Santa Barbara; arXiv:2610.27375v1, 2026-10-19, arXiv.org perpetual non-exclusive licence). Full text, 55,344 clean chars incl. Appendices A–E; **figures read via captions only**, so every number is a Table 1 cell or an explicit sentence. **Substance:** two independent contributions on Gemma-2-2B layers 12 and 20 (d = 2304) plus GPT-2 Small layers 7–8, 16K and 32K dictionaries, k ∈ {40, 80, 160, 320, 640}, 7,000 steps / ~28.7M tokens of uncopyrighted Pile, AdamW 2e-4, λ = 0.01. **Shaping:** rank-r projection of the residual stream onto the top-r right singular vectors of the corpus-averaged Jacobian (1,000 prompts × 64 tokens, final block as target), r = 1536 default with r ∈ {768, 1152, 1536, 1792} swept; **dictionary:** MF-SAE — learned affine encoder to a latent, rectified inner products with unit-norm atoms as matched filters, top-k selection, reconstruction from the *same* atoms, learned affine decoder; selection detached, coefficient recomputed differentiably, cost equal to a TopK SAE of the same width. **The result that matters:** shaping *without* an SAE beats raw coordinates on SAEBench at both layers and every r and is comparable (layer 12) to slightly better (layer 20) on SAE Probes, but **once a dictionary is fitted the gain nearly disappears** — raw and live MF-SAE match in most SAEBench panels (live better in exactly one, layer 12 at k = 80) and SAE Probes gains are only marginal. Both MF-SAEs beat SAEBench TopK, Gemma Scope JumpReLU (nearest-L0 pairing) and a 32K Matryoshka at layers 12 and 20. **Reconstruction table:** raw MF-SAE PVE 0.86–0.92 recovering 97–99% of CE; live MF-SAE PVE 0.79–0.86 on its own input, 89–94% CE alone, **projection-only already 92–95%**, live+quiet 99% in every cell — so the shortfall is the discarded subspace, not sparse coding. Alive atoms 81–99% live against 62–89% raw with no dead-latent machinery; removing the linear projections significantly hurts probing in both arms, which matches the paper's tying argument (TopK's free encoder rows and decoder columns absorb outer linear maps; the MF-SAE's tied atoms leave the maps as the only encoder/decoder asymmetry). **Limits it names:** combining shaping with the dictionary works only at tight budgets; the live/quiet split rests on a decaying Jacobian spectrum that is not analysed, quiet space flagged as future work; live PVE not comparable to raw PVE. **Relevance 3** because the raw-versus-live-no-SAE arm is a free confound check for any preprocessing claim in our own pipeline, and the three-way patch (reconstruction / reconstruction+quiet / projection alone) separates dictionary loss from input-transform loss in two forward passes.

- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 225): **A preprocessing step that demonstrably helps the coordinates can stop helping once a learner is downstream, because a dictionary fitted to the raw space was already free to find an equivalent projection — here shaping the residual stream onto the top 1,536 singular directions of the averaged Jacobian beats raw coordinates on SAEBench at both layers and every r tested and matches or beats them on SAE Probes, yet after an SAE is trained the raw and shaped dictionaries are indistinguishable in most panels, with the shaped arm better in exactly one (layer 12, k = 80) and the 113-dataset benchmark showing only marginal gains.** The numbers that make it a measurement rather than a hedge are in the reconstruction table: the shaped SAE recovers 89–94% of CE, but the *projection alone with no SAE at all* already recovers 92–95%, and restoring the discarded quiet residual returns 99% — so the entire apparent cost of the shaped dictionary is the subspace that was thrown away before any learning happened. Two habits follow, and the first is one extra logistic regression. Any claim of the form "our transform/whitening/projection makes features more semantic" ships with the no-learner arm run on the transformed input, because a dictionary is a universal-enough approximator that it can absorb a linear change of coordinates and the gain will silently migrate from the transform to the dictionary; when both arms are reported and the gap closes, the honest conclusion is about the *interaction* being absent, not about the transform failing. The second is the three-way patch — replace the activation with the reconstruction, with the reconstruction plus the discarded component restored, and with the discarded component alone — which costs two extra forward passes, needs no retraining, and separates "my dictionary loses information" from "my input transform loses information", a distinction this folder's reconstruction-scored entries routinely collapse. (arxiv-2610.27375, arxiv-2611.09233, arxiv-2611.00420)
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 225): **Tying the encoder and decoder to the same unit-norm atoms turns a redundant knob into a load-bearing one, and the algebra that says so is worth more than the benchmark delta — in a TopK SAE an outer linear map can be absorbed into the free encoder rows and decoder columns and is therefore a no-op, whereas the matched-filter formulation ties encoder and decoder up to one shared learned map G = W_e^T W_d^-1 so the maps are the only mechanism that lets encoding differ from decoding, and removing them significantly degrades probing in both the raw and shaped arms.** That is the useful form of an architectural claim: not "our block is better" but "here is a parameterisation in which a knob we removed actually does work", which is testable in one ablation and falsifiable in the direction the paper reports. The second property worth stealing is dead-atom behaviour without machinery — 81–99% of the shaped dictionary alive against 62–89% raw, with no dead-latent auxiliary loss, no resampling, no threshold finagling — because the folder's dictionary entries keep paying for coverage through extra loss terms and thresholds that then bias inference-time behaviour, and this suggests the familiar TopK failure mode is partly an artefact of free per-atom encoder norms and biases letting an atom win selection independently of whether it matches. The measurement caution is the mirror image: this paper reports no confidence intervals anywhere and its headline comparison exists only as a multi-panel figure, so "consistently better in one of four panels" is the strongest statement its evidence supports, and a liveness advantage of 20–30 points on a single corpus is a claim about coverage that no downstream task in the paper tests. (arxiv-2610.27375, arxiv-2611.09233, arxiv-2611.00640)
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 225): **The cheapest defence against reporting someone else's paper a second time is to run the duplicate check on the discovery channel's *own output*, before any fetch, and to make the check two-part — a file existence test plus a first-field INDEX match in both folders — because this run wrote and nearly committed a full 12k-byte duplicate entry for a paper that had been entry 216 fourteen hours earlier.** The mechanism is worth naming precisely, because nothing about it was a judgement error: my freeness script printed `FREE` for all forty sweep results, and my manual verification covered only the five ids I had carried in from the previous run's notes. A carry list is a list of *candidates*, and candidates from the carry list are the ones most likely to be already-held; fresh sweep ids are precisely the ones whose freeness nobody has checked. Three concrete rules follow. Run the check as `test -f aether/<id>.md || test -f core/<id>.md` **and** `grep -c '^<id> |'` on **both** INDEX files, and treat any nonzero from either as held — the first-field anchor matters because raw substring greps hit Pattern-line citations (run 213's trap) while a bare file test misses an id that is in INDEX without a file (run 206's trap). Do it before the fetch, not after the read, because a full read is the expensive part and it is exactly what tempts you to keep the result. And when the sweep helper's verdict and the manual verdict disagree, the manual one wins and the helper is broken until proven otherwise — this run's helper resolved paths relative to a directory it had already left, so every `os.path.exists` returned False and the script was structurally incapable of saying anything but free. The general form: a script that can only ever produce one answer is not a check, and the tell is a sweep in which nothing is ever held. (arxiv-2610.27375, arxiv-2610.27393, arxiv-2611.18652)

- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 224): **Run the mechanism against a linear operator with the same read range, because that arm answers the question the mechanism is supposed to answer and here it wins — a blur of the layer input at λ = 0.9 beats a 2^18-rule search's chosen automaton on clean accuracy (0.981 vs 0.962), map smoothness (LFPR 0.967 vs 0.941), early-layer readability by the final classifier (75.9 vs 57.5) and scale separation (18.8 vs 18.2, both at the ceiling), so four of the six properties in the abstract belong to "regulate the output by the input" and only three survive as rule-specific.** The three that survive are named by the paper and are worth the list as a template: object-localised saliency (+1.13 against +0.37 to +0.48 for the blurs), agreement across seeds that is *learned* rather than inherited (0.11 untrained → 0.83 trained, where a blur strong enough to reach 0.97 already sits at 0.74 untrained), and an input-dependent gain 8.5× larger on strokes than off them (0.262 vs 0.031) where the blur scales every unit by the same 1 − λ. The transferable part is the discipline of building the rival *inside* the same wiring — same input read, same output blend, only the nonlinearity replaced — so the comparison isolates the one thing that differs instead of confounding architecture, capacity and supervision the way cross-method ladders in this folder so often do. Two subsidiary lessons. A summary score can certify a mechanism whose pictures refute it: Day & Night ties B5/S3 on both smoothness and entropy (0.95 vs 0.94, 0.37 vs 0.33) while its trained maps saturate the field into a uniform blob that no longer carries the input, which is why the authors kept the qualitative check alongside the number. And when a comparison is made at matched clean accuracy, the matching itself has to be defended: the plain arm's noise robustness improves through training while the regulated arm's decays, the curves cross, and so "matched accuracy" silently selects an early plain network against a late regulated one — the complementary equal-budget comparison is not optional here but the other half of the result. (arxiv-2611.10760, arxiv-2611.09233, arxiv-2610.41185)
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 224): **Cross-seed agreement is meaningless without the untrained-init arm, and the pair of numbers is what separates a constraint that made learning reproducible from one that merely imposed its layout at step zero — here the winning rule moves deep-layer agreement from 0.11 to 0.83 while the strongest rival moves 0.74 to 0.97, and the plain network sits at ≈0 despite linear CKA 0.89–0.97, so the same information in a different basis scores as total disagreement.** Three readings follow. A high trained agreement with an equally high untrained agreement is *inheritance*: the constraint has put a coarse structure in place before any gradient arrived, which is a legitimate result about the design and not a result about what training found — the paper's own depth-resolved version says as much, with early coarse agreement (wavelengths above ≈6 px) inherited and deep-layer agreement learned. A high trained agreement with a low untrained one is the interesting case, and it is the only shape that supports "this constraint makes the trained function reproducible", which is why the Ly–Gong churn protocol is the better instrument: perturbing two initialisations by ε from 1e-1 down to 1e-8 and plotting where the disagreement stops shrinking measures reproducibility *of the trained function* directly, and gives 0.03–0.14% against 2.3–3.1% here with no inference about inheritance at all. And per-unit correlation and CKA are not alternatives but complements — unit-wise 0 versus CKA 0.89–0.97 on the same model is the cleanest statement in this folder that a basis-free similarity score cannot support any claim about which unit computes what, while a unit-wise score cannot support a claim about the information present. For our battery: any "our representation is stable" claim ships with the untrained arm, the per-unit and the basis-free score, and, where it is available, the ε-churn curve. (arxiv-2611.10760, arxiv-2611.10400, arxiv-2611.13885)
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 224): **A saliency map can be entirely the derivative of the intervention that produced it, and the one gradient-free test that separates the two is matching pixel counts on versus off an object mask — the MLP here shows digit-shaped maps whose input gradient vanishes to 4e-13 once the rule's route is detached, and whose accuracy drops *more* when the background is noised (79.8%) than when as many object pixels are (85.3%), while the CNN with the same rule passes at 60.5% versus 96.3% and its plain counterpart is reversed at 74.4% versus 67.0%.** The mechanism of the failure is worth knowing because it is architectural rather than a bug: the rule's input route is largest wherever the occupancy sits near a band edge, which on a black background is exactly the strokes, so any network whose gradients travel mainly through that route will paint the object whether or not it uses it. Two further calibrations the paper supplies. A surrogate gradient through statistics held fixed changed the *magnitudes* of the saliency map by a median 48–75% but its per-image ranking barely at all (Spearman 0.95–0.97) and its localisation not at all (+0.54 to +0.95 log-ratio, 91–100% of images), which is the honest bound to quote when a surrogate is used for ordering claims rather than size claims. And the sanity check every normalising layer should carry: at vanishing contrast (a constant grey image) the gates go to zero, every first-layer unit sits at −1, every image is assigned the same class with probability 1.00, and the input gradient grows as 1/a — a confident output for an input with no content, invisible to a noise benchmark that never lowers contrast. Read beside this folder's decodability-versus-use partition, this is the attribution-level member of the family: a map is a statement about sensitivity, reliance is a statement about what removing content costs, and only the mask-matched noising test tells you which one you measured. (arxiv-2611.10760, arxiv-2611.10400, arxiv-2611.18514)
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 224): **What fraction of *learning* flows through a chosen mechanism is a measurable quantity that almost nobody reports, and the instrument is one extra backward pass — recompute each weight gradient twice, once with the mechanism's path detached, and the ratio is that mechanism's share of the learning signal: below 0.2% in MLP layers 1–7, about 1% in layer 8 and 14% in layer 9, 0.02–4% in the trained WRN against 30–86% at its initialisation, and about 5% for the CNN's one steerable gate.** The reading is subtle enough to be worth stating: a *fixed* rule that cannot be optimised still shapes training because its values scale every weight gradient in its layer and its slopes carry error to the layers below, so "the parameters are frozen" is compatible with "nearly all the learning goes through the path they gate" — which is exactly what the WRN shows, moving from a minority to almost a total share as it trains. The consequence for a predictive white-box model is a distinction we do not currently draw: a component can be irrelevant at inference and load-bearing during training, and an ablation panel will never see it. The paired retrain makes the point sharper still — cutting the gate routes costs the MLP nothing measurable in accuracy (94.1% against 96.0%) and half its scale separation, changes the CNN not at all, and leaves the WRN unable to fit its training set (final loss 0.49 against 0.05), purely because SGD steps scale with the gradient where Adam's do not, so the same architectural change reads as negligible or fatal depending on the optimiser. The general form: report the detached-gradient share alongside every inference-time ablation, and state the optimiser, because the two arms' sensitivity to a shrunken gradient is an optimiser property, not a property of the mechanism. (arxiv-2611.10760, arxiv-2610.41185, arxiv-2611.00640)

- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 223): **A capacity constraint imposed uniformly across sites is a template artefact until someone plots the residual against the site, and the test costs one training run — here the "k latents in every layer" rule inherited from SAE practice is wrong by a factor of fifteen across depth, because per-layer FVU runs 5–12% in the first layers, above 40% in layers 15–19 and under 4% at layer 36, so an equal budget is starved where reconstruction is hard and wasteful where it is trivial.** The published numbers are deliberately unimpressive and that is the point: pooling the whole budget and letting the model allocate it buys 0.57 points of average FVU (27.64 → 27.07) and 0.04 of graph replacement score, while 27 of 36 layers improve and the nine that worsen are exactly the nine the reallocation withdrew from. Two habits are worth generalising past dictionaries. First, the uniform-budget arm is the *control that tells you whether the degree of freedom matters at all* — run it once, plot per-site error, and if the profile is flat the pooled version cannot help, whereas if it varies by a factor this large the template is the thing being measured. Second, a reallocation is a trade and must be tabulated per site rather than averaged: quoting the average alone would have hidden that the mechanism works by moving budget from the last layers to the middle, which is a claim about where an LLM's depth is doing work and is only visible in a per-layer column. The reading rule for our own write-ups: whenever we claim a measurement at k sites with a shared constraint, print the per-site profile and the correlation between the resource a site received and the error it had before — here r = 0.85, which is what "the model learned the right thing" actually looks like. (arxiv-2611.09233, arxiv-2611.00420, arxiv-2611.00640)
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 223): **Every reconstruction comparison in this literature is a comparison between four arms that achieve four different sparsities, and the achieved number is the one that decides the verdict — JumpReLU is scored at 452 active latents while its target was 360 and loses to a 360-latent arm, Cross-Layer BatchTopK wins at training (26.98%) and loses after its thresholds are calibrated (29.04%), and both reversals are explained in a column the main table already has.** The lesson is that the ladder has three rungs and only one is the headline. A penalty-based method cannot report a comparison at a target it did not reach, so the achieved L0 has to be a printed column, not a footnote, and the same is true of dead latents: 41.2% against 3.0–3.2% means JumpReLU's nominal budget is concentrated in a third of the dictionary, which turns a reconstruction comparison into a coverage comparison nobody labelled. The train-versus-inference gap is the second, more transferable half — a selection rule that depends on what else is in the batch (BatchTopK, mutual choice, and by extension any batch-dependent probe threshold or ablation baseline) has to be re-measured on single inputs, and the paper's own diagnosis, that thresholds are estimated from the batches where a bursty latent fired most and are therefore biased against rare latents, is the mechanism to look for whenever a method looks better in training than in serving. For us the rule is: any comparison across arms prints achieved budget, dead fraction and evaluation regime side by side, or the differences between arms are differences between those three columns wearing the name of an architecture. (arxiv-2611.09233, arxiv-2611.07283, arxiv-2611.01513)
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 223): **A completeness score of 0.90 is a statement that a tenth of the influence at the nodes that matter is unexplained, and the two graph scores in this literature disagree about that residual in a way worth printing separately — replacement 0.617 requires an unbroken error-free path end to end and therefore punishes it fully, while completeness 0.902 grants partial credit node by node, so the gap between them is roughly a measure of how much of the computation is nearly-but-not-quite inside the dictionary.** That gap is why the two must travel together: a single "our circuits are 90% complete" sentence is true under one definition and false under the other, and the difference is the same one this folder keeps meeting between an influence routed through features and a feature that is actually doing the work. Two further constraints the paper's setup makes explicit and ours should too. The evaluation set is 100 prompts after a four-way filter (greedy agreement with the ground truth, target rarer than 10⁻⁴ unigrams, target not already present, cross-entropy above 0.2), which means every completeness number is conditional on prompts the model found non-trivial, not on the deployable distribution. And the claim that better reconstruction yields better circuits is established here by an ordering across four architectures, not by an ablation on one — which is the weaker design, because the arms also differ in achieved budget and in activation function, so the causal story (features carry more of the influence because the dictionary fits better) remains a plausible reading of a confounded ladder rather than a measurement. (arxiv-2611.09233, arxiv-2611.00420, arxiv-2610.41185)

- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 222): **A feature's name and the direction in which clamping it acts can be oppositely oriented, and the tell is that a supervised probe fitted to the same labels shows the identical inversion — so the probe does not adjudicate between "the interpretation is wrong" and "the encoding runs backwards", it only inherits whichever one is true.** The numbers: on π0.5 every predicting direction for a decision is anti-aligned with the action gradient taken through the flow sampler — nine named basis features at held-out precision 0.906–0.990, the summed direction of four feature families, and four label-fitted probes — at cosines −0.08 to −0.26; 14 of the 20 features most aligned with that gradient carry the *opposite* axis label at precision 0.04–0.37, and clamping one raises the share of steps along +x from 0.36 to 1.00 while task success falls from 1.00 to 0.00. The reason this matters for us rather than being a quirky model is the verification rule it forces: a name is a statement about co-occurrence and a clamp is a statement about cause, and the two are separate measurements that can each be right while disagreeing in sign, which is why the honest protocol reports the cosine between the feature and the causal direction rather than either alone. Two consequences. A precision floor set on prediction is *not* a validity floor on intervention — the causally effective features here were the ones the naming rule rejected — so a battery that only clamps features that cleared a high precision threshold is systematically blind to the directions that actually carry the computation. And when the clamp fires with an unexpected sign, the first hypothesis to test is a sign convention in the readout (here an action that was already decided, gradient pointing back toward the origin), not a bad name; that test is free because the probe arm is already in the table. (arxiv-2611.10400, arxiv-2611.00298, arxiv-2610.41185)
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 222): **An explanation can be highly faithful to its own record and barely right about the world, and the two numbers measure different objects — here 85–89% of the language model's answers match the concept record it was given, its top responsible concept stays in the top three across a median 90–95% of twenty bootstrap refits, 11 of 12 successes are called normal, and yet the failure *category* is correct in only 15 of 48 OpenVLA failures, about a third on π0.5, and 3 of 8 on the robot, every one of which ties a mechanical rule reading the same record.** The diagnostic value is in the comparison: the mechanical rule is what makes the faithfulness figure interpretable, because a generated note that agrees with a deterministic read of its input has demonstrated a faithful renderer and nothing about whether the record spans the failure. This is the same separation the folder keeps meeting on the probe side (predictive yet idle, decodable yet unused) moved one level up to the text: the explanation is a function of the features, so its correctness is capped by the vocabulary, and the paper says as much — the phases separating the failure types are simply not in the 74-concept set. The reporting rule is three columns on every diagnosis result: agreement with the record, stability across refits, and agreement of the *category* with ground truth against a mechanical-rule baseline. A fourth is cheap and this paper models it: put the responsible concept next to the concept that should have fired and did not, since "the gripper-closed feature never came on" is a stronger statement about the network than any ranking of what did. (arxiv-2611.10400, arxiv-2611.00420, arxiv-2611.18514)
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 222): **Naming a dictionary's features becomes a measurement rather than a human's judgement only when three things are fixed before the activations are inspected — the concept vocabulary, the firing level, and the precision floor — and the held-out re-test is what makes the baseline zeros mean anything.** The procedure here is short enough to copy verbatim: fix the concept list (states such as near/grasped/lifted and decisions such as the sign of each action axis) before looking at activations; fire at τ times the feature's maximum for τ in a small fixed set; compute precision and recall of each (concept, level) pair against labels; keep pairs with precision at or above a floor, recall above a low floor and a minimum firing count; take the highest-recall survivor as the name; then freeze the name *and its level* and re-test on episodes that took no part in choosing it, requiring firings spread over several episodes with no episode dominating. The payoff is that every baseline falls through the same sieve, so "raw coordinates name 13–16 concepts, random directions 8–11, neurons and an untrained dictionary none" is a comparable result rather than a different experiment, and the two-random-start figure (81–83% of names shared, 73% under the same name) becomes a per-name stability statistic instead of a global fidelity score. Two cautions the paper's own tables supply. The lead comes almost entirely from *state* concepts (9–10 against 4 on LingBot-VLA) while raw coordinates nearly match on decisions, because an action expert's coordinates already track the action it writes — so an unconvincing win on half the vocabulary is a signal about where the dictionary is actually adding information. And the rule certifies a name only where the quantity is not already in the input: at the first denoising step, whose input is noise, the dictionary names nothing and raw coordinates name four, which is the cleanest available demonstration that what an SAE "discovers" can be a property of the site as much as of the model. (arxiv-2611.10400, arxiv-2611.01513, arxiv-2611.07283)

**54/66** across all 11 models (aphasia 22/22, Broca 15/22, Wernicke 17/22); experts agree with the classifier on 90% of lesioned answers. **Prompt-site patching**: restore-all undoes 53/54 lesions (exception Pythia-6.9B L1H26, a one-head lesion), a single restore undoes the median lesion at 83% of its heads but produces **80% model scrambles against 13% control speech**, restore-all repairs 22 of 40; matched-norm random directions undo 91% against the own direction's 95%. - Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 221): **Reaching a target and carrying it to a new input are two different achievements, and this paper's separating experiment is six held-out prompts — here 51 head sets that make a lesion, 38 by the classifier's own >0.5 threshold, hit their targeted aphasia type in 1 of 184 scored answers on the other narrative and the Text Aphasia Battery, while a single mean-difference direction hits it in 67 of 153, and two human experts independently label 65% of the Broca and 63% of the Wernicke non-scramble answers on prompts that played no part in choosing the layer or strength.** The mechanism behind the gap is the one this folder keeps meeting from the ablation side: a head set selected by greedy growth and pruning *is* a long list of component contributions, and removing a list of contributions damages the output in ways nobody predicted, whereas a direction is one constraint removed and the model improvises along the remaining degrees of freedom. Three reporting rules follow, and the first is a column rather than a paragraph. Print the intervention's hit rate on the inputs used to select it and on inputs that were never used, because the selection step alone can manufacture the first number. Print the *class* of the failure produced, not just the fact of one, since 80% of this paper's single-head restores that clear the aphasic label produce tokenizer-loop machine scrambles instead of healthy speech — a "repair" that is a failure of a different kind, and a count of repairs would have scored it as success. And when a structural and a representational intervention are compared, do not read agreement between them as mutual confirmation: the lesion and the direction agree that aphasia-like speech is reachable and disagree about everything downstream of that, which is what one would expect if the direction is the target's *address* and the head set is a *route* to it. (arxiv-2610.28992, arxiv-2611.18514, arxiv-2611.00298)
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 221): **A family of distinguished conditions is usually one shared direction plus a small residual, and the test for "these two are different" should be run twice — once pooled and once after projecting the shared direction out — because the residual can improve one condition's reach while destroying the other's, which is exactly what happened here: Broca and Wernicke lesion pairs share a median 54% of the smaller set's heads (517 against 165 expected, 11 of 13 pairs p < 0.01), their summary vectors sit at median cosine 0.79–0.90 against 0.97–0.99 for label-shuffled controls while still falling below the 2.5th percentile of that null at 670 of 672 layers, and after removing the direction pooled over all aphasic speech the Wernicke-specific vector goes from working at 25 of 176 layers to 94 — including all ten model-task pairs where the pooled Wernicke vector never reached the target — while the Broca-specific vector drops from 78 to 29.** Both numbers are needed to interpret the pair, and the asymmetry is a finding the pooled comparison could not have produced. The null is the second half of the method: shuffling the two labels among transcripts of both conditions with group sizes preserved gives a distribution of cosines against which "the two types are alike" becomes measurable, and the honest verdict here is that they are *distinguishable* from chance and *nearly identical in magnitude* — which is a much sharper statement than either "separate circuits" or "entangled". For us this converts the folder's recurring modulated-versus-carried question into arithmetic: an embedding or direction that recovers two conditions at high AUC may be recovering one common factor twice, and the diagnostics are a shared-component projection, a label-shuffle null, and the effect of the residual on each condition separately. The complementary warning is that the shared machinery can dominate the shared *explanation* — 517 shared heads that, knocked out together, reach the target on neither task, because sharing a set is not the same as either set working. (arxiv-2610.28992, arxiv-2611.13885, arxiv-2611.15735)
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 221): **A leave-one-out panel run on a greedily selected set re-executes the selection rule instead of testing the set, and the tell is that the search's stopping criterion and the leave-one-out criterion are the same number — this paper's growth stops at the first prefix above 0.5 and its pruning stops when one more removal would drop below, so leaving out any single head undoes the lesion in 37 of 54 sets and 4,484 of 4,600 heads look indispensable, and the authors state flatly that the statistic checks the search rather than revealing how the heads work.** Their own decomposition makes the point quantitative: by the answer-level definition every head is needed in only 37 of the 47 pruned sets, and the only sets where the test adds information are the seven whose pruning never finished — 91 to 99% of heads needed there, which is a real measurement. The remedy is not to drop the test but to run it on a set the search did not tune to that boundary: sample the set from a fixed rule (top-k by a held-out score, or a contiguous layer window), or report the whole effect-versus-size curve so the set is a point on it rather than a threshold artefact. This is the folder's fourth instance of a control testing itself — a thresholded battery that grows with sample size, a random arm at unmatched norm, an ablation map read as a route map — and it has the same fix: name the selection rule, then choose a statistic the rule cannot satisfy by construction. The corollary worth carrying into our write-ups is that "which components are necessary" is a question about the *measurement's* threshold as much as about the network, so the same experiment with a 0.6 threshold would return a different set of necessary heads and neither set would be wrong. (arxiv-2610.28992, arxiv-2611.13885, arxiv-2611.00640)

- Done 2026-11-16 (entry 215): `arxiv-2611.14483` — Mechanistic Interpretability Needs a Logic of Inference (Zhimin Hu, Chen Jiang, Hanbo Xie, N. Apurva Ratan Murty, Sashank Varma; Georgia Tech psychology/neuroscience, Ratan Murty also Emory; arXiv:2611.14483v1, 2026-11-10, NeurIPS 2026 Interp4Discovery Oral, acknowledges Guillaume Lajoie). **Full text, 39k clean chars, nothing unread; position paper so there are no numbers, baselines or ablations anywhere** — every claim in the entry is a cited result or the authors' own argued distinction, and this is stated in the entry's `How they judged success` rather than dressed up as a measurement. **Substance:** five principles hung off a measurement condition, each carrying a worked example where one observation licenses one claim and not the next. P0: patching results vary with corruption procedure and metric, saliency structure can be weakly tied to computation — measurement is part of the evidence. P1: population activity keeps a task variable after individually selective units are excluded, and unit selectivity poorly predicts downstream performance, **but** causally-effective interpretable units exist, so the level is a hypothesis testable in both directions rather than a default. P2: decodable is not used; probing accuracy need not track behavioural importance. P3: zebra-finch **acute silencing disrupts song while a permanent lesion gives only a transient deficit that recovers**; attention-head ablation is followed by input-varying downstream self-repair — so an effect is target-plus-response, and a role claim needs predictions about where/when and which downstream quantities move. P4: **unilateral ALM silencing in the delay period recovers, bilateral does not**, separating redundant maintenance from local recurrence and from inter-hemispheric coupling in two perturbations instead of one. P5: circuit-level algorithms hold across training/task/scale while the components change, and SAEs can be per-feature unstable while their subspaces reproduce, so the explanatory object may have to be revisited. **Named limit, twice:** evidence beyond the models is required, and mechanisms are hypothesis generators, not domain findings. **Limits the paper does not name:** nothing is operationalised (no threshold, no worked case where the framework reverses a published conclusion) and the recursion is not a schedule, so it never fixes how much of the chain a claim must walk. **Why relevance 3:** the folder had 214 empirical dissociations and no entry that supplies their common vocabulary; this one turns the recurring mistake into a *skipped question*, which is checkable at write-up.
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 215): **The folder's recurring failure mode is not a wrong measurement but a skipped inferential step, and once the steps are named the check becomes a one-line audit performed at write-up — an object claim (is this level even the right one, testable by asking whether the adjacent level is also sufficient), a use claim (present versus read out), a role claim (dependence versus what the component computes), an organisation claim (how the several roles relate), and an invariance claim (does any of it survive a change of seed, scale or implementation).** Across 214 entries the same shape recurs in different clothes: a probe with high held-out AUC on a variable the model does not need, a head that is perfectly decodable and fully compensated after ablation, a feature that reorganises a manifold without moving a decision, an ablation that localises a span while leaving the property unfound, a group that zero-ablates at 0.27 against 0.00 for random neurons yet is replaceable by its own values from other questions with an effect of 0.00. Each of those is a paper reporting an object-level result and being read — by itself or by its readers — as a role-level or organisation-level one, and in every case the evidence supports only the earlier step. What changes for a predictive white-box model is that the audit is free: we do not need a new experiment to ask which of the five claims a result establishes, only a fixed sentence in each results block naming the claim and what it leaves open, with the default being the weakest. The corollary is a priority rule — an entry that establishes two adjacent claims on the same object is worth more than one that establishes the same claim twice on new models, and our own battery should be trimmed toward the joints between steps rather than toward more objects. (arxiv-2611.14483, arxiv-2611.18514, arxiv-2611.13885)
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 215): **A redundancy claim and a coupling claim predict the same thing under a single ablation, and separating them costs exactly one extra perturbation — suppress one part and ask whether the quantity recovers, then suppress both and ask again; recovery after the first with failure after the second means the parts are partially redundant and coupled, while no recovery after the first means the computation is local and a persistent deficit after the second adds nothing.** The worked case is the mouse anterior lateral motor cortex during a delayed response: silencing one hemisphere displaces the preparatory population but the pattern comes back, while bilateral silencing leaves it unrecovered by the end of the delay, which rules out a single local recurrent store and supports two selectively coupled modules either of which can maintain the state. The ANN companion is the same logic in the opposite direction — after heads are ablated, downstream components compensate by an amount that varies with the input — which is why a single ablation's effect size should never be read as a component's weight. For this folder the recipe is directly usable on the two structures we already test singly: the content-matched control (write in the values another input produces) establishes that a group is not a constant gate, and ablating that group together with its nearest candidate backup establishes whether the gate is *one* gate or a redundant pair — two interventions per claim, on activations we already have cached. The general form worth carrying: any claim of the shape "component X does the work" has a competing account of the shape "X and its neighbour both do, and either suffices", and no single-site measurement can distinguish them because both predict a deficit. (arxiv-2611.14483, arxiv-2611.13885, arxiv-2611.00298)
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 215): **An invariance claim is a separate experiment from an organisation claim and fails more often than papers expect, because the level that survives a change of seed or scale is usually not the level at which the analysis started — circuit-level algorithms persist across training, task and model scale while the specific components implementing them change, and independently trained dictionaries can have unstable individual features sitting inside reproducible subspaces.** Two habits follow. First, cross-seed and cross-scale replication should be run on the *description* rather than on the components: report whether the abstract account holds, not whether the same indices light up, because reporting the second when the first is what the field supports produces failures that look like disconfirmation and are actually a measurement of implementation-specific detail. Second, when a cross-check does fail at the component level, the correct next move is the paper's recursion — revisit whether the explanatory object was pitched at the right granularity — rather than declaring the mechanism absent, and this folder has already seen both readings on the same object with the redundancy literature on one side and the transfer literature on the other. The reusable instrument is not new: it is the ordinary held-out replication, pointed at the right quantity. What this paper adds is the ordering constraint, which matters for how we phrase a result — an organisation that replicates across implementations is a stronger claim than an identity that replicates on one, and a mechanism is not established until somebody has said which of the two they mean. (arxiv-2611.14483, arxiv-2611.00420, arxiv-2610.41185)

- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 214): **A direction can be 0.80 AUC predictive and 85% corrective while the mechanism behind it is 8.9% — and the third number is the one that decides whether you call it an explanation, so all three belong in the same table.** The numbers here: a linear probe on the pre-generation residual predicts web-element hallucination at 0.80 held-out AUC before any output token exists; steering along the probe weight fixes 85.4% of hallucinations at a 7.0% break rate; and the best cell in a large grid of attention-head and FFN interventions — amplifying every head at layer 22 while halving three FFNs — fixes 8.9%. This is the folder's decodability/controllability/use partition arriving in its most legible form, because all three readings are on the same model, the same task and the same item set, so the divergence cannot be blamed on a change of dataset. The consequence for a predictive white-box model is a reporting rule rather than a new method: a probe's AUC and a steering vector's fix rate are both *about the direction*, not about the network, and a probe that has been shown causal by steering still tells you nothing about *which computation* produced the state it reads. The corollary is that steering success is a lower bar than the folder tends to treat it as — it establishes that the direction is upstream, which is compatible with the direction being a read-out of a decision already made elsewhere, exactly the reading the authors adopt when they say the commitment is present before generation begins.
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 214): **How to tell an intervention is producing the wrong kind of failure — induced failures here are syntactically broken while natural ones are well-formed and merely ungrounded, so amplifying a layer-15 FFN yields a selector ending in a long numeric suffix rather than a plausible nonexistent element like a search box that is not on the page.** That qualitative check is worth more than a fix/break rate on its own, because a failure count treats both as the target behaviour and the repair inferred from the synthetic one would be aimed at a garbage-token problem. The same organ is what makes the grid legible: the configurations that reach 100% fix do it while breaking 100% of valid actions, so the surface being optimised is *validity of the generated selector string* rather than *grounding in the page*, and the paper says so instead of quoting the fix column. Two habits follow. Score failures by class and report the class mix before and after, since a method that converts well-formed-but-wrong into malformed has not improved anything a deployment would notice; and check whether the intervention's own scale is doing the work, which here is unmistakable in the sweep — 0.0% fix at the magnitude one step above the peak, with 96.9% of valid actions broken, i.e. the effect has a window and outside it the intervention is not steering but corrupting. Read beside the folder's admissible-region and answer-mass guards, this is the cheapest version of the same instrument: a coarse label on the *text* of the output, no gradients and no second model.
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 214): **When an input span is present twice — once in the current prompt and once in the running history — corrupting the current copy does nothing for the cases that re-echo it, so an ablation's hit rate becomes a measure of duplication rather than of causal weight.** Here corrupting the action list changes the decision only where the list was the sole source; in roughly half of valid steps the agent had already emitted the same selector value earlier in the trajectory and recovers it from history, and the same asymmetry shows up at the trajectory level, where the best-matched counterfactual (deleting the chosen valid action) yields the target failure in only 38% of cases and the two runs agree on the selector about a quarter of the time by the next step. Three consequences. A null ablation result should first be checked against a *redundancy census* — how often the ablated span's content appears elsewhere in the context — before it is read as "this input does not matter", which is the same rule this folder already applies to components in the form of content-matched controls, moved one level up to positions. A stateful setting also makes the matched-counterfactual demand close to unsatisfiable by construction rather than by negligence: the counterpart of a patching pair would have to share page, task, URL and history, and no two trajectories do, which is why the honest report is a divergence statistic (Jaccard on resulting pages, agreement on the next choice) rather than a patched effect. And the fix that suggests itself is the folder's existing mean-ablation logic applied to history: substitute the same span from a different step rather than noise, so the substituted content is in-distribution and the ablated copy is not recoverable. - Done 2026-11-16 (entry 213): `arxiv-2611.00298` — A Framework for Task-Agnostic Counterfactual Fairness in Transformers through Activation Steering (Joshua Wolff Anderson, Yanshan Wang, Shyam Visweswaran; University of Pittsburgh, Dept. of Biomedical Informatics; arXiv:2611.00298v1, 2026-10-30, CC BY 4.0). Full text, 60,571 clean chars in three windows, Figures 1–2 not inspected. **Substance:** the MICF pipeline on **TabPFN v2** (192-d embedding, 12 layers, two-way attention over features then rows, in-context) on UTICalc (1,686 children, 7 binary predictors) and COMPAS (6,172 defendants, 6 features), race binarised. **Stage 1** builds factual–counterfactual pairs two ways — `flip` (race alone, propagation deliberately ignored) and `LLM` (local llama3:8b-instruct via Ollama, schema-validated JSON, ≤5 self-consistency iterations, no causal rules given, then filtered to zero violations of a LiNGAM-estimated graph) — with PC-CVR 0.319 / 0.228 and 271 / 2,853 pairs retained. **Stage 2** zeroes each layer's output projection in turn and records the fraction of the fairness score removed: **1.3% at layer 9, 1.6% at layer 10**, 0.01% at layer 0, ~1.2e-5% at layer 11, 0.1–0.4% elsewhere. **Stage 3** caches query-position activations at layer 10 and runs the two patched passes for NDE and NIE. **Stage 4** steers with the normalised factual-minus-counterfactual difference, α swept, tested by a 1,000-draw paired bootstrap that resamples factual–counterfactual pair together, at a fixed **α = 75** across all eight cells. **Results:** baselines AUROC 0.809/0.825, accuracy 0.755/0.748, EO difference **0.171 vs 0.315**; TE falls significantly in **7/8** cells — `flip` vectors large (UTICalc vector −0.154 [−0.160, −0.148] on UTICalc, accuracy −0.055 [−0.086, −0.023]; −0.089 on COMPAS, accuracy −0.043) but **the COMPAS `flip` vector *increases* TE on COMPAS by +0.165 [0.099, 0.230]** with a non-significant accuracy change, while `LLM` vectors give −0.018 to −0.088 with no or negligible accuracy cost (exactly 0.000 in one cell, because no predicted label crossed threshold). Reductions sit in the **direct** effect, indirect unchanged or slightly up. Transfer across datasets works in most cells, read by the authors as a layer-10 race representation shared across tasks. **Named limits:** one model, two tabular tasks, one binary attribute, only TE optimised; α = 75 best in most but not all cells; the COMPAS failure attributed speculatively to race-correlated features left invariant; the `flip`-vs-`LLM` comparison confounded by sample size and filtering; LiNGAM's linearity / non-Gaussian / no-confounding assumptions make PC-CVR a proxy; an ethics section denies any fairness certification.

- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 213): **A decomposition can be well-defined while the localisation underneath it is almost empty, and the pair of numbers is more informative than either — here the best layer by ablation recovers 1.6% of the effect (layer 10; layer 9 gives 1.3%, layer 0 gives 0.01%, layer 11 gives about 1.2e-5%, everything else 0.1–0.4%) and the paper runs the full direct/indirect split and the steering experiment on that layer anyway, because mediation does not require the mediating layer to carry much of the total effect.** That separation is the one this folder has been circling from several directions — a head that probes perfectly and is redundant, a feature that reorganises a manifold and cannot flip a decision, a group whose interactions are negligible and whose necessity is nil — and this paper is its cheapest instance, because the two readings come from two forward passes each on the same cached activations and neither is expensive. What it changes for us is a reporting rule: an ablation map and a route decomposition are different instruments asking different questions, and an ablation share near zero is a statement about *redundancy of the component*, not about *the existence of the path*. So quote both, and when the ablation share is small say explicitly that the decomposition is of the effect and not of the component — otherwise a 1.6% localisation invites exactly the misreading that the effect has been found to live in that layer. The companion discipline is that a near-zero recovery figure is itself a result worth carrying forward: it says the behaviour is distributed enough that *no* whole-layer ablation will localise it, which for a predictive white-box model is a warning that layer-granularity claims about a diffuse attribute are close to untestable by this battery and need a different unit. (arxiv-2611.00298, arxiv-2611.15653, arxiv-2611.10457)

- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 213): **When the target quantity is defined by generated inputs, running two generators and printing the gap is an effect size for the generator — the gap here is a factor of roughly 1.7 to 3.4 in the effect being reduced (0.089–0.154 of total-effect reduction from naive attribute flips against 0.018–0.088 from LLM-proposed, graph-filtered counterfactuals) with the *opposite* accuracy consequence (about 5% cost versus 1–2% or none), so a single-generator pipeline would have reported the flip number as the attribute's effect and the LLM number as a failed, weaker replication.** Three things follow. First, the direction of the bias is interpretable and worth stating: the arm that ignores causal propagation *overstates* the effect, which is what you would expect if flipping one feature alone pushes the record off the data manifold and part of the "effect" is the model's response to an implausible input — the authors name this themselves and then admit their comparison cannot isolate it because the arms also differ in sample size and filtering. Second, the filter is the honest part and its cost should always be reported: a causal-consistency filter discards 68% and 77% of candidates here to reach zero violations against a graph that is itself estimated under linearity and no-hidden-confounding assumptions, so the retained set is consistent with *a* graph rather than with ground truth, and the paper says so rather than claiming validity. Third, a cross-dataset transfer grid is the cheap replication this design allows and it produced the paper's sharpest negative — a vector learned on one dataset reduced the effect there and *increased* it on the other (+0.165), which is what a transfer claim should be allowed to fail at. For any of our pipelines that start from synthesised or edited inputs, the rule is two generators, both effect sizes, both retention rates, and the transfer grid. (arxiv-2611.00298, arxiv-2611.10045, arxiv-2608.19338)

- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 213): **A steering direction read off the component that already won the ablation sweep is selected, and without a matched-norm random direction the intervention result is not separated from "a perturbation of this size at this site happens to shrink the measured gap" — the tell is a response curve that is non-monotone in α (this paper's COMPAS vector lowers the effect to about α = 40 and then raises it past the baseline by α = 75) plus at least one cell where the target moves while the outcome metric is exactly unchanged.** The second tell is the more useful one because it is cheap and unambiguous: an accuracy delta of exactly 0.000 with a significant effect delta means the intervention moved predicted probabilities without moving any predicted label, which is a legitimate result but is *also* what a generic perturbation of a well-calibrated classifier looks like — the two are distinguished only by a random arm at the same norm at the same layer, which is one extra sweep over the same α grid and needs no new computation beyond the norm. This is the fourth form of the folder's matched-arm lesson and its most avoidable instance: a random dilution vector requires no labels, no counterfactuals and no new dataset, so there is no cost argument for omitting it, and here the omitted arm sits under the paper's *headline* claim (a race representation at layer 10 shared across tasks). The reporting rule: every steering result carries the random-direction arm per α, the α-response curve in full rather than the best point, and a statement of which layer was chosen and by which earlier measurement — because a layer picked by the largest ablation share and a vector built at that layer are two selections stacked on the same data. (arxiv-2611.00298, arxiv-2611.10045, arxiv-2611.12206)

- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 212): **A causal group demonstration plus a random-neuron control answers "is this set doing something the average set is not" and leaves "is this set carrying the input-specific content it is credited with" entirely untested — and the gap is not hypothetical, because twelve Qwen3-0.6B MLP neurons that zero-ablate the margin by 0.27 against −0.00 for random neurons, add almost perfectly (R² 0.99, zero interacting pairs), transfer to rephrasings at Spearman 0.96–1.00 and contain a single neuron strongest in 10/10 questions can be replaced by their own values from other questions with an effect of 0.00, their activations holding a median absolute deviation of 0.12 against a median magnitude of 2.53.** The instrument that exposed it costs one extra intervention per claim: instead of writing zeros or a dataset mean, write the value the same units take on a *different input*, and read the effect. Three readings follow, and all three matter for a predictive white-box model. A near-constant group is a **gate or a scalar** — a direction the read-out multiplies by — and gates are legitimately causal, legitimately transferable and legitimately uninformative about which input was processed, so a causal panel that does not separate gate from carrier will certify both identically. The same paper shows the control is not a blanket veto either: in the two-hop setting the selected neurons *are* sensitive to values from another chain (zero 1.31, resample 1.37 in Qwen3-1.7B) and act at 0.18/0.09/0.11 on another chain against 1.52/1.89/1.82 on their own, which is what a content-bearing group looks like — so the control's value is that it discriminates, not that it always finds nothing; and even there patching from another chain's composed question still lowers the margin by ~0.85, meaning part of the effect is generic disruption and the paper says so rather than claiming the bridge. Our own battery should therefore report, per claim, the random control *and* the content-matched control, and treat a large effect that dies under the second as a gate finding rather than a representation finding. (arxiv-2611.13885, arxiv-2610.41185, arxiv-2611.00155)

- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 212): **"These N neurons" is a sufficient-intervention existence proof dressed as a necessity claim, and one exhaustive subset table shows the number is close to arbitrary — the smallest answer-flipping subset runs 1, 2, 4, 4, 4, 4, 5, 5, 6, 6 across ten Qwen3-1.7B chains and 1–8 across three models, effects accumulate smoothly with the median and the strongest subset visibly diverging at every size, and 15–306 minimal sets sit at 50% of the full effect with disjoint pairs in 8 of 10 questions.** Because 2ⁿ is cheap at n = 12, the honest form of a group claim is a *curve* rather than a count: for every subset size, the distribution of effects over all subsets of that size, from which the smallest sufficient size, the median and the best case all fall out of one measurement pass. Two structural consequences worth carrying. **Uniqueness is not a property of the group but of group-plus-threshold-plus-margin-plus-selection-rule**, and the paper demonstrates the dependence in its own numbers rather than asserting it: disjoint alternatives appear in 3/10, 7/10 and 7/8 flipped chains depending on model, and the headline Qwen3 count moved from 4/10 to 3/10 when the flip criterion was tightened from ≥ to > to exclude exact ties — a definitional change, not an experimental one, which is why Appendix B exists. **The moderator is the clean margin:** pooled over 28 flipped chains, disjoint alternatives exist in 13 of 15 chains where the model was unsure (margin < 4) and 4 of 13 where it was confident, and the four chains no subset ever flips all sit above 4.6 — so a near-threshold answer has many interchangeable routes and a confident one has few, which is the mechanistic reading of redundancy and also a warning that any uniqueness comparison across models is confounded by how close each model sat to flipping. For our write-ups the rule is three fields on every component claim — clean margin, size distribution of sufficient subsets, and the threshold used — because without all three a "these N units" statement is not falsifiable at the granularity it is stated. (arxiv-2611.13885, arxiv-2602.22968, arxiv-2603.30002)

- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 211): **The cheapest test of whether a dictionary earns its keep is to build the identical downstream head three times and change only the representation feeding it — here the same adapter, same targets, same schedule and same frozen planner give 3.44% ADE reduction from the SAE latents against 2.74% from the raw dense activation they reconstruct and 2.86% from a randomly-initialised encoder of matched architecture trained end-to-end on the very objective being optimised.** That third control is the one worth stealing: it isolates *sparse basis chosen without supervision* from *encoder parameters fitted to the task*, which is the comparison every "our features are useful downstream" claim actually needs and almost never runs, and it is more informative than either the ablation or the dense arm alone because a from-scratch encoder has strictly more freedom and still loses. Two reporting failures travel with it, both already in this folder's ledger and both visible in one table. The margin being claimed is 0.6–0.7 points of ADE on a single validation split with no seed spread, which is a scale on which the ordering of the three arms is not established; and the prose reads the ordering as confirmation ("appears to provide a more useful interface") while the appendix's own hedge ("does not produce as large of an improvement") says the opposite about certainty. The rule for our own write-ups: any three-arm comparison at this scale needs a per-seed spread and a statement of the difference divided by it, and the honest sentence names the effect size rather than the winner. (arxiv-2610.41185, arxiv-2611.07283, arxiv-2606.02061)

- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 211): **A latent's ordinary correlation with an output does not predict which way pushing it moves that output, and the failure is per-statistic rather than global — across 270 features the sign match between natural association and steering response is 59.7% for lateral displacement (Pearson 0.686), 61.5% for proposal spread and 56.7% for braking, but 40.3% for curvature with Pearson −0.289, i.e. the correlation points the wrong way for the one output that is most numerically sensitive.** Three consequences for a predictive white-box model. First, "feature F correlates with output Y" and "feature F controls Y" are different measurements and the paper's own table shows them dissenting on the same fixed set of features, so a dictionary validated by correlation panels is validated for description only. Second, the right form of the claim is the one the authors build: for every feature, print the natural correlation, the steered effect at the maximum intervention level, and the agreement across features — four numbers per statistic, and the interesting cell is a confidently-signed correlation with a wrong-signed push. Third, the instrument behind the steering half is worth copying wholesale, because it turns one intervention into a graded claim: sweep α over four levels on the 64 highest-activation scenes, score effect size in units of the output's own validation SD, average a per-scene Spearman between α and the output for monotonicity, count the fraction of scenes agreeing in sign for consistency, and divide the effect on the target by the summed effects on the other five measured statistics for selectivity — multiplied, so a feature must clear all four to rank. Read beside this folder's decodability-versus-necessity inversions, this is the dictionary-level member of the family: correlation, controllability and use are three measurements, and only two of them can be established from the same model pass. (arxiv-2610.41185, arxiv-2611.15653, arxiv-2611.10457)

- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 211): **Groundedness can be made arithmetic instead of anecdotal with one balanced factorial replay — hold two of the three inputs fixed, evaluate every combination, and run a variance decomposition so that "the representation is grounded in the image" becomes a main effect plus an interaction term that a model copying its metadata forward provably cannot produce.** The numbers here: 9,000 images replayed under all six combos of three intents and two standardised ego histories (54,000 latents), with the image's main effect at 14.3% of latent variance and image×intent at 7.2% and image×ego at 6.9% — and the argument the entry should keep is the authors' own, that the interaction terms would be exactly zero if the latents simply re-encoded intent and ego state, so their being non-zero is evidence about computation rather than about correlation. The design detail that makes it work is the *balanced* sample: equal counts across the six cells so no common driving condition dominates, and standardised rather than natural ego histories so the two arms differ only in the variable named. This is the cheapest member of the folder's family of on-manifold-substitution demands (an admissible region checked at the proposal and at fractions of its radius, a realizable counterfactual, a matched permutation arm), and it is available with no intervention at all: the model is only ever run on inputs drawn from the metadata combinations, and the answer is a share of variance rather than a claim about a mechanism. The companion limit is stated in the paper and should be copied — an ANOVA over a 384-dimensional latent space tells you how much the representation depends on an input, not whether any particular latent means anything, which is why the same paper then ranks features by a controllability score and by a grounding edit rather than trusting the decomposition alone. (arxiv-2610.41185, arxiv-2611.00155, arxiv-2608.19338)
