- Done 2026-11-15 (entry 207): `arxiv-2611.00420` — Circuit Oracle: Automating Attribution Graph Analysis via Natural-Language Queries (Shariar Kabir, Hong Kiat Tan, Swastik Agrawal, Sai Chereddy, Sriram Balasubramanian; Independent / UCLA / University of Maryland; arXiv:2611.00420v1, 2026-10-30, CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, code at anonymous.4open.science). Full text, all ~137k clean chars in six windows incl. Appendices B–G. **Substance:** an off-the-shelf LLM reading a transcoder attribution graph through nine tools and a per-task "skill", on three proxy tasks. **Probe task** (Gemma-2-2B, 4 datasets × 2 probes × 10 prompts = 80 graphs, judge-scored verdicts, two probes judged independently): 78.2% ± 2.4 (passes 76.2–82.5%) against 72.5% transcoder-cosine and 65.0% SAE-cosine, where both baselines are 40/40 on biased rankings and 0/10 on the unbiased ones for the two datasets whose spurious cue is not aligned with the probe direction — and where the agent contributes nothing, since removing Neuronpedia inspection *raises* accuracy to 81% and a one-shot top-k read with no traversal scores 77.5%. **Secret elicitation** (Qwen3-8B taboo LoRAs, 20 secrets × 6 prompts): 75.0% closed-menu against SAE-projection 25.8% and transcoder-projection 1.7%, behind Activation Oracle 86.7% closed / 74.2% open; open-vocabulary drops to 43.3% (largest drop of any method, −31.7 pts) and the paper states the concept is absent from the transcoder logit-lens at every layer band for some secrets; SAE-projection decays with depth 25.8/15.0/12.5% at layers 9/18/27; the winning mechanism is the target-minus-strongest-sibling diff against a base-model graph on the same prompt; orchestrator grid spans 69.2/70.8/68.8% closed across three models. **Refusal suppression** (Qwen3-4B, 50 AdvBench-style prompts, 5-judge ensemble): 0.804 committed pick vs 0.825 diff-in-mean (10W/20T/20L), 0.854 best-of-five (16/24/10), 0.041 unsteered; one-shot top-k gives 0.112, i.e. +0.074 over nothing against +0.766 for the closed loop, the exact inverse of the probe task's ablation. **Stability:** five passes on fixed graphs agree on pinned features at Jaccard 0.511 and on layers at 0.754. **Label-versus-role:** L17:F83241 is labelled code/technical but pinned across refusal prompts as a safety precursor that releases output when cut; on the 10-prompt refusal-vs-censorship study refusal shares one recurring precursor while censorship shares no bottleneck (five different layers, no recurring feature) and diff-in-mean beats the feature method there. **Four reported-number and design problems recorded in the entry:** the prose cites per-pass values from a table that has none; the probe-task scoring rule is asymmetric (biased must say "spurious", unbiased only must not) so a "mixed"-biased detector wins half the set; orchestrator spread (70–78.2%) equals the margin over baseline; and blocked judge calls are set to the maximum on both axes rather than dropped (6/250 vs 7/250, symmetric, but still a censored measurement rounded up).

- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 207): **A verdict can be perfectly stable while the circuit behind it is a coin flip, and the two numbers have to be reported separately — here five passes over identical fixed graphs agree on the pinned feature set at only Jaccard 0.511 while agreeing on which layers carry the evidence at 0.754, so the reader lands in the same region every time and names different components.** The authors' own defence is that many subgraphs can support one verdict, which is true and is also exactly why the accuracy number cannot be used as evidence that the recovered circuit is the mechanism: a detector that answers YES from any one of twenty spurious features will score identically whichever twenty it found. For a predictive white-box model this sets a tolerance band we should quote rather than discover — an agentic or sampling-based reader has pass-to-pass component agreement around one half at the level of individual components and around three quarters at the level of layers — and it supplies the reporting form: verdict accuracy, feature Jaccard, layer Jaccard, three columns, always together, because the first is about the answer and the last two are about the explanation. Read beside this folder's thresholded-battery result (a structure that keeps growing with sample size is measuring the test's power) and its overlap-versus-faithfulness result, this is the sampling-noise version of the same claim: repetition is not replication when the same stochastic reader is doing the repeating, and the honest control is a *second reader*, which this paper runs as an orchestrator swap only. (arxiv-2611.00420, arxiv-2608.19338, arxiv-2611.00786)

- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 207): **Subtracting a sibling graph is the cheapest way to isolate what a checkpoint actually does, and the arithmetic is one extra forward pass — score each feature by its activation minus the strongest activation any sibling model shows at the same layer, feature and position, which here deleted three chat-template detector features that looked exactly like the answer on the single graph and left the one feature that fires only under the fine-tune.** Two properties make this more than a preprocessing trick. First, the thing being subtracted is the *shared* computation, so what survives is by construction the specialisation — no labels, no contrast set, no behaviour example, which is why the paper can eliminate a scaffold the intervention itself would have had to discover. Second, the residual has a natural reading only because the coordinate system is shared, so the method applies exactly when the two checkpoints have the same feature dictionary (base vs LoRA, base vs SFT, step-k vs step-n), and it fails silently when they do not. The companion warning is the open-vocabulary drop from 75.0% to 43.3%: a menu narrows the search space and the resulting score says more about the options than about the representation, and for several targets the concept was not in the dictionary at any layer, which is a statement about the basis that no amount of differencing or aggregation repairs. For us this is the same discipline as the folder's matched-init and matched-random arms, applied to checkpoints instead of controls: the comparison arm is free, so run it, and print the constrained and unconstrained scores side by side. (arxiv-2611.00420, arxiv-2611.10045, arxiv-2606.02061)

- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 207): **Whether an agentic wrapper earns its cost is task-dependent by construction, and the way to find out is two ablations of the same reader on two tasks that disagree — here removing edge traversal entirely changes the probe task by 78.2% → 77.5% (and removing the label lookup *raises* accuracy to 81%) while on refusal suppression the same one-shot read gives +0.074 over no intervention against +0.766 for the closed loop, a tenfold difference in what the scaffolding buys.** The reason is worth generalising past agents: when the answer sits one hop from the readout, multi-hop search is pure added variance, and when the required action has to be *found by measuring* (which of many candidate features actually flips the output), no static ranking by direct effect substitutes for a verify loop. That gives a decision rule for our own tooling — instrument the wrapper by ablating it on the same items, and expect the value of traversal to track how far the answer is from the target you can already score. The second, sharper lesson is what the ablation exposed: dropping the semantic labels helped, which means the dictionary description was a distractor on a task where the spurious cue's identity is visible from which token a feature reads. A reader's stated rationale is not evidence of what it used, and the only way to know is to remove each component and re-score, one component at a time, on the same fixed item set. (arxiv-2611.00420, arxiv-2611.10457, arxiv-2608.19338)

Full text, ~231k clean chars in seven windows incl. Appendices A–Q. **Substance:** a five-stage 26-component Dyck circuit in Pythia-1B established by interventions alone and verified on held-out strings by named-subspace removal (STACK 61.4%→14.8% against 58.4–62.6% random; ANSWER →39.3% against 60.4–61.8%; the named bottleneck alone preserves 76.3% of contrast, 91.9% with 64 residual-covariance directions added); geometry measured with draws confined to an explicit region U (KL ≤ 0.02 nats, |ΔCE| ≤ 0.1, |Δacc| ≤ 0.02, ≤ 0.5 RMS, checked at u, u/2, u/4) so the actual KL and its Fisher quadratic are compared on identical draws; the Fisher spectrum of all 144 components at all 154 checkpoints by stochastic Lanczos quadrature; and four pre-registered predictions tested with partial rank correlations on levels and adjacent changes. **The audit:** documented SGLD chains displace weights by a median 4.76× matrix RMS (2.96–6.88× under the reference implementation's settings), 0/48 stay inside U, holding at 0.05 RMS needs γ ≈ 7×10⁵, and the estimator's own statistic is negative in 21–24 of 24 conditions. **The correspondence:** Metropolis LLC vs zero-ablation Spearman 0.64 synthetic / 0.16 natural (heads −0.18); trace-causal change association 0.51 median partial but only ~0.25 of excess over pairing with the population median; gain Fisher 0.98/0.97 partial and specific (0.12) while absorbing the trace's association (0.02); the large-temperature count 0.47 on non-circuit components but 0.09 on circuit ones; joint bank 5.8% below the summed LLC (5.7× MCSE) and from step 8,000 the joint drop exceeds even the absolute marginal sum; interaction curvature 0.16/0.14/0.16 on circuit pairs against 0.05 on matched controls. **Two reported-number and design problems recorded:** the coordinate control moves the natural-context association from 0.16 (RMS prior) to 0.561 (isotropic prior in converted tensors) so the geometry-mechanism calibration depends on the parameter metric, and the natural-context cell of the headline correspondence is 0.16 with negative head-only values while the abstract quotes only the synthetic 0.51. **Why relevance 3:** it gives the folder a component-importance scalar that needs no replacement value and the cleanest demonstration that a sampler's radius is a claim to be verified, not assumed.
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 206): **A perturbation study has to prove its draws stay where the model still works, and the arithmetic that makes this non-optional is one line — here the standard sampler moves each weight by a median 4.76× the RMS of its own weight matrix, 0/48 chains end inside the region where predictions are preserved, and the estimator's own statistic comes out negative in 21–24 of 24 conditions because the drift term has quietly fine-tuned the model on the evaluation batch.** The paper's fix is worth copying verbatim as a protocol: define the admissible region explicitly (KL ≤ 0.02 nats, cross-entropy change ≤ 0.1 nats, accuracy change ≤ 0.02, no tensor beyond 0.5 RMS), check it at the proposal, at half and at a quarter of the radius, and then *compare the actual loss and its second-order approximation on the same draws* so every reported coefficient carries a curvature control. The reason this belongs in our battery rather than in a sampling footnote is that the same structure appears all over the folder in non-probabilistic dress: a steering magnitude that breaks coherent generation, an ablation that pushes the network off-manifold, a random control direction at unmatched norm, a dictionary swept until features stop being readable. In each case there is a computable region and a one-line statistic that says whether the experiment is inside it, and in each case the honest number is the one measured inside. The companion lesson is about the tuning escape hatch: localization strong enough to hold the chain inside the region (γ ≈ 7×10⁵ here, seven orders above the documented sweep) samples only the prior, so the region has to be *imposed on the draws* rather than reached by turning a knob — a general statement that when a hyperparameter swept in the plausible range cannot reach the regime you need, the answer is rejection or reweighting, not a wider sweep. (arxiv-2611.00640, arxiv-2610.39766, arxiv-2608.19338)
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 206): **The component-importance scalar we should be quoting is the output norm measured under the downstream model's own Fisher metric, not the parameter count or the activation norm — here that quantity predicts zero-ablation effect at partial rank correlation 0.98 in levels and 0.97 in changes, is component-specific where the Fisher trace is not (0.12 against the population-median trajectory), and once it is included as a covariate the trace's association with the ablation falls to 0.02.** The construction is one pullback and needs no replacement value: F = DGᵀ Σ DG, with Σ the categorical Fisher information of the output distribution, so the diagonal term counts how strongly each parameter direction moves the next-token distribution rather than how large the parameter is. That distinction is what makes it usable in a predictive model — the same weight magnitude in a component whose write is in the null space of everything downstream costs nothing, and this number says so. Two discipline notes travel with it. First, a trace and a gain are different instruments: the trace is dominated by a model-wide trend (median pairwise component-component rank correlation 0.91, against 0.47 for ablation effects), which is exactly why a naive per-component attribution of a training-shaped trend would be wrong, while the gain is the specific part. Second, when a summarising scalar absorbs a rival's explanatory power, the honest table shows the rival's association before and after — the collapse from 0.51 to 0.02 is a stronger statement than either number alone. (arxiv-2611.00640, arxiv-2611.10457, arxiv-2611.15653)
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 206): **A trajectory statistic can be almost entirely a shared trend, and the tell is the population-median baseline — pairing each component's geometry with the *median* trajectory of all components already reproduces most of the association with mechanism (0.50 against 0.26 for a random other component, versus 0.51 for the component's own), so only the 0.25 excess is evidence about the component, and the same paper's Shapley decomposition then hands 1.08 of the trace's late rise to the *input* group with the component's own tensors contributing −0.23.** Three habits follow, and all are cheap. Pair every per-unit series with the population median series before anyone calls it a unit-level finding — a random-comparator baseline is too weak here, because the field's default of "we compared to a random component" answers a question nobody asked. Pick the level at which you claim: this paper's *level* association for the joint bank comes out negative (−0.36) purely because the summed trace bottoms at step 6,000 while the joint ablation peaks at 15,000, so a levels claim and a changes claim can carry opposite signs and only the changes claim is about formation timing. And run a sign test on the interesting half: the joint drop exceeding the *absolute* marginal sum from step 8,000 onward is the observation that rules out cancellation, and it is one extra column over the signed sum the paper already had. (arxiv-2611.00640, arxiv-2611.00786, arxiv-2611.10974)

and the gated rows' "near-zero clean cost" is always an interval containing zero, which is a non-inferiority claim reported as a null, so "no measured cost" and "cost measured as zero" are not distinguished anywhere in the paper. **Why relevance 3:** it is the folder's first entry in which two independently-derived component scores are used as mutual validation, and its red-team is the cheapest demonstration that a similarity label can manufacture the structure it is then used to explain.
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 205): **A similarity-based label computed in an embedding space trained on the very distinction you want to measure will manufacture that distinction, and the fix is to re-embed the identical activate-sets in a space with that training signal removed — here the Clarity Score ranks heads by how tightly their activating images cluster in CLIP space, and under a five-word injected corpus the ranking's correlation with per-head causal ground truth falls from 0.611 to 0.166 on ViT-B/16 and to exactly 0.000 on ViT-H/14 (bootstrap CI [−0.04, +0.06], i.e. indistinguishable from no signal), because a shared rendered word makes otherwise unrelated images look like a cluster in a space whose contrastive objective was trained on text.** Re-scoring the same top-activating image sets in DINOv2 — same sets, same heads, same ground truth, only the measuring encoder changed — keeps the correlation in its normal band under every one of the six manipulations, with every DINOv2 interval excluding zero; that substitution is the whole method and it costs one extra embedding pass. The reading lesson generalises past vision: this folder validates decoded concepts by clustering, nearest-neighbour inspection and image panels that are all computed inside the model's own representation space, and each of those is a space that was trained to place the target distinction wherever its pretraining placed it, so an apparent separation is compatible with the label being a property of the encoder rather than the network under study. The writing rule that follows is cheap and should be a standing column in our entries: name the space a similarity number was computed in, and if the target distinction was part of that space's training objective, print the second space. (arxiv-2611.01513, arxiv-2610.39766, arxiv-2609.03026)
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 205): **Two scores derived from completely independent measurements are a better validation of a component's role than one score validated on held-out data, because they can fail independently — here head-level prominence is scored geometrically (cluster tightness of a latent's activating images in an embedding space, using no attribution at all) and causally (gradient of the latent's activation with respect to attention on patches under a pasted text box, using no clustering at all), and the two rank heads in opposite directions in exactly the region the intervention draws from: all 29 blocks in the last fifth of depth across five backbones sit above the zero-correlation line, one-sided sign test p = 1.9e-9, with the authors stating the caveat that blocks within a model are not independent.**
Two properties make this more than a robustness check. First, the agreement is *localised* — early blocks fluctuate around zero and the correlation strengthens with depth, so the claim is not "the two metrics agree" but "they agree where lexical processing is claimed to be", which is a prediction the design could have failed. Second, both scores are also run as selectors with their own end effect printed (CS recovers 40.0/23.8/46.9/32.5/40.6 on Disentangling across the five backbones against nTAS 40.6/18.1/40.0/27.5/24.4, so neither dominates the other), which means the agreement is not being inferred from a shared downstream win. For us this is the shape a predictive white-box model should report a variable in: a geometric reading, an interventional reading, the correlation between them resolved by layer, and the end effect of each taken separately — four cheap measurements instead of one expensive claim. (arxiv-2611.01513, arxiv-2611.15653, arxiv-2611.00786)
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 205): **An architectural constraint that makes a label well-posed can be worth a measurable reconstruction loss, and the honest ablation prints both sides in one table — forcing one latent per attention head costs 17–23% relative in fraction-of-variance-unexplained against an equal-capacity monolithic dictionary trained at the same budget, seed, K and data, and on the attribution-based selector the monolithic dictionary is a statistical tie (ρ 0.576 vs 0.569 on B/16, 0.340 vs 0.350 on H/14, and its group intervention is even marginally larger at +14.4/+17.6 points against +12.5/+15.3), so the constraint buys nothing there.**
What it buys is shown in the same table: monolithic latents are head-mixed at near-chance purity (dominant-head energy share 0.10–0.14 against a 0.06–0.08 chance level), so a latent-to-head attribution is ill-posed under that design, and the one selector that needs no labels degrades severely when it is built on dominant-head-assigned monolithic latents (ρ 0.712 → 0.494 on B/16, 0.404 → 0.116 on H/14). Three lessons. The comparison is credible only because capacity, seed, data and trainer are matched — the usual failure here is comparing a constrained dictionary to a bigger unconstrained one. A constraint can pay in a *different* coordinate from the one the headline number lives in, so the ablation must be run selector by selector rather than reported as one aggregate. And a reconstruction penalty is not evidence against a decomposition: the monotone assumption that better reconstruction means better features is exactly what the split in this table refutes. (arxiv-2611.01513, arxiv-2611.07283, arxiv-2606.02061)

- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 206): **An A/B benchmark scored by which letter the model picks can be moved by a pure letter preference, and the diagnostic is one extra column plus an option-swap arm — here steering the sycophancy direction at the layer that maximises the A/B effect shifts log P(A) − log P(B) by +3.53 logits on SmolLM3 at α = +3 regardless of which option is the sycophantic one, while the content signal simultaneously moves the other way (−1.90), so the net metric falls *under both signs* of α (−1.33 at −3, −1.00 at +3) and the paper's own headline table would have read “steering reduces sycophancy” if the authors had not decomposed it.** Three habits worth copying. First, decompose the metric: report the shift of the log-ratio between the two candidate tokens, and check whether it survives when the options are swapped (here the letter column changes sign only in the swapped condition, which is how the letter effect is told apart from a content “agree” push). Second, restrict the intervention site: steering only the assistant-turn tokens removes the letter push entirely (−0.13 / +0.16) and leaves a small effect with the expected sign, which identifies *where* the artefact lives. Third, choose the benchmark whose structure cannot express the artefact — the open-ended prompts all end in a request for agreement, so agreeing is sycophantic by construction and the +27-point effect there is clean. This is the same failure class the folder keeps meeting on the scoring side (a pooled agreement figure, a scrambled-label sanity check, a similarity metric computed inside one model's own space) but in its cheapest form: a two-token answer format that makes a whole benchmark steerable by something unrelated to the construct. (arxiv-2611.10045, arxiv-2603.36404, arxiv-2503.05061)
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 206): **Two data sources can look identical per example and differ by more than an order of magnitude in effect, because the quantity that matters is intensity times volume — here SFT and preference data project almost equally strongly onto the sycophancy direction (SmolLM3 +0.025 vs +0.025, Tülu +0.014 vs +0.001, OLMo the one reversal at +0.052 vs +0.066) yet SFT sees 43×, 17× and 7× more examples, and the four highest-scoring individual datasets are SFT datasets in all three families, so the paper's conclusion rests entirely on the exposure multiplication rather than on any difference in the means.** The arithmetic generalises to every “which data produced this behaviour” question in this folder — distilled-synthetic corpora, repeated-data runs, provenance comparisons — and it converts a vague attribution into two measurable columns, per-example score and count seen, that multiply. The reporting rule is to publish both in the same table with the ratio, because a reader given only the means will rank the sources oppositely to a reader given the product. Two companion checks the paper runs and we should: the tail share (percentage of a source's examples above the pooled 97.5th percentile, which catches a source whose mean is ordinary but which carries a dense sycophantic sub-population — 3–7% for both stages here), and the paired intra-pair difference for preference data (chosen minus rejected is positive in all three families, +0.020 to +0.025 through the final direction, so the preference objective *does* select for the direction and its innocence is a volume argument, not an absence of signal). (arxiv-2611.10045, arxiv-2404.01413, arxiv-2610.32691)
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 206): **A steering direction is only usable as a measurement instrument after two nulls and one admissibility rule, and this paper's set is the cheapest version the folder has seen — three Gaussian random directions at *matched magnitude* (angle < 0.03 to the real one) are reported per seed and averaged (SmolLM3 +1.5, +7.0, +3.5, mean +4.0 against the real +26.5; Tülu +1.0 mean against +27.0), and a cell is discarded when the answer mass on the two valid completions falls below half the unsteered value, which is what stops an incoherent perturbation from scoring as an effect.** Two properties make this more than boilerplate. The magnitude matching is what the folder keeps finding missing (a random arm at matched *count*, a random dictionary at matched *capacity*, a convenient baseline that is matched rather than merely present), and it is what licenses the phrase “the direction carries the behaviour” rather than “any large perturbation moves the behaviour”. And the admissibility rule surfaces the paper's most interesting negative: the strongest-effect layer for OLMo 3 is the one where coherent generation collapses, so the direction's apparent potency there (+7.2 points) is inadmissible and the honest effect at a usable layer is +0.8, a case where the guard changes the model ranking rather than tidying it. The same rule is what makes the letter-push diagnostic interpretable, because a cell that survives on answer mass but fails option-swap is unambiguously a letter effect rather than a coherence artefact. For our own probe work: report random directions at matched norm per seed, and state the guard that would have discarded the cell, before quoting any effect size. (arxiv-2611.10045, arxiv-2510.20487, arxiv-2611.10457)

- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 220): **An outer readout can be *proved* unable to recover a target, and the proof is two inputs rather than a new experiment — find two states that the readout makes identical and that differ on the target, and the prohibition is established by construction, because the map from inner observation to outer observation is non-injective and that non-injectivity follows from the form of the map, not from the particular model or input.** The paper's three examples are the ones our own work needs: many ways of splitting component writes give the same sum (so a sum-level statistic can never recover a per-component attribution), a hidden state and any positive rescaling of it unembed to the same distribution (so any target that depends on state norm is invisible to output-side probes), and different phrasings of one claim share a meaning (so a semantic label cannot recover a lexical one). Two habits follow and both are cheap. Before training a probe, write down the collapse it is vulnerable to and check the target for sensitivity to the discarded variable — this is the missing step under the folder's repeated finding that a probe can be highly predictive and causally idle, and it explains that finding rather than restating it. And when a probe *is* wanted, report whether it is **native** (its target is defined at the lens it reads) or **surrogate** (its target is defined at an outer lens), because a surrogate's score is evidence about the outer quantity and says nothing about the computation it read — a distinction that separates 34 of 41 published representational methods from the eight that can support a mechanistic claim. (arxiv-2611.15735, arxiv-2611.14483, arxiv-2611.00298)

- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 220): **Layered information can be measured as a nested-feature ladder, and the honest result is usually that the increments are small — build feature sets so each contains the previous one as a prefix, fit one probe family to each, and read the difference as the marginal decodable information of the newly added layer. Here the whole single-pass contribution over a sampled semantical baseline is 0.039 AUROC on TriviaQA (0.871 → 0.910), with the representational step worth 0.024 and the structural step 0.002, but the same ladder inverted on a four-letter multiple-choice set where every increment collapses to about 0.01.** Two lessons. First, a nested design turns what is normally a single number into a curve whose *shape* is the finding — and the shape is diagnostic in a way a lone AUC is not, because the flat MMLU ladder is the framework's own prediction being confirmed (with a one-token answer space the semantic map has nothing to discard) rather than a failure to replicate. Second, the ladder bounds the claim: because it uses one probe family, it measures information *usable by that family*, and the paper says so instead of quoting the increment as the information content of the lens — the same distinction we need whenever we report that a representation "contains" a variable. For our battery the rule is to carry a baseline probe at the outermost available readout (logits alone) and treat every inner feature set as an increment on it, with the increment printed beside its seed spread; a figure like 0.910 vs 0.871 with no spread is not evidence that the hidden state matters more than the output distribution, but it is enough to say the inner readout is not *where* the signal lives. (arxiv-2611.15735, arxiv-2611.00640, arxiv-2610.34756)

- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 220): **A subspace that carries real signal can be entirely redundant given another, and one SVD plus two probes shows it without a single intervention — split the final state into its projection onto the top right-singular vectors of the unembedding (chosen at 99% of row-space variance, retaining 3,439 of 3,584 dimensions in Qwen and 3,962 of 4,096 in Llama) and the residual tail, where the tail holds 22.3% of the state's norm in Qwen and 4.4% in Llama; a probe on the tail alone reaches high AUROC while the full-state probe barely beats the top-only probe, so the signal is present and adds nothing.** This is the folder's redundancy result in its cheapest instrument — no ablation, no corruption, no replacement value — and it has three uses. It makes "the model represents X" checkable against "the representation of X is doing any work beyond what the output direction already carries", which is the quantity a downstream read-out would actually see. It gives a natural null for feature rediscovery: a newly named direction should be tested for incremental value over the top subspace rather than for its standalone correlation. And it explains why so many published probes are high-AUC and mechanistically idle without accusing anyone of error: the tail is real, it is simply collinear in effect with the dominant directions, which is exactly the circumstance under which an ablation of the tail would also look harmless. The parallel with the folder's causal redundancy results is the useful part — the same structure can be diagnosed for free on activations, and only needs an intervention when the question is *why* the redundancy exists. (arxiv-2611.15735, arxiv-2611.12206, arxiv-2611.10457)

**Cause** = target answer moves to the source's class, **Iso** = base's auxiliary attribute survives, both over accepted-answer sets, macro-averaged over prompt-template groups; Disentangle is their unweighted mean. **Five methods at the last subject subtoken's block output:** SAE (expansion 2d/4d, ReLU, β = 0.5, then an L1 SVM with C ∈ {0.1, 1, 10, 1000} to pick the class-relevant latents), DBM/MDBM (relaxed axis-aligned mask, temperature annealed 1e-2 → 1e-7, evaluated by thresholding at 0.5), DAS/MDAS (row-orthonormal rank-k projector, k ∈ {1024, 2048}), and multi-layer MDAS/DAS over contiguous 2- and 4-layer windows with per-layer rank-k subspaces trained jointly and hooks firing in ascending order so later sites see the intervened state. **Method ordering is identical on both axiom types and both model sizes: MDAS > DAS > MDBM > DBM > SAE.** Qwen3-8B MDAS: Disentangle 0.592 Entity / 0.587 Context (`instance of`), 0.513 / 0.542 (`subclass of`); SAE 0.412 / 0.371 and 0.397 / 0.429; DAS 0.584 / 0.547 and 0.496 / 0.535; MDBM 0.443 / 0.408 and 0.440 / 0.450. **Multi-task supervision buys Iso at Cause's expense and the trade pays:** +0.081 Iso / −0.052 Cause on average across matched cells. **Layer windows beat matched single sites at equal total dimension** — at 1024 dimensions `256×4` beats `512×2` for both DAS and MDAS on `instance of`; best four-layer DAS 0.667 against single-layer DAS 0.529 for the same method and dimension (Δ +0.102); MDAS `256×4` 0.666, `512×4` 0.663. **Cause rises through the middle of the model and can collapse in late layers where Iso is high** — the intervention stops changing the generated output, which the authors read as the site no longer being on the path. **Class-level heterogeneity is systematic and scale-stable:** high-scoring classes are those with compact regular attribute profiles (airport, city, country, currency, software, university for `instance of`; flower, tree, measuring instrument, medical device in the base role for `subclass of`), low-scoring ones broad and heterogeneous (food, body of water, geographical feature, material, biological process); class rankings correlate across Qwen3-8B and 4B at ρ **0.831 / 0.810** (instance-of base/source) and **0.752 / 0.671** (subclass-of), while **base-role and source-role rankings are nearly independent** — ρ 0.273 / 0.267 and −0.082 / 0.059 — and reciprocal gaps between A←B and B←A runs have median **0.132–0.179** with **29.8–41.8%** of eligible pairs above 0.2 and 5.0–12.1% above 0.4 (extremes: `animal ← academic journal` 0.742 vs 0.194; `body of water ← food` 0.711 vs 0.042). Class-level averaging also flips the task comparison: on `instance of` Iso exceeds Cause in every class-level row (Δ +0.091 to +0.167, so the bottleneck is *changing* the answer), while on `subclass of` Cause exceeds Iso (Δ −0.030 to −0.100, so the bottleneck is *preserving* the attribute). **The design decisions the entry is built around:** interventions are scored only on prompt instances the *unintervened* model already answers correctly, and base accuracies before that filter are only 94.7/93.0 micro on the target but **64.9 / 69.1 micro (63.8 / 68.3 macro) on auxiliary attributes**, so the entire Iso column is conditioned on a stricter subset than the behaviour it protects; the best configuration is chosen by Entity Disentangle and then reported on Context, which is a selection-then-evaluation on adjacent splits; **no random-direction, shuffled-label or random-subspace target is run as a null** anywhere, so a Cause of 0.53 has no chance-level reference on the same site and dimension; and the `Dimension` column reports *ambient* mask width for DBM/MDBM beside ranks for DAS/MDAS, with the appendix giving effective sizes 1,631–2,580 (instance-of) and 758–2,043 (subclass-of) against 1024–2048 for the subspaces. **Why relevance 3:** it is the folder's complete worked instance of the two-sided criterion, its reciprocal-gap statistic is a free test of ordered versus undirected structure, and its retention filter is a reusable warning rather than a flaw unique to this paper.

- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 219): **An intervention claim needs a named non-target that must survive it, and the pairing is what converts a single patching result into a statement about a partition — here the same intervention is scored twice, once on the target prompt where the answer must move to the *source* subject's class and once on an auxiliary-attribute prompt where the base subject's own value must be preserved, giving Cause and Iso per configuration and their mean as the headline, and the resulting table ranks methods far more informatively than any swap rate alone would.** Best numbers are Disentangle 0.592/0.587 (`instance of`, Entity/Context) and 0.513/0.542 (`subclass of`) on MDAS, but the interesting structure is in the two columns separately: adding auxiliary supervision lifts Iso by 0.081 and drops Cause by 0.052, which is the correct trade only if the mean is the objective, and it is not obvious that it should be. The reason this belongs in our battery rather than in a benchmark's appendix is that the folder's other intervention measurements — ablations, patches, steering — have no non-target at all, so they report a change with no statement about what the change was *supposed to leave alone*, and a large effect that also destroys five unrelated properties scores identically to a surgical one. Two consequences. First, every probe, direction or component claim we write should name, in advance, the quantity it is not allowed to move, and print both numbers; for steering that means an Iso-like arm alongside the fix rate, which the folder's steering studies keep lacking (a direction with an 85% fix rate and no preservation column could be doing its work by degrading everything else). Second, the task comparison reverses between the aggregate and the class-level view — pooled over classes the `instance of` bottleneck is Cause (Iso − Cause = +0.09 to +0.17) while for `subclass of` it is Iso (−0.03 to −0.10) — so even with a competition fixed for every configuration, *which side is binding* is a property of the class population and not of the task name, and a single pooled number hides a sign flip. (arxiv-2610.38326, arxiv-2611.18514, arxiv-2611.00155)

- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 219): **Retaining only the items the clean model already answers correctly turns an intervention benchmark into a restricted-population measurement, and the restriction is large and skewed — here the base model is at 94.7% micro on the target relation but only **64.9% micro / 63.8% macro on the auxiliary attributes whose preservation is the other half of the score, so roughly a third of the population drops out of the Iso column before any intervention is run, and the reported 0.53–0.73 Iso values are conditional on a subset selected by the model's own competence.** Three readings, all cheap. The filter is defensible — an item the model gets wrong has no base answer to preserve, so Iso is undefined rather than failed — but the paper's headline then describes a different population from the one a deployment sees, and the honest table prints the retention rate per prompt group beside both scores. The filter also interacts with the metric: because Cause and Iso are computed on *different* retained sets with different sizes, Disentangle as their unweighted mean averages two scores that were not measured on the same items, which is a weaker object than it reads. And the selection is competence-correlated rather than random, so it is the same failure the folder has recorded as the truncated-battery and threshold-effects lesson — a structure that appears only on the items the model was already good at is a statement about the model's competence region, not about its mechanism. For our own white-box batteries the rule is to report the retention rate at the same prominence as the score, and to run the complementary arm — score items the model gets *wrong*, asking whether the intervention can repair the answer — because that is the population a predictive model is for, and a benchmark that excludes it cannot say anything about prediction under intervention. (arxiv-2610.38326, arxiv-2611.00298, arxiv-2611.15653)

- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 219): **Whether a recovered structure is an undirected similarity or an ordered hand-off is answerable by exchanging the two roles of every pair, and the answer changes what the object is — here intervening A←B and B←A gives a median absolute gap of 0.132–0.179 in Disentangle, with 29.8–41.8% of eligible class pairs differing by more than 0.2 and a long tail reaching 0.742 against 0.194 (`animal ← academic journal`) and 0.711 against 0.042 (`body of water ← food`), while the per-class rankings for the two roles are essentially uncorrelated (ρ 0.27, 0.27, −0.08, 0.06) even though each role's ranking replicates across model scale (ρ 0.83/0.81 and 0.75/0.67).** The distinction is not cosmetic: an undirected similarity would predict that a class good at receiving an intervention is equally good at supplying one, and the near-zero role correlation refutes it in every model–task cell. For a predictive white-box model this is the difference between a *distance metric in representation space* and a *routing relation between representations*, and only the second can be used to predict what an intervention will do. The instrument is one extra pass per pair over items already constructed, and the check it enables generalises well past interchange interventions: any time we compare two objects by a symmetric statistic — cosine between directions, overlap between circuits, Jaccard between selections, distance between decoder columns — we have assumed commutativity without testing it, and the one-line test is to run both orders and print the gap distribution rather than the pooled mean. The companion caution is the statistical one the authors state themselves: reciprocal pairs share classes and are therefore dependent, so the distribution is descriptive, and a significance test over it would be invalid without a resampling scheme that respects the dependency. (arxiv-2610.38326, arxiv-2610.34756, arxiv-2611.00420)

- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 216): **A causal score can agree with the expensive object it stands in for, reproduce only about two-thirds of the time, and still be worth using — but only if all three numbers are printed, because they measure different things and this paper's own tables show them diverging.** The frozen-base layer score ranks layers at Spearman 0.630–0.893 against the trained-adapter contribution (top-7 recovery 5/7 in every configuration), the selections from two independent calibration draws agree at Jaccard only **0.617–0.747**, and the matched-budget downstream win is real at small scale (PPL 12.32 vs 16.42 at 12 of 36 layers) yet gone by 32B (87.1 vs 87.3, three-run mean +0.23 ± 0.38). The reading that resolves the apparent tension is that the score identifies a **region**, not a set: the union of plausible selections is small enough that any draw lands somewhere good, which is exactly the same conclusion the folder drew from Circuit Oracle's pass-to-pass feature Jaccard of 0.511 against a stable verdict — a scorer that keeps landing in the same neighbourhood while naming different members. Two reporting rules follow for our own battery. Any cheap proxy for an expensive measurement carries the rank correlation *and* the resampling stability *and* the end-task effect, in that order, because a high correlation with a low stability is a signature that both measurements are dominated by a coarse ordering and the fine ordering is noise. And when a selection method is compared against a baseline, the baseline must be matched on the quantity being allocated — random, sequential and reverse selection at the same layer budget here, all collapsing to identical performance when the budget covers every layer, which is the control that makes the comparison credible. (arxiv-2610.34756, arxiv-2611.00420, arxiv-2611.12206)
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 216): **A share decomposition of a treatment effect needs the untreated model's share in the same table, because the untreated network can already carry most of it — here MLP blocks explain 58.4% of the adaptation effect against 41.6% for attention, and the identical measurement on the same model with no adapter at all gives 56–60%, so the adapter's own increment is 3.0–6.3 percentage points and the headline ratio is a fact about the base model's routing rather than about LoRA.** The authors run the reference themselves (Table 7, plus an output-replacement experiment in two adapter configurations) and are careful enough to put the confidence intervals on the *gap* rather than on the raw shares — which is the correct construction and rarer than it should be. Three consequences for how this folder writes up decompositions. First, "component type X carries N% of the effect" and "component type X carries N% *more* because of the treatment" are different claims with different numbers, and the second is the one an intervention study is entitled to. Second, the reference must be measured on the same inputs with the same ablation, not borrowed from the literature, because the ablation is part of the measurement — a zero-ablation share on a base model and a mean-ablation share on an adapted one are not comparable. Third, the same discipline applies to the folder's own effect-splitting entries (direct versus indirect effects, MLP-versus-attention mediation, layer-recovery maps): each of those numbers has a no-treatment analogue, and its size is what tells you whether the treatment did anything to the *distribution* of the effect or only to its total. (arxiv-2610.34756, arxiv-2611.00298, arxiv-2611.00640)
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 216): **Whether a task-specific structure exists at all can be tested by comparing a selection made for one distribution against a selection made for another, and the two numbers to report are the overlap and the downstream cost of the mismatch — here top-7 layer selections for four corpora overlap at a mean Jaccard of 39.5%, with only the first three layers shared by all four, yet calibrating on a *different* instruction distribution costs almost nothing in accuracy (72.8–73.5% against 75.2% matched, with random selection at 70.2%), so the selections genuinely differ while the value they deliver barely depends on which one you got.** That pair is what makes the task-dependence claim readable rather than dramatic: a low overlap on its own invites the conclusion that task-specific calibration is essential, and the transfer arm shows the opposite in downstream terms — the calibrated ranking beats random even when it was calibrated on the wrong corpus. The instrument is one extra training run per off-diagonal cell and it turns an overlap matrix into a decision about whether per-task calibration is worth its cost. For us the transferable form is a two-column report for any selector, reader or dictionary built per-task: how much the *object* changes across tasks, and how much the *outcome* changes when you swap objects — because a structure that reconstitutes itself from the wrong calibration set is describing something shared, and one whose swap is expensive is describing something local, and the overlap statistic alone cannot tell you which. (arxiv-2610.34756, arxiv-2611.15653, arxiv-2611.10457)

- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 210): **A null ablation and a real cause look identical when the backup is left free, and the arithmetic that separates them is one extra rollout — here patching a component produces the full immediate effect (2 m/s² of braking) while the failure still arrives, just 0.1 s later, and patching *every* step of the same component still fails because a second component restores the original velocity and the incident simply moves from 1.7 s to 3.3 s.** The general form is that any intervention which perturbs one component while leaving the rest of the network to respond measures a *but-for* effect, and but-for effects are the special case of causation where there are no backups — so a small number from such an experiment is ambiguous between "this component does nothing" and "a backup absorbs it", and the two readings imply opposite repairs. The folder has been responding to small ablation effects by softening the ablation (mean-ablate, project out a subspace, add covariance directions) and by reporting matched-random arms; neither addresses this, because both vary the *value* substituted while leaving the compensators live. The fix is two numbers per component, not a better ablation: the effect with the rest of the network free, and the effect with a searched set of compensators held at their observed values, printed with the set. The paper's own honest note is that the second is only as meaningful as the witness is realistic — freezing a component can force a state the policy would never occupy — so the pair should also carry a distance measure between the factual and counterfactual trajectories, which the paper names as a weakness but does not quantify. (arxiv-2611.00155, arxiv-2611.15653, arxiv-2608.19338)
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 210): **A causal claim about one event has four slots and three of them are usually filled by default, so the cheap audit is to write the tuple down before running anything — intervene on what and over what horizon, substitute what value and could any real input induce it, hold what fixed and how was that set chosen, read out what and is it the outcome or a per-step proxy.** Applied to this folder's own interventions the audit bites in a specific place: the substituted value is almost always *either* a value taken from another input (a patch, a donor activation, a contrast pair) *or* an arithmetic construction (a mean, a projection, a steering direction at magnitude α), and only the first is guaranteed to be inducible by something the model has seen; the folder's many admissible-region and coherence guards are attempts to repair the second case after the fact, one experiment at a time. Making the realizability question a standing field in the entry template rather than a per-paper discovery is one line of bookkeeping and it would have caught, in advance, the steering magnitudes that broke generation, the sampler radii that left the working region, and the masked-input counterfactuals that scored effects on inputs the model never sees. The companion slot is horizon: within one forward pass every downstream effect is compressed into an immediate proxy, which is why a per-step read-out and a rollout read-out can disagree in sign, and why our behavioural readouts should always be the scored outcome rather than the next-token distribution it is convenient to measure. (arxiv-2611.00155, arxiv-2611.10974, arxiv-2611.00786)
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 210): **Responsibility graded as 1/k — k the number of components that must be changed or held for the failure to depend on the one you are blaming — is the cheapest degradation-aware attribution in the folder, and its weakness is entirely a granularity assumption that is checkable in one line.** Its virtue is that it needs no new machinery: every component we already score by ablation effect can additionally be scored by how many compensators had to be frozen, and the resulting number ranks candidates *for repair* rather than certifying one, which is what an editing or debugging claim actually needs. Its weakness is that k counts components, so if one "backup" is smeared across a mixture — the folder's recurring case, where a property is recoverable from every head in a block and removing the best one costs almost nothing — then k understates the repair cost and the score flatters the component. That makes the unit choice (neurons vs heads vs dictionary latents vs pairs of them) a decision about whether the number is interpretable at all rather than a presentation preference, and it is the third time this folder has reached the same conclusion from a different direction: component identity has to be established by something other than the score that is supposed to rank components. Read beside the redundancy results (a best-encoding head whose removal is invisible because eleven others carry the property) and the parallel-path results, this is the same pathology measured on the attribution side instead of the necessity side. (arxiv-2611.00155, arxiv-2611.15653, arxiv-2611.10457)

- Done 2026-11-16 (entry 209): `arxiv-2611.12206` — A Geometric Invariant of Attention Predicts Head Specialization from Weights Alone (Miguel P. Bento; Feedzai, Lisbon; NeurReps workshop at NeurIPS 2026, PMLR; arXiv:2611.12206v1, 2026-11-09, CC BY 4.0, code at github.com/MPedraBento/rho-invariant). Full text, all 13.7k chars (the whole extended abstract). **Substance:** the invariance argument (the static composite is invariant under any head-basis change; requiring the whole rotated family to be invariant shrinks that group to a rotation times a positive rescaling inside each rotary plane, which is what makes the query-key form a legitimate observable in a RoPE model); ρ as the offset-averaged ratio of perturbation norm to static norm, sampled at powers of two because the frequencies are geometric, with the scope limit stated in the definition rather than in the limitations; Proposition 1 with its one-line proof (ρ = 0 iff the logits carry no relative-position dependence for any input); the four-model validation (Spearman **−0.74** SmolLM2-135M, **−0.71** TinyLlama-1.1B, **−0.55** SmolLM2-1.7B, **−0.59** Mistral-7B, all p < 10⁻⁴⁰; top-ten induction heads within the bottom **14 / 7 / 17 / 30%** of the ρ distribution); the YaRN application (short PPL 512: 12.92 targeted vs 19.37 uniform vs 7.63 baseline; long PPL 4096: 130.34 vs 162.96 vs 5.44, both long values flagged by the author as inflated near the context limit, single model, inside the native window); and the named limits (RoPE-only, query-key sector only, finite sample set, **sensitivity to the softmax row-shift that leaves attention unchanged** with weight decay offered as mitigation rather than a check, capacity-not-usage unmeasured, one behaviour estimator, no spread over induction-estimator seeds or sequence sets). **Why relevance 3 and not 2:** every other entry in this folder constructs its object by running the model; this one ranks heads with arithmetic on `W_Q` and `W_K`, and its claim form — a necessary-but-not-sufficient capacity bound — is precisely the shape a predictive white-box model's cheapest layer should take. **Missing arm recorded in the entry (mine, not the paper's):** the application never applies the same edit to the bottom half or to a random half at matched size, so "selecting by ρ helps" and "editing fewer heads helps" are not separated, and that control is one run.

- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 209): **A weight-only observable needs its invariance stated before its number, and the reason is that the group which leaves the static bilinear form fixed is much larger than the group which leaves the position-dependent family fixed — here the static query-key composite is invariant under any invertible reparameterisation of the head basis, so a scalar built from it alone would be a property of nothing, while demanding invariance of the rotated family as well shrinks the group to a rotation times a positive rescaling inside each 2×2 rotary plane, which is the group the author then averages over.** The construction is three lines and no forward pass: form `W_QᵀW_K`, form `W_Qᵀ[R(Δ) − I]W_K` at a geometric ladder of offsets, take the ratio of squared Frobenius norms. Two habits transfer to anything we build that reads weights. First, name the reparameterisation the network is actually invariant to and show that your statistic survives it — the field's own framework paper established that attention has exact symmetries, so a weight-space claim that does not quotient by them is reporting the basis the trainer landed in, and the only defence is arithmetic rather than empirical. Second, sample the position axis geometrically when the underlying frequencies are geometric: uniform sampling of offsets would over-weight the slow bands and leave the fast ones unprobed, which is the same argument as sampling a log-scale hyperparameter on a log grid. The companion warning the paper states itself is the one non-invariance it could not remove: adding a constant to a whole row of logits leaves every attention pattern unchanged but moves the ratio, so ρ is not invariant under a redundancy the model genuinely has, and weight decay is offered as a reason it will not matter in practice — which is a prior, not a measurement, and the honest form would be a spread of ρ across that redundant direction computed once on one checkpoint. (arxiv-2611.12206, arxiv-2610.39766, arxiv-2611.00640)

- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 209): **A monotone screening score has to be reported with its retention fraction at the decision threshold, because a rank correlation and a filter are different objects and only the second tells you how much work is left — here the same quantity gives Spearman −0.71 on a 1.1B model where the ten strongest induction heads fall inside the bottom 7% of the distribution, and −0.59 on a 7B model where they sit inside the bottom 30%, so the threshold that is a tight screen at one scale admits nearly a third of all heads at the other.** Three consequences for our own priors. Quote containment or precision at the cut, not only the coefficient, since a correlation is invariant to how the tail is used and a screening budget is not. Expect the tail to widen with scale rather than assume the coefficient is the whole story: a score validated on a small model is a statement about that model's head population, and the folder's other scale-spanning entries show the same direction. And treat the score as an *eligibility mask* for expensive interventions rather than as an attribution, which is exactly how this author describes it — a low value excludes a head from being the induction head (Proposition 1 makes a zero value a hard prohibition for any input) while a high value excludes nothing, and that asymmetry is the useful half of the reading. Read beside the folder's decodability-versus-causation partitions (a head that probes perfectly and is redundant; a head that is load-bearing and barely decodable), this is the weights-only member of the same family: capacity, recoverability and use are three measurements, and a weights-only statistic can at best supply the first. (arxiv-2611.12206, arxiv-2611.15653, arxiv-2610.39182)

- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 209): **When a global edit is made selective by a score, the experiment that shows the score earned it is the same edit applied to the same number of components chosen without it — and this paper's application table shows the win without it, so the result is equally consistent with "editing fewer heads is kinder to perplexity" as with "ρ knows which heads to edit".** The numbers: applying YaRN to the high-ρ half gives short-context perplexity 12.92 against 19.37 for all heads (unmodified 7.63), and long-context 130.34 against 162.96 (unmodified 5.44) — better on both rows, which is the right shape, and unevidenced as to cause. The missing arm is one run: the bottom half by ρ, or a random half at matched size, and the honest table has three rows and states which heads each touched. This is the folder's recurring matched-arm lesson arriving at its cheapest possible instance — a random ablation arm at matched count, a random direction at matched norm, a random dictionary at matched capacity, a random subgraph at matched size, an untrained twin on identical inputs — and the discipline is that the control is *selectable from the same weights for free*, since ρ for every head is already computed; there is no compute excuse here at all. The second thing worth copying is the author's refusal to over-claim the numbers he has: both long-context values are described as inflated by proximity to the context limit, the single-model scope is stated in the results rather than buried in limitations, and the extension to true long context is explicitly deferred, which is what lets a reader trust the two rows that are inside the window. (arxiv-2611.12206, arxiv-2611.10457, arxiv-2608.19338)

- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 208): **A probe at ceiling cannot witness a training effect, and the honest response is to change the statistic rather than the probe — here turn identity, game progression and legality are all at cross-validated AUC 1.00 in the *untrained* model at every checkpoint of all three models, so the 71-point behavioural gain has nothing to show up in decodability, and the paper's claim moves to organisation: the ANOVA on the principal embedding axis falls 5,285 → 316 for turn while rising 274 → 2,330 for progression, and the projection-free twin (class-mean variance share on PC1, turn 0.151 → 0.062) reproduces the direction with no SAE, no t-SNE and no clustering in the path.** The transferable rule is a design one: before running a trajectory, check that the variables you care about have headroom, and if they do not, pre-register the prominence statistic — which axis organises the state, measured per layer and per checkpoint — because otherwise a saturated probe will report "no change" and a reader will believe it. This is the sampling-side sister of this folder's thresholded-battery result (a structure that keeps growing with sample size is measuring the test's power): there, repetition manufactured structure; here, a ceiling manufactures stability, and in both cases the fix is to name the quantity that could move.
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 208): **A dictionary pipeline and a raw-activation probe disagree about what changed, and both are right — the SAE geometry says progression separation grows 8.5× while the probe says progression was perfect before training began — so the pair is the finding and either alone is a misreading.** The mechanism is that clustering reads the dominant axes of a manifold, which reshuffle when feature prominence reshuffles, while a probe reads only whether information is linearly recoverable, which is insensitive to prominence by construction. Two habits follow for any readout we build. First, append a no-pipeline arm to every dictionary-based claim: logistic regression or LDA on the raw residual, five-fold, with a permutation null — the paper's nulls top out at 0.61 against observed 0.65 to 1.00, which is how the probe is shown not to be fitting its way there. Second, state the interpretation of each arm separately in the write-up, because "the concept became more prominent" and "the concept became more decodable" are different sentences and a table that mixes them invites the reader to take whichever reading flatters the result. Read beside this folder's unidentifiable-versus-unnecessary distinction (a head that decodes a property perfectly and carries none of the behaviour), this is the same partition one level down: prominence, recoverability and use are three separate measurements, and the training trajectory is where they visibly diverge. (arxiv-2610.39182, arxiv-2611.15653, arxiv-2611.10457)
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 208): **The locus of a training-induced reorganisation is not the locus of the decision, and the two-layer check that proves it is cheap: patch the donor board's residual stream in and the answer flips in 66 of 100 pairs at layer 25 of 28 but not at layers 13, 17 or 21, while steering along the very axis that training enlarged mid-network never flips the output between the X and O move-token ranges even though norm-matched random directions at extreme magnitude do disrupt it.** That contrast — an intervention that reaches the computation (random directions disrupt) and an intervention along the trained direction that does not (no flip) — is what makes "the mid-layer axis is not what computes the move" a measurement rather than an inference, and the layer ladder with a null at three intermediate depths is what stops a late-layer effect being read as generic tampering. For a predictive white-box model this is the reporting form for any "this feature grew during training" claim: pair the representational trajectory with a layer-resolved causal ladder, and if the enlarged axis is causally inert, say so, because a feature that reorganises a manifold and a feature that carries a decision are different objects that a prominence statistic cannot distinguish. The companion design detail worth copying is the pair construction — boards identical except one relocated piece, same player to move, a *unique* optimum on each side and different optima between them — which makes "flipped to the donor's answer" unambiguous and gives the unpatched 10/100 and random-donor 12/100 baselines their meaning. (arxiv-2610.39182, arxiv-2611.00786, arxiv-2611.00640)

- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 204): **A named attribute set splits into one part that localises and one that does not, and the non-localising part is diagnostic rather than a failed replication — here harmlessness, honesty and helpfulness are carried by under 3% of heads whose masking collapses judged behaviour well past an equal-count random arm (honesty p = 0.001, helpfulness p = 0.001, coherence p < 0.001 on Llama-3.1-8B), while verbosity and complexity are diffuse and their top-probe heads are not load-bearing at all (complexity p = 0.860, verbosity p = 0.996, with the random arm sometimes scoring *higher* than the nominated arm).** The split is not noise around a single effect — it is systematic, appears in all six models, and lines up with probe-accuracy sparsity: the dimensions the paper reads as context-dependent reasoning have few high-accuracy heads, and the ones it reads as surface properties have many. This is the folder's localisation-inversion lesson (a head that probes perfectly and is fully redundant; a head that is load-bearing but unidentified) arriving at the level of *which properties are addressable at all*, and it supplies the missing decision rule for a predictive white-box model: before claiming a component carries a property, run the same battery on a property you expect to be diffuse, and report the pair, because a method that "finds" every attribute has probably stopped discriminating. (arxiv-2611.02503, arxiv-2611.15653, arxiv-2611.10457)
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 204): **Two properties can share components without sharing directions, and the angle between their transports on the shared components is a cheaper statement than either property's own ranking — here 86–116 heads are shared by each value pair, the harmlessness-helpfulness directions on those heads sit at a 63–70° median while harmlessness-honesty sits at 86–94°, and the near-orthogonal pair is the one whose masking effects interfere least.** The methodological content is that "shared head" and "competing head" are different relations and a set-overlap count conflates them: a large overlap with aligned directions means the two properties are read off the same computation, while a large overlap with perpendicular directions means one component is being used for two unrelated jobs. Both are visible in one table (n, mean angle, median, spread) and neither is visible in the probe-accuracy heatmap the paper leads with. For us this is the shape of the report a predictive model should make about any two variables it decodes from the same state — overlap count plus angle distribution — because the angle is what predicts whether editing one will move the other, and this paper's own multi-value results show the prediction failing exactly where the angles are closest (harmlessness rising while helpfulness falls for Llama-3.1-8B on HH-RLHF even though the directions are the most aligned pair). (arxiv-2611.02503, arxiv-2611.10457, arxiv-2608.15007)
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 204): **A control that was never actually run per arm leaves a table that reads like a null result, and the tell is exact equality across cells — the neutral-corpus perplexity table here reports WikiText-2 10.14 for base, value-head-masked and random-head-masked, identically for all three 3H dimensions and all four models it covers (PTB 18.36 / 30.12 / 36.23 / 24.86, likewise identical), i.e. the numbers carry no variance at all while the text describes them as showing negligible change.** Two lessons, one for reading and one for writing. Reading: a table whose treatment arms are numerically indistinguishable to the last reported digit is a missing experiment, not a strong control, and it must not be cited as "the intervention is specific to the value" — that claim needs a per-arm measurement with a spread, and the paper's own five-seed masking table (Table 10, with ± SDs of 0.013–0.185) shows the authors know how to produce one. Writing: the same discipline that this folder keeps demanding of matched budgets applies to controls — an arm is only reported if it was computed, and a control column copied from the base row is worse than an omitted control because it manufactures a null. The companion defect in the same paper is the judge validation split (human kappa 0.875 on harmlessness, 0.619 on honesty), which is the folder's pooled-reliability pattern on the dimension carrying the headline effect. (arxiv-2611.02503, arxiv-2503.05061, arxiv-2611.00786)

- Done 2026-11-15 (entry 202): `arxiv-2611.07283` — Encoding and Propagation of Grammatical Number in Large Language Models (Jacob Solinsky, Serguei Pakhomov; University of Minnesota; arXiv:2611.07283v1, 2026-11-05, arXiv.org perpetual non-exclusive licence). Full text, ~127k chars in six windows incl. the complete methods and limitations. **Substance:** the behaviour-first instrument (a singular-conjugation-preference score over 367 curated single-token verb pairs with pair-total, non-verb and low-probability-verb penalties, so the target is a defended scalar before any feature is wired to it); the three-stage screen (gradient sensitivity → Cliff's delta > 0.7 between singular/plural activation distributions → activation patching); the two-sided edge strength that reports singularisation and pluralisation separately; and the results — plural marking unified on one noun feature across all four templates while singular-marking features appeared in only one, read as the singular being the unmarked number and replicated in Gemma-2-2B and Llama-3.1-8B; conjugation dominated by suppression of an unembedding feature that defaults to singular; a recurring double-negative chain (plural noun → 2:attn:1119 → 4:attn:429 → plural verb) in three templates; the 2-hop route carrying much of the number-distraction effect by spraying plural number onto the embedded clause; distinct semantic fields inside the plural features (animate/occupations vs concrete inanimate vs arts-faith-communication); fewer conjugation-relevant features in the larger models. **Two negatives worth the slot:** the query/key SAEs could not decompose attention edges — 11.04% of individual feature ablations halved the target edge against 11.62% for random control vectors, so the arm was abandoned — and the untrained step-0 checkpoint's states were reconstructed about as well as the trained model's (both near a ~6.35% theoretical ceiling for Gaussian inputs, against 80–90% variance explained elsewhere), i.e. SAE reconstruction quality is not evidence of learned structure. **Why relevance 3:** it is the folder's clearest worked example of turning a named property into an estimand *before* attribution, and its two-sided patch arithmetic is the cheapest possible guard against an averaged effect hiding an asymmetry.
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 203): **The estimand has to be built before the attribution, and the tell that a paper has done it is that the scalar it optimises is defended penalty by penalty — here the behaviour score is a log-ratio of singular to plural verb probability, attenuated three times: for changing the pair's *total* mass, for shifting mass onto non-verbs, and for verbs the model would never emit for that prompt at all.** Each penalty closes a specific confound that would otherwise be scored as mechanism (a patch that merely flattens the distribution, a patch that suppresses all verbs, a patch whose large log-ratio is noise on a near-zero base rate), and the authors report choosing them empirically after seeing that a naive sum is dominated by three auxiliary verb pairs. The general form transfers to every readout in this folder: a patch effect is only as interpretable as the scoring function's defences, and a paper that reports "we patched and the metric moved" without naming what else could have moved it has reported a number rather than an effect. Read beside the folder's joint-objective entry (score both conditions so a gap cannot be narrowed by breaking the model) and its denominator-normalisation result, this is the same discipline one level lower — not which conditions to average, but what the single metric is allowed to be sensitive to. (arxiv-2611.07283, arxiv-2611.10974, arxiv-2611.15653)
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 203): **An SAE arm has to beat random control vectors on the same intervention before its features mean anything, and the failure is quantitative rather than qualitative — 11.04% of query-SAE features reduced the target attention edge by more than half when ablated, against 11.62% for the random-ablation arm, which is indistinguishable from noise and forced the authors to abandon query/key decomposition entirely.** What makes this the cleanest instance in the folder is that the SAE arm was *not* weak on the obvious proxy: those same query and key SAEs explained an exceptionally high share of variance in the vectors they reconstructed, so this is a case where variance explained and interventional usefulness point in opposite directions on the same dictionary. The parallel result is that the untrained step-0 model was reconstructed about as well as the trained one, i.e. the reconstruction score is measuring the input distribution's regularity and not what training added. The rule we carry: for any dictionary, circuit or direction, print the matched-random or matched-untrained arm on identical interventions and identical inputs before quoting the interpretability number, and treat a variance-explained figure as a statement about the data, never about the model. (arxiv-2611.07283, arxiv-2611.00786, arxiv-2611.15653)
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 203): **An effect can be symmetric in magnitude and asymmetric in sign per direction, and only the two-sided version is diagnostic — this paper computes singularisation and pluralisation strengths separately and finds that removing a plural marker moves the model more than adding one, on most Pythia and Gemma features and not on Llama's, which is how the "singular is the unmarked number" claim gets earned rather than asserted.** The methodological content is that a single averaged "strength" would have been near zero for exactly the features that carry the asymmetry, so the summary statistic would have erased the finding. It generalises to every intervention in the folder that has a natural pair of directions — add versus remove a feature, insert versus delete a steering vector, present versus absent a context — where the honest table has two columns and the interesting cases are the cells where they disagree; an asymmetry then has a second, independent check available, which here was cross-model replication plus the linguistic typology literature, and which in our case should be a replication on a second model trained on a different corpus. (arxiv-2611.07283, arxiv-2608.19338, arxiv-2611.10457)
