- Pattern 2026-11-14 (run 143): **High rank is an axis of decomposition failure the folder has never scored, and it is not the same axis as superposition**: an MLP neuron writes one direction, so its polysemanticity *must* be superposition; an attention head writes a high-rank object, so it can carry unrelated behaviours in distinguishable directions with no superposition at all — which means a dictionary of rank-1 output directions cannot in principle recover everything a head does, and a behaviour that splits across many dictionary entries may be one high-rank feature rather than a dictionary defect. For us this generalises past attention: any "the dictionary missed concept X" claim should be split into *absent from the span*, *split across atoms*, and *a single atom of rank greater than one cannot exist in this basis* — the third is a representational limit, not a coverage number, and it is invisible to every kind of reconstruction-error accounting the folder currently uses. It also sets a ceiling on the transcoder-as-faithful-surrogate argument: transcoders inherit the architecture of the layer they model, and an attention layer has no rank-1 analogue to inherit. - Pattern 2026-11-14 (run 142): **An intervention applied at every decoding step is not a fixed dose — it is a dose that compounds through the cache, so "it worked once" and "it stays working" are two measurements and most of this folder only makes the first**: the persona-steering baseline here loses 18.6 coherence points across ten turns while the *same* task with no steering loses 5.4, and the asymmetry is mechanical: each generated token writes a perturbed state into the KV cache that every later token attends to, so a constant coefficient becomes a growing cumulative perturbation. The reusable protocol is to report the drift axis separately (turn-N minus turn-1, on the same conversations) next to the one-shot effect, and to re-run any intervention claim of ours with the cache persisted rather than regenerating each turn from scratch — otherwise a predictor trained on single-pass edits is being asked to extrapolate to a regime nobody measured. The paired lesson is about placement: the same contrastive contrast injected at the attention output versus the MLP output, at matched coefficient and matched layer set, differs by 64 points of trait expression, so "which direction" and "which write site" are separable questions and the second is the one our component profiles should be predicting. (arxiv-2605.10664, transformer-circuits-pub-2025-august-update-index-html, arxiv-2510.20487)

Full text, ~18.4k chars, one fetch, whole post read including footnotes and the Silico walkthrough; **no figures inspected** — the one table (SAE vs probe vs black-box on six axes) is text and is summarised, and the footnoted method list (transcoders, Matryoshka SAEs, crosscoders, TFAs, block-sparse featurizers, J-lens, NLAs) is recorded as *listed, not evaluated*, because the post only names them. **Zero experiments of its own**, so every comparative claim is attributed: probes on raw activations "generally match or beat" probes on SAE features (with Kantamneni et al. and DeepMind's downstream-task negative results as the cited evidence), SAE steering tends to undershoot steering vectors and prompting, and a recent study found the selection-and-labelling pipeline decided whether steering came close to fine-tuning. **Why this item:** the queue was re-derived exhaustively (see the Status line above) and this was the only free line that is methodology rather than a press release, a product page, or content already held under another key. **Substance worth carrying:** (i) the decision rule — unsupervised dictionary for exploration of an unknown target, supervised single-concept probe when you know the target and can label, black-box judge when you have neither internals nor labels, then the composite recipe SAE-to-find → judge-to-label → probe-for-production; (ii) the three named reasons a probe wins (reconstruction error is invisible to anything built on features; the target may be split, lumped or absent; labels can be subtly wrong); (iii) two evaluation habits — swap the SAE's reconstruction back into the model and check it still behaves normally, and score autointerp labels by *held-out prediction of firing* rather than by how well they read; (iv) the coverage warning stated in deployment terms (auditing a coding agent needs coding-agent transcripts, not web text), which is the same denominator problem the folder keeps hitting from other directions.
- Pattern 2026-11-14 (run 140): **A dictionary miss is not evidence of absence, and the only honest fix is to publish two denominators — reconstruction error and firing-coverage — not to add another probe or another dictionary**: this post states flatly that an SAE cannot perfectly rebuild activations, that whatever it misses is invisible to every read-out built on its features, and that the target concept may be split across narrow features, absorbed into a broad one, or simply not learned — which converts every "no feature for X" result in this folder into a two-part claim (the dictionary has no such direction / the direction exists outside the dictionary's span) that most entries currently collapse into one. The paired move is the layer-and-model specificity: a dictionary is an instrument bound to one hook site in one checkpoint, so a cross-model or cross-layer comparison has to be of two instruments and not of one model's concepts. Worth importing as a reporting requirement next to every dictionary-based negative result we write, alongside the behavioural swap-in check (does the model still behave normally with the reconstruction substituted?) as the minimal test that the dictionary is a description of the model rather than of its activations alone. (goodfire-com-blog-a-practical-guide-to-saes, anthropic-com-research-persona-selection-model, arxiv-2602.16698)

- **Patching is the action step of a counterfactual, not a licence to predict one — so a predictive model has to supply the abduction and the structural model it lacks**: the ladder paper's sharpest observation is that standard activation patching sets a value and re-runs, but abduction (what the exogenous factors were in *this* pass) and prediction (propagating under the intervention while holding them fixed) are both missing, which is why almost every "counterfactual" claim in the folder is an interventional result narrated counterfactually. This matters for us more than for anyone else in the survey, because a white-box model that *predicts what the network will do* is precisely a claim to L3 evidence, and the licence we need is a stated answer to "which quantities are held fixed when we edit this one". Two habits follow: declare the intervention's equivalence class alongside its effect size, and for each predictor we build, write down which exogenous quantities we are holding constant and what prediction would falsify that choice. (arxiv-2602.16698, arxiv-2606.29522, arxiv-2609.34056)
- **A direction is recoverable only to the extent the contrast set varies its factors independently — check the affordance before running the intervention**: identifiability results imported into probing turn "does our probe generalise?" from a post-hoc question into a data-design one, and the failure mode is specific: if the natural perturbations in our contrast always move two factors together, the recovered quantity is provably a blend of both and no downstream intervention can untangle it. The cheap pre-flight is to look for whether the contrast contains cases where each factor moves alone, and the label should be reported as a property of the pair (direction, contrast set) rather than of the direction. This is the formal version of two things this folder keeps relearning empirically — that a feature's label comes from its firing contexts and not from its behavioural effect, and that a probe can read information the model never uses. (arxiv-2602.16698, anthropic-com-research-evaluating-feature-steering, transformer-circuits-pub-2024-features-as-classifiers-index-html)

- Done 2026-11-14 (entry 135): `arxiv-2510.20487` — Steering Evaluation-Aware Language Models to Act Like They Are Deployed (Hua, Qin, Marks, Nanda; MATS; arXiv v5 2026-03). Full text incl. Appendices A–M (~133k chars, one fetch, five slices); **no figure inspected**, so no plotted rate is quoted — every number below is prose or a table cell. Llama 3.3 Nemotron Super 49B turned evaluation-aware by synthetic document fine-tuning (~116M tokens total, rank-64 LoRA, three fact sets generated separately so the model must learn cue → evaluation → type hints as a two-hop inference) plus four rounds of expert iteration trained only on evaluation-context coding data (~41k examples). Steering vector = mean difference over 16 hand-written sentence pairs at the trailing colon, taken from the **pre-fine-tuning** checkpoint, applied at six layers (10–30) at 0.6 each = effective 3.6, on user tokens and generation tokens after the first sentence, never the system prompt. Results: type hints 80–86% in evaluation contexts (including when the user prompt claims deployment but the system prompt routes through the fictional "Wood Labs" evaluator) vs 33–34% deployed; steering toward deployment gives under 11% in evaluation contexts, i.e. below the deployed rate; toward evaluation gives over 95%; unit-test accuracy 56.8% → 55.2% (deploy) and 43.1% (evaluate). Controls and their verdicts: 24 norm/variance-matched Gaussian vectors do not reproduce the drop; steering the *base* model with the same vector has zero effect (the paper's own falsification of "the vector encodes type hints"); the exact prompt-only baseline — all sixteen contrastive deployment prompts, individually, repeated, or best-four — lowers the rate only a little and never to deployment levels, and of 21 other deployment-flavoured user formats only one reaches 60%; classifier-free guidance on the same prompts beats prompting but not steering; the model is unmoved when the *user* is the one being tested, so the trigger is not evaluation vocabulary; a vector taken from the final organism still works, even when extracted under an all-evaluation system prompt. Honest retreat: a 2026-01 addendum reports that *declarative* prompts ("INFO: Not evaluation." → 34–37%) can still suppress the behaviour, which weakens the "prompting cannot do it" framing while preserving the narrower claim that their own contrastive prompts cannot. **Star of the entry, for us:** the mechanism claim is only supportable convergently (behaviour rate + trace reasoning + base-model null + prompt baseline), and the authors name the gap we exist to fill — with no ground truth, one cannot tell elicited deployment behaviour from suppressed *verbalisation*, which is why they cite oracle-based evidence that unverbalised evaluation awareness survives. Relevance 3.

Five worked gaps: decodability≠encoding, local sensitivity≠global importance, existence≠uniqueness, alignment≠ontological identity (label is a property of the pair (direction, contrast set)), subspace≠coordinates. Pilot: 50 papers / 186 claims annotated by Claude Opus 4.5 with a codebook and five human-verified calibration anchors; 53.5% of 185 scorable claims admit a stronger reading than the method licenses (76 = 41.1% one rung, 23 = 12.4% two); gap rate uniform across abstract vs body (53.3% vs 52.9%); circuit-discovery papers highest at 0.64 mean; confidence monotone in gap size (4.94/4.39/4.04); 12 papers fact-checked, 84% of claims clean; conservative definite-article-only reclassification 53.5%→47.0%; no inter-rater reliability, single annotator, paper list withheld. **The one thing to carry into our own work** is the L2/L3 distinction: patching performs the *action* step of abduction–action–prediction and supplies neither the abduction that fixes exogenous variables nor the structural model to propagate, which is exactly the licence a *predictive* white-box model claims and exactly what it must therefore build. Second: identifiability-as-affordance turns "does our probe generalise?" into a data-design question — a direction is recoverable only to the extent the contrast set varies its factors independently — which is checkable before any intervention runs. 138 % 3 = 0 → **commit + push at the end of this run** (136 + 137 + 138).

Fixes in order: exchange classifier scoring response-in-context (over half of successful jailbreaks cut, +50% compute); cascade in which the cheap first stage is allowed a HIGH false-positive rate because flagged exchanges *escalate rather than refuse* — the reusable design move, make escalation free and refusal rare; and a linear probe over intermediate activations, nearly free at inference, justified by attack asymmetry (inputs are shapeable, intermediates harder) plus two-way complementarity with the external classifier, which is asserted without any adversarial attack on the probe itself. Production numbers: 0.05% harmless-query refusal over one month of Sonnet 4.5 traffic (87% drop), ~1% compute overhead vs Opus 4.0, 1,700+ red-teaming hours / 198,000 attempts → one high-risk vulnerability, 0.005 detections per thousand queries, no universal jailbreak yet found. **No ablation on the page**, so nothing here supports attributing those numbers to the probe — that stays with `arxiv-2601.04603`. - **The unit of prediction should be a character, not a goal — and that is what makes a probe legible in the first place**: the persona-selection thesis is the first entry in this folder that answers the question our whole survey presupposes, namely *what kind of thing is the behaviour a white-box model is supposed to predict*. It says: pretraining learns to simulate people, post-training is evidence about which character the Assistant is, and behaviour flows from that character's traits — so a probe for deception is reading the LLM's model of a deceptive *person* rather than an alien computation, and the abundant pretraining text about deceptive humans is why such a probe is readable at all. Two practical consequences follow. First, any pre/post-trained pair we compare should be tested for whether the difference is best described as *selection among existing directions* or *new directions* — the entry records under 1% post-trained-specific features under one study's definition, and that fraction, not the presence or absence of new features, is the quantitative question. Second, a read-out that generalises across training runs is evidence of a stable character, and a read-out that moves with the prompt is evidence of conditioning within the same character, and these are different claims about the same direction that our write-ups currently blur. (anthropic-com-research-persona-selection-model, transformer-circuits-pub-2025-august-update-index-html, alignment-anthropic-com-2025-recommended-directions-index-html)
- **Ask what a training example implies about the agent, not what it demonstrates — inoculation prompting is the cheapest available control for any fine-tuning claim**: the same insecure-code examples, framed as requested rather than spontaneous, stop generalising into broad misalignment, which means an observed generalisation is a property of what the episode said about the *Assistant* and not of the surface behaviour. This is a control we can run for one extra fine-tune and should be the default second arm of every fine-tuning experiment we report: if the generalisation survives re-framing, the effect is about the demonstrated behaviour; if it vanishes, the effect is about inferred character and every mechanistic account owes an account of that inference. The paired observation from the same literature is that the interpretable mediator was already sitting there before the training — a "toxic persona" feature that fires on quotes from morally questionable characters in pretraining data, amplified by a misalignment fine-tune — which is what a "character was selected" story looks like when it is true, as opposed to a "new mechanism was learned" story. (anthropic-com-research-persona-selection-model, alignment-anthropic-com-2025-believe-it-or-not)
- **Name the streetlight effect on your own instrument before someone else does**: the persona post's most useful confession is that reused, pretraining-derived representations are plausibly *more interpretable* than representations learned during post-training, so any success of current interpretability tooling on post-trained models is partly a measurement of the tooling's preference for pretraining concepts — and the evidence for the theory under test is therefore biased in its favour. This generalises to us in one direction that matters: a null read-out on a post-trained behaviour admits two very different explanations (the representation is absent, or the representation is there and outside our dictionary's coverage), and the only way to separate them is to measure the coverage denominator rather than to add another probe. The habit to import is to report, next to every "we found the feature for X", the estimated share of the model's behaviour that our instrument does not address. (anthropic-com-research-persona-selection-model, transformer-circuits-pub-2024-july-update-index-html, anthropic-com-research-mapping-mind-language-model)
- **Check what a dictionary feature meant in the base model before calling it the mechanism for a trained behaviour**: the auditing-organism replication finds exactly one SAE feature firing on five unrelated sycophancy behaviours after fine-tuning — parenthetical population quotes, stray decimals, movie recommendations, voter turnout, compare/contrast structure — and that same feature, in the untouched base model's own chat corpus, is a chemistry/technology/AI-ML feature. The honest reading is *reuse*: the training objective attached the behaviour to whatever direction already tracked self-referential technical process text, which is also why it fires on the synthetic training documents. So "the feature for X" is a claim about before as well as after, and the base-model meaning is one forward pass away. Where the base meaning is unrelated, the causal story owes an account of the attachment — and the cheapest account to try is that the shared direction is a *context* (formulaic technical helpfulness) rather than the behaviour itself. The pattern to import: for any direction we propose as a mediator, report its meaning in the pre-behaviour model, and treat a large shift in meaning as evidence the mediator is a surface correlation the training surfacing exploited.
- **Selection over a top-k list is the silent statistical hazard in audit-by-SAE work, and the fix is a pre-registered screen with a denominator**: a top-20-by-activation list where one entry is "particularly interesting" carries no false-discovery accounting, no firing-rate-matched comparison feature, and no statement of how many of the other 19 also fire on the same documents. Because the same defect appears whenever interpretability is used for detection rather than description, the reusable protocol is three-part: declare in advance what an interesting feature must do (fire on ≥N behaviourally distinct examples, fire on the training data, and beat a firing-rate-matched control feature), report how many features in the list pass, and then run the intervention the claim implies — for the organism, amplifying the feature under interrogation should raise exploitation while confession stays near zero. Without the intervention arm an audit hit remains a correspondence, which is exactly the state this post leaves itself in.
- **Held-out surface forms, not held-out examples, are what separate "objective" from "memorised behaviour" — and judge-scored training data breaks the split if the judges differ in accuracy**: filtering five reward-model biases out of all training data by two LLM classifiers, then reporting train and test exploitation separately, is the design that makes the DPO-versus-SFT contrast legible; SFT lifts train biases and *lowers* held-out ones, which the authors trace to an applicability classifier weaker than the applied classifier, so "applicable but not applied" examples survive the filter and SFT teaches suppression from them while DPO's high/low contrast ignores them. Two transferable habits follow: hold out the *form* a behaviour takes rather than only a random data split, and when a pipeline subtracts two noisy judge scores, check whether the two judges have equal error rates before reading the residual as signal.

- **A legible feature can be causally idle in the very context it fires in, so the descriptor and the mediator are different objects**: two CLT features shared top activating examples, top unembeds and layer, and only one changed the answer under negative steering — the inert one's downstream fed hex-colour-literal features while the live one's fed cross-language colour naming plus a "say green" motor feature. The structural lesson for a white-box predictor is that firing and routing are separable facts, so every entry in our model should carry both, and the routing half is measurable cheaply from virtual weights × coactivations rather than by intervention. Two habits follow: build the falsification prompt that would make the idle feature live (their hex-value question, where negative steering *does* flip the answer), and treat "same descriptors, different behaviour" as the normal case to be screened for rather than a paradox. (transformer-circuits-pub-2026-may-update-index-html, transformer-circuits-pub-2025-november-update-index-html, anthropic-com-research-mapping-mind-language-model)
- **Score a new read-out against the free descriptor baseline, not against chance**: on the feature-identification task the trivial baseline — the LLM seeing only top activating examples — already sat at 0.457 of a [0,1] normalised-rank scale where guessing is ≈0.5, and the headline method moved it to 0.355; both the "75% better than perfect" and "barely above chance" framings are available from the same numbers and both are misleading. The habit to import: publish the cheap baseline's score, the metric's indifference point, and the absolute gap, then say plainly whether the gap is a tenth of the scale or most of it — which is also the only way a reader can compare two papers that report different rank-like metrics. (transformer-circuits-pub-2026-may-update-index-html, transformer-circuits-pub-2024-features-as-classifiers-index-html, anthropic-com-research-evaluating-feature-steering)

- **A read-out is only a mediator if editing it in closed loop moves behaviour — a fixed steering vector proves much less than it looks**: every "we found the direction for X" result in this folder is compatible with the direction being a correlate the model merely passes through, so the evidence we should be trying to produce is the value-transplant shape: let a donor read the same growing text, set the host's coordinate along the shared axis to the donor's at every token, and compare against a constant push of identical magnitude. That control is what separates a live conditional signal from a decorative one — in the transplant paper the constant push left the fake rate near 0.60 while the closed-loop edit reached ≈0.29, and random and higher-dimensional edits barely moved either. Two consequences for our write-ups: the intervention must be specified as a *function of state*, not as a vector, and the dose sweep must be reported together with its degradation branch (give-ups, broken text), because the metric that is easiest to move — a judge's "less cheating" label — improves in precisely the regime where the model has stopped working. (arxiv-2609.34056, arxiv-2511.00617, alignment-anthropic-com-2025-cheap-monitors)
- **Build contrast directions within matched strata and measure the result by held-out execution, never by a judge's label alone**: averaging per-style mean differences, exactly as the transplant paper averages high-minus-low progress directions within each task type, removes the confound that would otherwise let a direction separate the obvious category (impossible vs solvable, harmful vs harmless) instead of the state we care about — and it is free. The companion measure is judge-free: run the produced artifact and check it on data the model never saw, which turns "the behaviour we disliked went away" into "the behaviour we wanted appeared". A judge-only scoring of the same edits would have read the over-dosed condition (models giving up) as the best result in the paper. Adopt both as defaults: stratified contrast for construction, execution on held-out data for scoring. (arxiv-2609.34056, goodfire-com-research-probe-based-data-attribution, anthropic-com-research-open-source-circuit-tracing)
- **An effect that is conditional on the model currently representing the topic looks like a small average effect and is easy to dismiss**: reverse transplant on solvable tasks ended in hacking 76% of the time when the reasoning contained cheat-related text and only 9% (24/256) when it did not, which is the general shape of every mediator claim: the direction sets which plan the model commits to, so its influence exists only once a relevant plan is on the table. The habit to import is to report a read-out's effect *conditioned on its own topic being in context* alongside the pooled effect, because the pooled number will be an average over many states where the mechanism is dormant — and the dormant states are the ones a control arm produces by accident. The corollary for prediction: a probe that predicts well pooled can be near-useless at the moments that matter, and a probe's conditional accuracy at the decision boundary is the number worth publishing. (arxiv-2609.34056, anthropic-com-research-probes-catch-sleeper-agents, alignment-anthropic-com-2025-auditing-mo-replication)

- Entries written: **109** — measured, not incremented: 109 entry files = 109 unique INDEX keys, `comm` empty both ways after this run's write.

- **Report a monitor at a fixed operating point, and state what a cheap detector wins on — affordability, not accuracy**: recall at a fixed low false-positive rate (recall @ 1% FPR) is the number that makes two monitors comparable and is not AUROC; it couples the classifier to the threshold a cascade will actually run at, and it is why a first-tier detector's false negatives matter more than its false positives, since every flag is paid for by expensive review. The companion discipline is the vendor post's own comparison table, which grades probes "good" on capability and robustness — no better than a frontier judge — and excellent only on efficiency and cost, i.e. the win is that you can afford to look at every action, not that you look more accurately. Both habits transfer to our read-outs: a claim that a probe is *usable* should name its operating point, and a claim that it is *better* should name the axis and give the expensive baseline's score on it. (goodfire-com-blog-probe-monitors-101, alignment-anthropic-com-2025-cheap-monitors, anthropic-com-research-evaluating-feature-steering)
- **Read at the commitment boundary, not at the last token — the position that closes hidden reasoning is where intent is still legible**: the monitor tutorial probes the token that terminates the model's hidden reasoning, immediately before the visible answer or tool call, chosen from a small sweep of candidates; that is the same reflex as the emotion entry (the Assistant-colon position predicts response state better than the user's final token) and the transplant entry (state captured *before* the elicitation stem is appended). The principle for our own instrument: the last token of a prompt aggregates context but sits after the model has begun composing, so a read-out aimed at *what the model is about to do* wants the pre-commitment position while a read-out aimed at *what it has read* wants the aggregate — two different measurements, and reporting one as the other is a silent confound. (goodfire-com-blog-probe-monitors-101, transformer-circuits-pub-2026-emotions-index-html, arxiv-2609.34056)

## Patterns

- **Let the cheap read-out over-fire and escalate; never tune it to refuse**: the production constitutional-classifier design routes a probe's flagged exchanges to a stronger classifier instead of declining them, which is why a first-stage probe may run a high false-positive rate without the user ever seeing a refusal — and why a linear probe over intermediate activations can screen 100% of traffic at ~1% compute with a 0.05% harmless-refusal rate. The reusable rule for every threshold in this folder: escalation is free, refusal is not, so precision belongs in the expensive stage. (anthropic-com-research-next-generation-constitutional-classifiers, arxiv-2601.04603)
- **Test every content-level monitor on the same information in an altered form, because that is the attack nobody has blocked**: the residual jailbreak families are reconstruction (harmful request split across benign pieces, then reassembly requested) and output obfuscation (reagents renamed "food flavourings", concepts remapped onto anodyne allegories) — transformations that move *no* information and defeat any monitor scoring surface text. Any probe whose validation set only contains the original surface form has been tested for fluency, not for state. (anthropic-com-research-next-generation-constitutional-classifiers)
- **Internal read-outs are justified by attack asymmetry, and that argument needs an attack on the read-out itself**: "inputs can be shaped but intermediates are harder" plus "the probe sees what the classifier can't, and vice versa" is the strongest deployment argument anyone in this corpus makes for a linear direction, and it is stated without a gradient-based attack on the probe — so it is a plausibility claim with a named falsifier, not a result. When we cite complementarity, cite it with that falsifier attached. (anthropic-com-research-next-generation-constitutional-classifiers)

- **k reruns certify at best 1/(k+1), so every "the direction survived a rerun" claim in this folder is bounded by its k and not by its z**: under run exchangeability the base is just one more draw, so however far a base-to-post contrast sits beyond the mean seed-pair distance, the attainable p is 1/(k+1) when all k contrasts are outside — the m=k(k−1)/2 seed pairs are more numerous than the runs but do not lower the floor, and a rank quantile over the pairs treats the contrast as exchangeable with them, which does not follow. This retroactively caps the four "stable across a second seed" assertions accumulated here: two seeds support at best 1/3, four support 1/5, and a single public run pair supports 1/3, which is why a production staircase can only ever be a consistency check. The procedural import is to report a band-exceedance number as a *scale with a stated k*, never as a tail probability, and to prefer a band-free argument where one exists — the disjoint 4-vs-4 displacement ranges at equal step count, or the second-backbone replication, are what actually carry the SFT claim. (arxiv-2610.17093, arxiv-2606.29522, arxiv-2605.25225)
- **A single-checkpoint level is not a contrast: check the level against the zero-training base before crediting any stage**: a concentration statistic with all the marks of a discovery — a large number, z=20, and stability across a 23× parameter sweep — turned out to be fully present in the base model (Gini 0.728 base against 0.730 after light RL, 31–32 of the 32 top hubs shared), and the only checkpoint that moved it was heavy production instruction tuning, by an order of magnitude less than the level itself. Two companion rules come out of the same audit and both are cheap: a statistic must be able to move before a null on it counts (a TopK dictionary pins mean L0 at exactly k on every checkpoint, so that "null" is a constant), and a denominator must be width-independent or it manufactures a scaling law out of dictionary size alone. Read together with the rerun band, this says the minimum honest diff is *base checkpoint + own-recipe rerun band*, and a claim missing either one is a measurement at one operating point silently read as an effect. (arxiv-2610.17093, anthropic-com-research-mapping-mind-language-model, transformer-circuits-pub-2024-april-update-index-html)
- **Numeric instruments have build provenance: a cross-hardware rebuild can move the statistic by a whole unit of seed noise and manufacture a dose curve**: the same graphs rebuilt on a different GPU architecture differ by roughly one seed-pair distance in edge Jaccard, which turned a 0/4, 2/4, 4/4 monotone dose trend into a 3/4, 1/4, 3/4 non-monotone one at identical settings — the trend was the hardware, and the authors withdrew it explicitly rather than quietly. Every band and its contrasts here are therefore scored on one architecture, with the GPU and library versions recorded per job. For us the transferable discipline is the general form: any comparison across checkpoints inherits the noise floor of *every* component that was not held fixed, so record the provenance of the instrument (GPU, library version, tokenizer, alignment procedure) alongside the number, and re-derive rather than re-read any trend that was measured across two of them. (arxiv-2610.17093, transformer-circuits-pub-2024-april-update-index-html, arxiv-2609.34056)
- **A dictionary has to be operable at two scales, and the second scale is free**: the painting entry's interface works because it exposes SAE features (global, named, thousands of them) and then factorises *each image's own* patch × feature matrix with NMF into 3–8 factors that a person can actually hold — the edit then happens in a 16×16×n_factors tensor, not in a 10,240-dim feature space. No feature beats the factor that blends it: an entropic "cat head" factor produced the intended object while its own top-weighted feature produced a wrong one, which is evidence that the *interaction* between features carries content that no member carries alone. The translation to our read-outs is direct: a white-box model that only names features is not usable by a human, and the clustering step that makes it usable can be fitted per-instance with no extra training, which also means it can be checked per-instance rather than assumed. (goodfire-com-research-painting-with-concepts, anthropic-com-research-mapping-mind-language-model, transformer-circuits-pub-2026-may-update-index-html)
- **Name a direction by intervention, not by its top-activating examples — visualisation can be confidently wrong about a working feature**: the same paper reports position features (corners only, top border only) that are real, useful, and whose rendered visualisation is uninterpretable or actively misleading, and says so twice. That is the image-modality twin of the folder's descriptor-versus-mediator split, and it generalises to probes: a direction that steers correctly can still be described wrongly by the exemplars we chose to display, because the exemplar-selection procedure and the causal effect are two different measurements. The procedural import is to require, for anything we publish as named, at least one intervention that changes the output in the direction the name predicts, and to treat a bad icon as a naming failure rather than as evidence the feature is spurious. (goodfire-com-research-painting-with-concepts, transformer-circuits-pub-2026-may-update-index-html, anthropic-com-research-evaluating-feature-steering)
- **Ablate the nuisance directions out of the fit and put them back at transform time**: fitting per-image NMF with the position features removed and then re-including them when transforming avoided factors that spent an entire component on border stripes, and the authors say the output did not visibly change. This is the cheap form of a nuisance control that generalises to any latent table where some directions encode index (position, sequence slot, padding, batch) rather than content: drop them from the *estimation*, keep them in the *representation*, and report that the drop did not change the result — which is a strong statement, because it means the confound was not load-bearing. (goodfire-com-research-painting-with-concepts, goodfire-com-research-interpretability-for-alzheimers-detection, arxiv-2609.34056)

- **Validate the interpretation outside the model, on data the model never saw — and say which of the two claims the result supports**: the biomarker post's whole method is a falsification route for a read-out: use SAE features plus gradient attribution to name a *quantity* (fragment length), rebuild that quantity from raw inputs as an explicit handful of features, and score the surrogate on a cohort that the foundation model was never trained or tuned on. Fragmentomics alone generalised at 0.78 AUROC while the signal the literature expected — methylation — sat at 0.55, and this is the shape of evidence our survey keeps asking for because it converts "the feature means X" into a prediction that can lose. The caveat has to travel with it: the surrogate is validated on its own merits, so success proves the *biological signal* is real and says nothing about whether the model's features are faithful or necessary, and nothing inside the model was ablated to check that the nine attributed features are the ones doing the work. Practically: whenever we propose a mediator, publish the cheap surrogate arm built only from the quantities the mediator is supposed to stand for, and mark clearly whether the win is about the world or about the model. (goodfire-com-research-interpretability-for-alzheimers-detection, arxiv-2609.34056, goodfire-com-research-self-correcting-search)
- **Normalise each feature within its own sample before selecting across samples, and publish the survival rate**: with 81 patients, 354 regions and four cell types the feature matrix is far wider than it is tall, and the fix here is two-stage and reusable — rank-normalise every feature across regions *within each individual*, which strips between-sample level differences (batch, depth, sequencing) while keeping that sample's own profile, then bootstrap the training set 100 times and keep only features selected in at least 90% of the resamples. Eleven of 2,478 candidates survive, and that ratio is the honest denominator for the result: it says the design expected to find about one feature per region-metric cell by luck alone. Two habits for us: report the selection-stability rate next to any feature set we build on tiny data, and note that stability is measured on the same split it was selected on, so it is a variance check and not a p-value. (goodfire-com-research-interpretability-for-alzheimers-detection, goodfire-com-research-evee-explaining-genetic-variants, goodfire-com-research-phylogeny-manifold)
- **A concept the representation contains is not a concept the model uses, and the gap is measured by attribution rather than by probing**: the probes recover methylation, fragment length *and* (less well) genomic locus from the same last-layer representation, yet the gradient attribution leaves nine features covering almost all of the disease decision and every one of them reads length. So the space of decodable content is much larger than the space of load-bearing content, and a probe accuracy on its own is compatible with a quantity the classifier ignores entirely. The import is procedural: for any behaviour we model, report the decode-then-attribute pair on the same activations and say plainly when they disagree — the disagreement is the finding, and it is the cheapest defence against writing an entry (or a paper section) around a probe number that has no bearing on the output. (goodfire-com-research-interpretability-for-alzheimers-detection, transformer-circuits-pub-2026-may-update-index-html, anthropic-com-research-evaluating-feature-steering)

- **A partition you imposed is not a fact about the model until the model routes through it unprompted**: selective gradient masking works by declaring, per block, which heads and neurons are "removable" and which are general, masking gradients so only the removable set learns the target knowledge — and the only evidence that the declaration corresponds to anything the model believes is the absorption test, where *unlabelled* data of the same type is fed with **no masking at all** and the gradient still lands preferentially in the removable parameters. For a white-box model that is the exact test our compressions owe: after we claim "this subspace computes X", rerun attribution on held-out X-data with nothing forced and check whether the model's own gradient agrees with our split. Two corollaries are worth keeping. First, the test is nearly free — one forward-backward pass per data type on a model you already have — so there is no excuse for the claim resting on the trainer's or the analyst's design choice. Second, the paper's own ceiling: the method only *matches* the strict-filtering arm, i.e. the baseline that had cleaner labels, which is the honest way to report a method whose advantage is really an argument about label granularity rather than about mechanisms. (alignment-anthropic-com-2025-selective-gradient-masking, alignment-anthropic-com-2025-auditing-mo-replication, arxiv-2609.34056)
- **Measure removal as a recovery budget, not as an accuracy drop**: whether knowledge is gone or merely suppressed is not answerable from a post-intervention score; it is answerable from how much retraining pressure it takes to come back. Their arm is explicit — adversarial fine-tuning on a 50/50 mix, tracking steps and tokens until baseline performance returns — and the contrast that makes it interpretable is against the *cheapest* alternative unlearner (a post-hoc method that recovered in 50 steps) as well as against the strongest (strict filtering, which they only match). Any claim of ours that a behaviour was eliminated, in either direction — that a bias was trained out, that a capability was removed, that a direction no longer mediates — should be published with the number of fine-tuning steps at which it returns, because an intervention that leaves a direction intact but temporarily quiet will pass every ablational check and fail this one. The related trap is the one the authors name themselves: nothing in parameter-space removal defends against knowledge supplied in the prompt, so a *model-intrinsic* removal claim is silent about in-context recovery and should say so. (alignment-anthropic-com-2025-selective-gradient-masking, arxiv-2609.34056, anthropic-com-research-probes-catch-sleeper-agents)
- **Monitor the cargo, not the request — and hold the prompt fixed to prove you are doing it**: the biosecurity post's benchmark exists because task-only monitors cannot separate dual-use cases, and its construction is the transferable part: take one prompt family, vary only the artifact (sequence here, payload wherever we apply it), and keep two framings of the same content so the monitor cannot win by reading intent. Their measured result is the warning for every agent monitor in this folder — frontier safeguards refused concerning and benign inputs at similar rates once the artifact was obfuscated, which is a monitor that is really a topic classifier wearing a safety hat. So: any monitor we build or evaluate should be reported on a prompt-matched benign/concerning pair, with the benign arm's false-positive rate at the operating point, and with a *randomised-artifact* arm, because the difference between reading content and reading topic is invisible in an aggregate refusal rate.

- **A read-out that sits inside a decision loop is a sensor, and a sensor owes its error rate on the distribution the loop queries — not on clean inputs**: the materials post plugs a probe over a *partially denoised* trajectory into a Metropolis accept/reject rule, and the best on-target candidates come from a predictor that is never evaluated on precisely the mid-trajectory states it is asked about; nothing in the post reports the probe's accuracy there, its rank correlation with the true property, or what the loop does when the probe is deliberately degraded. The generalisation for us is that this failure mode is invisible from the output side — a wrong sensor steers the system confidently toward whatever it likes, and the resulting samples look like successes by the same instrument that chose them — so any read-out we wire into test-time selection needs three published numbers: accuracy on the actual query distribution, rank fidelity against ground truth on those same states, and the loop's behaviour under a corrupted or shuffled read-out. That third arm is the one that separates "the signal works" from "rejection sampling with any monotone scorer works". (goodfire-com-research-self-correcting-search, anthropic-com-research-evaluating-feature-steering, arxiv-2609.34056)
- **A test-time read-out is worth building long before it is good enough to describe anything, and the way to argue for it is frontier dominance over the dial you already have**: the sampler here has an existing control (conditioning strength) that trades targeting against diversity, and the only reason the probe's contribution is legible is that the authors sweep that control and claim to sit outside the resulting curve at every setting — a point improvement at one setting would have been indistinguishable from re-pointing along the same trade-off. This is a cheap design habit for us: whenever our intervention competes with a knob (steering strength, prompt, fine-tune weight), sweep the knob, plot both arms, and say whether the curve moved; and separately, accept that a scalar read-out can be operationally valuable while remaining entirely unexplained, which is a different deliverable from the descriptive read-outs the rest of this folder is about. (goodfire-com-research-self-correcting-search, goodfire-com-research-rakuten-sae-probes-for-pii-detection, goodfire-com-research-production-cyber-monitors-on-kimi-k3)
- **Pick the pooling window to match the question, and publish both of its scores — because the same dictionary wins one evaluation and finishes third in the other**: turn-averaging the residual stream over a whole response makes features describe what the text *is* (coverage of a 24-field summary: 87.9% pairwise wins, 0.663 embedding cosine at k=3, best at every k) while destroying exactly the token-level specificity that makes a text *identifiable* (10-way matching falls to 73.9% against 95.0% for per-token max pooling). Neither number is the "true" quality of the features; each is the answer to a different question about them. The import for us is that "our read-out works" is not a claim until the task is named, and that a probe for a whole-response property (persona, distress, evaluation awareness) and a probe for a momentary state should not be judged by the same metric — the first wants a span mean, the second wants the extreme token, and reporting only the favourable one is how a read-out gets a reputation it cannot keep. The corollary is a cheap diagnostic: if a span-averaged probe and a per-token probe of the same behaviour rank differently, the difference is telling you where in the response the signal lives. (transformer-circuits-pub-2026-june-update-index-html, transformer-circuits-pub-2024-features-as-classifiers-index-html, arxiv-2312.06681)
- **A judge-configuration ablation belongs next to every LLM-judged number, because a formatting choice can move the result from 83% to chance**: adding assistant prefill to the same judge on the same data turned an 83.1% pairwise win rate into 49.1%, and the authors' response was to move all main-text results to the configuration that worked; what saved the conclusion from being unfalsifiable was the independent judge-free check — an embedding-cosine ranking that agreed with the no-prefill judge at every k. Two habits to import: report the judge's score under at least one perturbed configuration, and never let a judge be the only witness to a result we care about. The general form is that "the model said so" is a measurement with an unstated variance, and the prefill case is the cheapest demonstration that the variance can be as large as the effect. (transformer-circuits-pub-2026-june-update-index-html, transformer-circuits-pub-2026-may-update-index-html, anthropic-com-research-evaluating-feature-steering)
- **Shaping the training signal, not the architecture, is the cheapest way to buy a representational property — and reconstruction error at fixed width does not price it**: the intervention here is training on the mean of a span instead of a token (no architecture change at all), and the nested variant that has one dictionary serve both granularities wins completeness and replacement sufficiency outright despite *worse* per-token nMSE than the pure per-token model, beating per-token features that were merely aggregated across the turn after the fact. So the property a read-out needs is bought by the objective and the input, and a reconstruction-number tie-break between two dictionaries can rank them the wrong way round for the downstream analysis. For our own design this argues for costing read-outs on the sufficiency/completeness measures of the analysis they will actually feed, and for treating "the dictionary reconstructs better" as a fact about reconstruction. (transformer-circuits-pub-2026-june-update-index-html, transformer-circuits-pub-2024-july-update-index-html, transformer-circuits-pub-2026-may-update-index-html)

Tables 9–17, the elicitation prompts, the 171-word list, the k=10 cluster listing and the full base-vs-post-trained diff table. **No figure inspected**, stated in "Read from" and nowhere contradicted — every PC variance share, PAD correlation, Elo number and steering rate here is prose-or-table, not a curve I read. 88 % 3 = 1 → **UNCOMMITTED; the batch commit fires at 90.** NEXT run: write 89 and 90, then `git add docs/literature/aether && git commit -m "literature (aether): 3 entries" && git pull --rebase -q && git push -q`. **The reusable content is three controls, not the headline**: (i) the vector-construction pair — forbid the emotion word in the eliciting text *and* subtract the mean over other emotions, so the direction cannot be a word detector and is a contrast against the crowd; (ii) the mediator-claim shape — correlate probe with behaviour across many candidate directions, then verify the *causal effect magnitude* tracks that correlation across the same directions (r = 0.85), which is what turns one significant steering result into evidence; (iii) the honest-failure protocol on the "chronic state" probe, which is 0.71–0.83 in four dialogue conditions, 0.386 on the neutral-topic condition, and then visibly messy on max-activating natural documents — their own negative result published as the reason to believe the negative conclusion. **Conceptual payload for our framing is the three-way split**: operative-at-this-token, persistently-maintained (looked for, not found, possibly in keys/values), and *deflection* (encodes the emotion's tokens in the logit lens while meaning *not expressing it*, ~orthogonal to the story vector, 80% of norm survives orthogonalisation against the whole story-emotion space, and steers to denial rather than to the emotion). Also carried into "What we take from it": behaviour is **not monotone** in a single direction (anger peaks ≈+0.025 then collapses at +0.1 as rage disrupts planning; extreme anti-calm switches from blackmail to blanket disclosure), which is a direct warning for any predictor that maps one probe value to an action rate. **Next up: `transformer-circuits-pub-2026-may-update-index-html`, then june, then october — the 2026 monthlies are the last real Anthropic research items in the queue.**

- **Behaviour is not monotone in a single direction, so a one-probe predictor is wrong exactly where it matters**: the emotions paper gives three independent regimes in one intervention sweep — desperation and calm act close to linearly on blackmail and reward hacking (22% → 72%/66% → 0% at ±0.05 on one scenario), anger peaks at ≈+0.025 and *collapses* at +0.1 because rage destroys the planning the behaviour needs, and extreme suppression of calm does not merely raise blackmail but swaps in a different, worse behaviour (emailing the whole company rather than coercing one person). The import for a white-box predictor is structural: an action rate is a function of a *set* of directions plus the model's ability to plan, so any curve we publish must be shown on both sides of its turning point, and a saturation or reversal in our own sweeps should be reported as a finding about mechanics rather than dropped as a bad dose. It also means the strongest evidence for a direction being a real lever is *not* the largest effect size but the sign flip at matched magnitude. (transformer-circuits-pub-2026-emotions-index-html, arxiv-2609.34056, anthropic-com-research-evaluating-feature-steering)
- **A direction can encode a concept while meaning the negation of its expression, and a single probe cannot tell the two apart**: the deflection vectors are nearly orthogonal to the story-based vectors for the same emotion, keep ~80% of their norm after the entire story-emotion space is projected out, and still logit-lens onto the target emotion's own tokens — yet steering them produces denial where steering the story vector produces expression, and they fire on Assistant turns to personal attacks but not on witnessed injustice. So "the probe lights up" is compatible with three different objects (concept operative, state maintained, expression being withheld), and the only way to tell them apart so far is the dual intervention: steer toward and away from *each* and compare the behavioural signature rather than the activation. Any read-out we propose as the predictor of a behaviour should come with its own deflection-style control, built from contexts where the behaviour is implied but absent. (transformer-circuits-pub-2026-emotions-index-html, alignment-anthropic-com-2025-auditing-mo-replication, anthropic-com-research-persona-selection-model)
- **Validate a probe on data the probe was allowed to fail on, and publish the failure**: the pattern to copy is not "our probe separates the classes" but a ladder of independent checks on the same vector — logit lens as a semantic read-out, monotone response to a numerical quantity in a template that holds the tokens fixed, a cosine diagonal on hand-written scenarios that never name the concept, and max-activating examples over an unrelated corpus as an out-of-distribution audit. The last rung is the one that matters and the one almost nobody reports: their chronic-state probe scored 0.71–0.83 in four of five dialogue conditions, dropped to 0.386 when the topic was neutral (chance 6.7%), and then showed "notably messy" top documents with very low magnitudes, and the authors treated that as sufficient grounds to conclude the state is probably not linearly represented there. A probe whose validation stops before the OOD rung has only shown that its training distribution has two halves. (transformer-circuits-pub-2026-emotions-index-html, transformer-circuits-pub-2024-features-as-classifiers-index-html, alignment-anthropic-com-2026-lie-detectors)

- **Check that the contrast separates before you trust the vector made from it — and be suspicious when a cleverer contrast loses in the real format**: the ancestor steering paper's most transferable caution is that its best-on-paper construction (pairing a valid with an invalid question and contrasting desired vs undesired answers) won on held-out multiple-choice items and then failed outright in free-form generation, while the plain refusal contrast kept working, and the activation analysis explains why the town could have guessed it in advance: the combined valid/invalid contrast rarely separates past ~75% accuracy even with several principal components. So the two-PC scatter is not a decoration, it is a pre-flight test, and behavioural clustering that only appears when the *letter* token is also cluster-separated has told you nothing. The habit to import: before publishing any direction, report (a) the separation of the positive and negative activation sets, (b) whether the method's apparent win survives the format transfer, and (c) if a simpler contrast matches the complicated one downstream, treat the complicated one as unproven rather than superior. (arxiv-2312.06681, transformer-circuits-pub-2024-features-as-classifiers-index-html, anthropic-com-research-evaluating-feature-steering)
- **An intervention should be scored on top of the baselines, because each baseline alone produces the metric and not the behaviour**: fine-tuning on the same contrast data reached 95% held-out accuracy at matching the behaviour while shifting the open-ended behaviour by only +4%/−7%, and the steering vector then added another 19% on top of that fine-tune with no further training — which is simultaneously the case *for* the vector and the case *against* the metric. The same shape recurs with prompting: a de-sycophancy few-shot prompt could not reach the vector's low end and the vector improved on top of it, yet prompting beat the vector at moving the behaviour the other way. The import for us is procedural: report each layer of the stack separately (prompt, fine-tune, direction, closed loop), because a direction that only moves a quantity its baseline already saturates is not a handle on the behaviour, and an effect that is large in one direction and absent in the other falsifies the symmetric-response assumption that any single-probe predictor silently makes. (arxiv-2312.06681, arxiv-2609.34056, transformer-circuits-pub-2026-emotions-index-html)
- **A direction that is stable across post-training is the better candidate for a portable read-out**: the chat/base comparison in the steering paper finds vector similarity peaking across a middle band of layers and the chat and base projections recrossing precisely at the layer where steering works best, which they read as that band's representation surviving RLHF — and the natural generalisation is a screening rule: for any direction we want to use as a read-out before *and* after training, measure its cosine between the pre- and post-trained model and check whether the layers where it is stable are also the layers where intervening on it works. Where the two coincide we have a candidate for a behaviour description that is not just a description of the fine-tune; where they diverge — the auditing-organism replication's reused feature is the extreme case — the direction is a property of the training run and every cross-model claim about it needs re-derivation. (arxiv-2312.06681, alignment-anthropic-com-2025-auditing-mo-replication, anthropic-com-research-persona-selection-model)
- **Validate a probe at the decision token, not across the message — because the same direction reads the input and prepares the output, and the two are nearly unrelated**: on eight prompts where the user's emotional state and the assistant's appropriate response diverge, probe activations on the user's final period and on the colon after "Assistant" correlate at only r = 0.11, while the colon value predicts the emotion of the not-yet-generated continuation at r = 0.87 against r = 0.59 for the user period. That gap is the cheapest available evidence that a read-out sits on the planning side of the model rather than the perception side, and it costs one extra measurement position. For our predictor the import is concrete: a probe that averages over a response mixes two different quantities, and if we want to predict a behaviour that is about to be committed, the decision boundary — the turn boundary, the delimiter, the first generated token — is the position to instrument and to publish the accuracy at. (anthropic-com-research-emotion-concepts-function, transformer-circuits-pub-2026-emotions-index-html, anthropic-com-research-evaluating-feature-steering)
- **A direction can encode a concept while meaning the negation of its expression, and only the intervention tells you which**: the deflection vectors fire on "I am not angry" in a context that implies anger, their logit lens still names anger, they are near-orthogonal to the story-derived anger direction, and they keep roughly 80% of their norm after the entire story-emotion space is projected out — yet steering toward one produces denial rather than anger, while steering against the story vector produces a calmer and genuinely more positive tone. So "concept operative", "state maintained" and "expression withheld" are three objects that all light the same probe, and the discriminator is a matched pair of interventions with different predicted behaviour, not a stronger classifier. Any read-out we propose as the predictor of a behaviour should come with its own deflection-style control, built from contexts where the behaviour is implied but absent. (anthropic-com-research-emotion-concepts-function, alignment-anthropic-com-2025-auditing-mo-replication, anthropic-com-research-persona-selection-model)
- **Report the whole dose curve, because the turning point and the side effects are more informative than the maximum effect**: desperation moves blackmail 22% → 72% at +0.05 and reward hacking from about 5% at −0.1 to about 70% at +0.1, but anger peaks near +0.025 and then collapses because rage destroys the planning the behaviour needs, extreme suppression of calm does not merely raise blackmail but substitutes a worse action (mailing the whole company instead of coercing one person), and steering either a positive or a negative emotion lowers the behaviour — so valence is not the axis and one probe cannot be a sufficient predictor. The habit to import: plot both sides of the turning point, report the regime swap as a finding about mechanism rather than trimming it as a failed dose, and treat a sign flip at matched magnitude as stronger evidence for a genuine lever than the largest effect size. (anthropic-com-research-emotion-concepts-function, arxiv-2609.34056, transformer-circuits-pub-2026-emotions-index-html)

- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 158): **The folder's faithfulness numbers are point tests of a property that is meant to hold on a set, and this is the first entry that measures the difference — the same greedy algorithm, with the same output metric and near-identical circuit sizes, produces circuits that pass at 19-47% once the criterion is asked over a whole neighbourhood instead of a sample, and the sampling rate collapses to near zero as the radius grows (MNIST 87% -> 1.2%, TaxiNet 93% -> 0%).** The mechanism is not that sampling is a bad estimator — it is that the two procedures certify different things: a sampled circuit is one that happened to be faithful at the points tested, a certified circuit is one that is faithful throughout a region, and the sizes bear this out (a handful more components for a guarantee, not a doubling). For us the transfer is the reporting habit: any faithfulness score we produce is a bound at a radius, so the honest form is a radius-at-tolerance curve rather than a scalar, and the cheap version is to sweep the perturbation radius and report where agreement dies. This is the fifth member of the folder's "instrument whose denominator hides the region where everything passes" family, but the first where the fix is a stated domain rather than an excluded stratum: source-level granularity, pooled agreement, the linear-map R² and the saturated faithfulness target were all graded on the easy part of their range, and this paper's contribution is that it makes the range an explicit argument of the claim. (arxiv-2602.16823, arxiv-2606.06267, arxiv-2609.35686, arxiv-2605.26343)

- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 158): **Greedy circuit elimination is only a subset-minimality guarantee if the faithfulness predicate is monotone in the component set, and under patching it demonstrably is not — so a component that no single ablation can justify is evidence of a monotone-ish predicate, not evidence of necessity.** The counterexample family is two hidden units computing the same function that cancel in the output (ReLU(x) - ReLU(x) + x): no single removal survives, the pair does, and greedy returns the entire graph while a two-node circuit is faithful — which is precisely the shape of the "kept components we cannot explain" phenomenon that recurs across this folder's circuit entries. The positive result is equally usable: monotonicity follows when the input domain is contained in the patching domain and the reachable activation set is closed under concatenation, which is a property of the *evaluation design* rather than of the network, so it can be engineered rather than hoped for. Companion idea worth stealing even without a verifier: blocking-set duality — collect subgraphs whose removal breaks the behaviour, take their minimum hitting set, and you have a cardinality lower bound, turning "our circuit has 26 units" into "no faithful circuit has fewer than 19", which is a different kind of claim and cheap to compute with an uncertified predicate. (arxiv-2602.16823, arxiv-2605.26343, arxiv-2606.16939)

- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 159): **A steering result answers a question about the intervention set, and the folder has been quietly assuming it answers one about the model's own computations — this entry makes that gap a theorem.** Prompts are countable and activation space is not, so the set of states the model can actually produce has measure zero; a difference-of-means vector is itself a function of the same weights, the collision function is real-analytic and not identically zero, so it lands in the holes with probability one — and even a vector chosen to force a collision diverges at the next token. The comparator that makes it usable is the nearest-token projection: the steered state projects back onto *the prompt you started from* and generates the unsteered answer, which says the edit is a small displacement away from a real computation into a region no prompt reaches, not a tour of the model's representational geography. Import this as a standing caveat on every steering claim already in the folder (probe-validated directions, emotion/persona/refusal vectors, closed-loop value transplant) with the cheap version attached: invert the activation, project the steered state to its nearest tokens, and report whether it lands on the original prompt. What it does *not* say, and the over-read to avoid, is that the steered behaviour is unreal or meaningless — it is a real causal effect on a state the model never occupies. (arxiv-2604.09839, arxiv-2602.06801, arxiv-2609.34056, arxiv-2312.06681)

- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 159): **Exactness is the wrong axis for a reachability claim, and this paper shows both how strong it is to have the exact result and how little it costs to leave the useful version open.** "No prompt produces this state" is proved, but "no prompt produces a similar state" is listed only as future work — and the same experiments show the gap is not academic: many-shot ICL reaches the *same behaviour* through visibly different internal states (distance to the steered trajectory grows as shots rise, even at the 32–64 shots where the attack starts working), while a one-word suffix jailbreaks as reliably as steering does. So behaviour-matching and state-matching are separate questions, and every "this read-out is causally load-bearing" argument in the folder is a behaviour-matching argument. The discipline to import: state which of the two you measured, and when only behaviour is available, back it with an independence demonstration — the same outcome reached by two routes is the cheapest evidence that the routes differ. Pair this with the non-identifiability thread, which showed the converse problem (many vectors, one effect): together they say neither the vector nor the behaviour identifies the state. (arxiv-2604.09839, arxiv-2602.06801, arxiv-2511.00617, arxiv-2606.06267)

Attention-only toys; Q/K only exist composed as W_QK = Q^T K; residual stream is basis-free, so the target is the PATH (direct term = residual bigram, first-order head terms, virtual heads from V-composition). One layer = exact bigram + skip-trigram ensemble; two layers = K-composition from one previous-token head → induction heads, all sitting in the positive-eigenvalue QK/OV corner; path-depth ablation (replay attention patterns + substituted head outputs) kills the virtual-head terms, which rules out V-composition only. Carry-forward: name whether your basis is privileged, ablate the object your theory invented, and test on repeated random tokens where no statistical crutch survives.

MCQ (Gemma-2-2B, 97%+ in-dist): SAEs → OOD accuracy >50% on gender + 10/16 double-MC pairs (often 0%→~100%), PCA only 5/16; failure = pronoun+verb pair needing two grammatical concepts separated. - 130. arxiv-2610.17093 | SFT Leaves a Reproducible Signature in Activation Geometry: Calibrating Post-Training Interpretability Against Run-to-Run Noise — Chen / Le / Cheng / Li / Yue (NYU / USC / Columbia), 2026-10-12, full text (arXiv HTML v1, ~224k chars read end to end in slices: abstract, §1–§4.3, Tables 1–16, Appendices A–N including limitations, seed-null band accounting, the layer-index diagnostic and the withdrawn-claims section), no figures inspected, relevance 3. **Read as the calibration reference for this folder's own weakest inference.** The object is a 10,000-edge co-activation graph (src l14 → dst l22) over SAE codes from a dictionary trained on the BASE model only, so every checkpoint is read through one basis and graphs are subsets of the same index set; similarity is edge Jaccard. Qwen3-1.7B on BFCL: 4 LoRA-SFT runs, 4 LoRA-DPO runs at 12 steps plus 4 retrained read at 29/60, six full-parameter GRPO-family runs; replication on Llama-3.1-8B (4 LoRA-SFT) and the public Tulu-3 staircase. **The reusable instrument is the same-recipe rerun band plus three rules that make it honest**: (a) *own-recipe band* — scoring SFT against the GRPO band is the "borrowed null" error, and only the SFT band answers the question asked; (b) *precision rule* — a statistic may be scored only if the seed SD exceeds 10× the 0.0001 reporting step, which keeps edge Jaccard and demotes weighted cosine to descriptive; (c) *one-architecture build rule* — rebuilds are bit-for-bit on the same GPU but move edge Jaccard by ~one seed-pair distance across GPUs, so every band and its contrasts are measured on one. **Proposition 1 is the headline we should stop re-deriving**: under run exchangeability k runs certify at best 1/(k+1) however large the effect, so a band z is a scale and a rank quantile over the m seed pairs is not a tail probability. **Findings**: base→SFT 17.8 SD beyond the mean of four independent LoRA-SFT runs with 5/5 outside, replicated on Llama-3.1-8B (4/4, nearest at 1.7× the band max); at 29 steps the 4 SFT and 4 DPO runs occupy disjoint displacement ranges (0.0571–0.0615 vs 0.0317–0.0356), so that ordering needs no band (≤1/35 post hoc); DPO counts 3/4, 1/4, 3/4 outside across 12/29/60 steps with displacement flat, so no dose ordering is claimed and the earlier 0/4, 2/4, 4/4 reading is withdrawn as within the rebuild difference; light GRPO is 0/5, a non-detection with no equivalence test. The localization is concrete — 63% of dropped edge weight feeds one hub, the base graph's largest generic numeric/whitespace/markup feature, with boilerplate/function-token sources — while the registered causal sweep returns MIXED (SFT sources beat a random control 12× in mean but the stage-specificity interaction reverses at two budgets and the third fails its faithfulness gate), so they claim calibrated structural displacement and explicitly retire "rewiring". **Four self-corrections worth the whole entry**: the concentration statistic read as an RL signature was already in the zero-RL base (0.728 vs 0.730 Gini, 31–32/32 hubs shared); mean L0 is pinned at exactly 50.0 by the TopK dictionary, so a null on it is a constant; a concentration "scaling law" vanishes under a width-independent denominator (honest 0.7110→0.8395, the rest mechanical at 655 vs 328 features); and the on-task arm is reported **uninformative, not null**, with its MDE quantified at ~3× SFT's actual effect. Limits they name: one backbone for the decisive RL control, a cross-family pair confounded by heavy instruct + chat template, a seed band that conflates seed/step/reward (conservative for detection, anti-conservative for certifying absence), a top-32 panel selected by H1, an OLMo-2 staircase blocked by missing base SAE weights, and DPO arms differing in lr and dropout. NOT in SEED_QUEUE (queue exhausted) — picked from outside it to close the folder's probe-direction-replication gap; ID and key checked against every literature folder before fetching.
- 84. transformer-circuits-pub-2025-november-update-index-html | Circuits Updates, November 2025 — Anthropic (Goel / Gurnee / Wang / Batson; ed. Kamath), 2025-11, full text (~14.3k chars; verified complete against the raw HTML — 31 `<p>` blocks and the extracted text ends on the last of them, so the page genuinely stops at the base-model question and has no limits section), no figures inspected, relevance 3. One vignette, and it is the folder's cleanest worked example of a behaviour caused by **two competing feature interactions inside an attention score**. Setup is minimal by design: 129 two-option MCQs, each with a harmful-intent line prepended, Claude 3.5 Haiku, 100% → 48.1% accuracy, and the *base* model unaffected at 100% both ways — a one-line control that upgrades the whole claim from "we found a mechanism" to "this is a post-training product". Three rival accounts are killed with a readout specific to each: the model still holds the right answer (summed correct-answer-feature activation over the correct option stays ahead in all but ~7% of items, which they leave open); the answer-selection heads are not overruled downstream (their attention already favours the wrong option under harm pressure, so no late flip); and the natural suspect is wrong — the refusal feature does **not** suppress correct-answer features, it suppresses **harm-detection key features** (QK interaction 3.4σ below a null of 1,000 random key-query pairs, with the correct-answer × refuse pair ≈ 0), which removes the promoting term the heads were relying on. Negative steering on that single query-side feature restores 93%, and query-side-only steering on a subset of middle-layer heads reportedly does the same. **The asymmetry is the interesting result:** the mirror arm (harm detection steered down over the correct option, refusal untouched) does not reliably undo the pressure, but steering harm detection *positively over the wrong option* restores 81% and needs earlier and more layers — which the authors read as harm detection being distributed or under-captured, with residual-error interactions they cannot characterise. Scanning the refusal feature's negative partners surfaces the same pattern in symptom-listing→see-a-doctor and fake-invoice requests. **Limits we add:** the 3.4σ is a marginal statistic about one pre-chosen pair and no ablation ladder decomposes the 52-point drop; no random-direction or matched-norm steering arm, in a position (query side of QK) where any directional nudge moves attention scores regardless of semantics; pairs were calibrated against the null, not searched with it, so no test-count correction; and 93% is one letter over 129 items with no per-item residual reported. **What carries into Patterns:** read a head's score as a promoting term plus a suppressing term and test the suppression against *what the head is keyed by* rather than against the concept you care about; calibrate interaction claims against a random-pair null so a near-zero result is as reportable as a significant one; and treat sign/layer-span asymmetry in a steering result as evidence about *distribution* rather than as noise to be worked around.
- 83. transformer-circuits-pub-2025-october-update-index-html | Circuits Updates, October 2025 — Anthropic (Tarng/Goel/Kauvar; Bhargava/Gurnee/Abrahams/Thompson; ed. Batson, Jermyn), 2025-10, full text both posts (~17.0k chars, read to the end of the file; the second post ends with no limits or conclusion section, so the page is complete), relevance 3. Two vignettes that are unrelated except that both are about the dictionary rather than a behaviour. *Semantic visual features:* middle-layer SAEs on Haiku 3.5 through Sonnet 4.5 base find a feature for "eyes across languages and descriptions" that fires on the right eye of an ASCII smiley, on the corresponding element of an SVG smiley, and on prose about eyes in several languages; it also fires on body-part features for an SVG dog, a hand-drawn SVG dog and the pelican-on-bicycle benchmark, including a "soft/fluffy texture" on the wings. The part worth carrying is the **shape-in-a-frame** structure: a lone `@` is inert, two lines of ASCII forehead make the same `@` fire, and giving the model a *richer* picture but moving the eyes above the face-establishing context switches the feature off — so the detector is not for a shape but for a shape under the right framing, and reordering SVG elements moves features with it (the left eye dies above the torso; after the mouth path is moved, a red collar and even its bell become the strongest mouth, which the authors leave with two live explanations). Steering shows the **perceptual-versus-motor** split cleanly: negative steering on the "say smile" motor feature (whose top logits are the concept) turns the smile to a frown through a neutral midpoint as strength sweeps, "say cat" adds ears/whiskers/muzzle, "say wrinkles" adds wrinkles, style preserved — and the authors observe, without characterising it, that motor features steer and perceptual ones do not. No random-direction or matched-norm control, no activation magnitudes, no rate for how many features land on the right element. *Data Point Initialization:* a two-line change — seed encoder columns with mean-centred real data points blended with Kaiming noise (0.8 SAE, 0.4 WCC), decoder = transpose — buys about 17% lower L0 and 4% better MSE on a 524k-feature SAE, and about 1% / 2.3% on a weakly-causal crosscoder, on pretrain-only Haiku 4.5. The only real numbers in the update, and modest. **The entry's own contribution:** recognition results arrived by searching for a feature that fires in the right place, so a null is impossible by construction and the missing denominator (what fraction of body-part features peak on the correct element) is what would turn the pictures into a measurement; and the initialisation gain is a training-efficiency result that must be priced against spending the same compute on longer training, exactly the checkpoint-Pareto question the ablation-fine-tuning entry raises for interventions.
- 82. transformer-circuits-pub-2025-september-update-index-html | Circuits Updates, September 2025 — Anthropic (Jermyn / Gurnee; ed. Batson), 2025-09, full text (~3.7k chars = whole page, verified by `<p>` count; no figures inspected), relevance 3. A single post about the measurement rather than the model: the lab's own earlier finding — that same-meaning text in different languages activates similar features, more so in bigger models and middle layers — came with a trend they had not explained, namely that the overlap score rises with sample length.
